records.name: HajnalSzemeredi.hajnal_szemeredi_of_maxDegree_lt
records.entry_name: The Hajnal–Szemerédi theorem on equitable colourings
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Hajnal–Szemerédi theorem (1970), conjectured by Erdős in 1964: every finite graph with maximum degree at most r has an equitable proper colouring with r + 1 colours, i.e. a proper colouring whose colour classes differ in size by at most one. The exact form is also proved: if the number of vertices is s(r + 1), every colour class has exactly s vertices (the colouring form of Erdős Problem #914). Version 2 adds the form with any number k > Δ(G) of colours (Mathlib's SimpleGraph.maxDegree), deduced from the theorem with r = k − 1. The proof follows the short argument of Kierstead and Kostochka (2008): induction on the number of edges; after deleting an edge, a nearly equitable colouring is repaired by moving vertices along paths of an auxiliary digraph on the colour classes (Lemma 2.1); when the large class is inaccessible, a family of terminal classes, solo edges and a discharging count with weights q/|S_z| (Lemmas 2.2–2.3) produce a recolouring that either finishes the colouring or strictly increases the number of accessible classes, using the induction hypothesis on the inaccessible part. The general case is reduced to the divisible one by adding a disjoint complete graph.

records.name: Vizing.lineGraph_colorable
records.entry_name: Vizing's theorem and equitable edge colourings
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Vizing's theorem: every finite simple graph G has a proper edge colouring with Δ(G) + 1 colours, stated with Mathlib's line graph (G.lineGraph is (Δ(G) + 1)-colourable, hence χ'(G) ≤ Δ(G) + 1), proved with fans and Kempe chain exchanges. It also proves the equitable refinement: for every c ≥ Δ(G) + 1 there is a proper edge colouring with colours Fin c in which any two colour classes (including unused colours) differ in size by at most one (McDiarmid 1972), obtained by balancing a Vizing colouring with alternating-component moves that strictly decrease a square energy. Version 2 adds the lower bound Δ(G) ≤ χ'(G) (the edges at a vertex of maximum degree form a clique of the line graph) and hence the dichotomy χ'(G) ∈ {Δ(G), Δ(G) + 1} (class 1 / class 2).

records.name: PlanarChoosability.isPlanar_iff_minorFree
records.entry_name: Wagner's planarity criterion and list colouring of planar and K5-minor-free graphs
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of classical results on planar graphs and graphs without a K5 minor. (1) Wagner's theorem (1937): a finite graph is planar if and only if it has neither K5 nor K3,3 as a minor. (2) Škrekovski's theorem (1998): every finite graph without a K5 minor is 5-choosable, proved along the route of Wood and Linusson, and Thomassen's theorem (1994) that every finite planar graph is 5-choosable, as a corollary. (3) DP-colouring: every finite graph without a K5 minor (Li–Wang, 2022), hence every finite planar graph (Dvořák–Postle, 2018), is DP-5-colourable. (4) Voigt's theorem (1993): an explicit planar graph on 238 vertices with lists of four colours has no proper list colouring, so 5 cannot be lowered to 4; its planarity and non-colourability are checked by kernel reduction. (5) Wagner's equivalence of the Four Colour Theorem with Hadwiger's conjecture for K5 (neither side is proved). (6) Wagner's structure theorem (1937, added in version 2): a finite graph has no K5 minor if and only if it is a spanning subgraph of a graph obtained by clique-sums of order at most three, keeping the clique edges, from planar graphs and copies of the Wagner graph V8. Planarity is defined combinatorially, by rotation systems of genus zero (Euler defect 0); as sanity checks K4 is planar and K5, K3,3 are not.

records.name: AsymptoticTrianglePacking.near_regular_nibble
records.entry_name: Near-regular hypergraph matchings and the asymptotic triangle-packing gap
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of four results. (1) A finite nibble theorem: r-uniform hypergraphs whose degrees are at most (1+μ)d everywhere and at least (1−μ)d outside an exceptional set of at most η|V| vertices, with codegrees at most μd, have matchings with at least (1−β)|V|/r edges. (2) The fractional–integral triangle-packing gap is o(n²) uniformly over finite graphs: every large graph has an edge-disjoint triangle family P such that every fractional triangle packing has weight at most |P| + εn² (the triangle case of Haxell–Rödl). (3) The cover form: a fractional triangle cover of weight at most |P| + εn² exists. (4) Version 2, the transfer form used in decomposition theory: every large graph on n vertices that has a fractional triangle decomposition has an edge-disjoint triangle family covering all but at most ηn² edges; it follows from (2), since a fractional decomposition is a fractional packing of weight e(G)/3 and a packing P covers exactly 3|P| edges. The proof of (1)–(3) combines a nibble with second-moment and Freedman-type concentration, a low-degree core reduction, Mathlib's Szemerédi regularity lemma with a cluster linear program rounded by explicit designs, and LP duality.

records.name: HadwigerMader.mader
records.entry_name: Mader's theorem and Hadwiger's conjecture for t ≤ 4
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Mader's theorem (a nonempty finite graph of average degree at least 2^(r−2) has a K_r minor), of Dirac's lemma (a graph without a K4 minor has a vertex of degree at most two, hence at most 2n − 3 edges for n ≥ 2), of Mader's bound for K5 (a graph on n ≥ 3 vertices with at least 3n − 5 edges has a K5 minor; equivalently, without a K5 minor it has at most 3n − 6 edges; added in version 2), and of Hadwiger's conjecture for t ≤ 4 (graphs without a K3 minor are 2-colourable, graphs without a K4 minor are 3-colourable). Minors are branch-set models.

records.name: HadwigerMader.exists_degree_le_two
records.entry_name: Mader's theorem and Hadwiger's conjecture for t ≤ 4
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Mader's theorem (a nonempty finite graph of average degree at least 2^(r−2) has a K_r minor), of Dirac's lemma (a graph without a K4 minor has a vertex of degree at most two, hence at most 2n − 3 edges for n ≥ 2), of Mader's bound for K5 (a graph on n ≥ 3 vertices with at least 3n − 5 edges has a K5 minor; equivalently, without a K5 minor it has at most 3n − 6 edges; added in version 2), and of Hadwiger's conjecture for t ≤ 4 (graphs without a K3 minor are 2-colourable, graphs without a K4 minor are 3-colourable). Minors are branch-set models.

records.name: FixedOrderFactor.muAvg_eq
records.entry_name: FixedOrderFactor: the order-r correction factor for mean squares of L(1, chi), and the factor 35/34
records.doc: For an integer r >= 2 and a finite set N of primes, the random Euler product model for Dirichlet characters of order r replaces chi(q) by independent uniform r-th roots of unity. The development proves that the order-r local factor E|1 - z/q|^(-2) equals (1 + q^-r)/((1 - q^-2)(1 - q^-r)), that its ratio to the full-circle factor (1 - q^-2)^(-1), multiplied over the primes outside N, is zeta^(N)(r)^2 / zeta^(N)(2r), that this correction factor is also the sum of (ab)^-r over the coprime pairs of integers prime to N, and that the model mean is zeta^(N)(2) zeta^(N)(r)^2 / zeta^(N)(2r). The factor exceeds 1, decreases strictly in r and tends to 1; for r = 2k and N empty it equals -binom(4k,2k) B_{2k}^2/(2 B_{4k}). For r = 4 and N = {2} it is 35/34, the ratio by which the limit of Louboutin's mean square of L(1, chi) with the factor at 2 removed changes when the average is restricted to quartic characters; with the forced factor 4/5 at 2 the development also proves the constants pi^2/10, 7 pi^2/68, 7 pi^2/36 and 7/136 = (1/20)(35/34) = (7/72)(9/17). It also identifies the pairs the model keeps: for positive m, n the average of z^m conj(z^n) is 1 exactly when m/n is an r-th power in Q, that is when (m, n) = (d a^r, d b^r) with a, b coprime, and 0 otherwise. Modulo a single prime p with r | p - 1 it proves the finite-character counterpart: there are exactly r Dirichlet characters mod p with chi^r = 1, the sum of chi(a) conj(chi(b)) over them is r when a/b is a nonzero r-th power mod p and 0 otherwise, so every pair (d a^r, d b^r) prime to p survives with sum r; by contrast, summed over all characters mod p, chi(m) conj(chi(n)) has sum 0 for distinct m, n < p. Release v1.2 adds the finite part of the Chebyshev bias in families p = a (mod M) of fixed order r: with rho_s(t) the average of exp(2 pi i u t/s) over the units u mod s, the sum over t < s of rho_s(c t) is s when s | c and 0 otherwise; for M > 0 and s | M the squares in Z/s x| (Z/M)^x give the prime-square term of the explicit formula as s times the square-root count beta(M, a, s) = #{y in (Z/M)^x : y^2 = a, y = -1 (mod s)}, a count of residue classes (the same finite-sum identity over the representatives 0 <= x < M holds for all M and s > 0, but is only an arithmetic identity there: vacuous at M = 0, representative-dependent when s does not divide M); beta does not decrease as s decreases along divisibility, at s = r it is 0 unless a is a square in H = ker((Z/M)^x -> (Z/r)^x) and is then the number of square roots of 1 in H; and for the imaginary families (r even, M = 2r, a = 1 + r) beta vanishes for every s unless 8 | r, and for s = r/d with d odd in every case.

The factor exceeds 1, decreases strictly in r and tends to 1; for r = 2k and N empty it equals -binom(4k,2k) B_{2k}^2/(2 B_{4k}). For r = 4 and N = {2} it is 35/34, the ratio by which the limit of Louboutin's mean square of L(1, chi) with the factor at 2 removed changes when the average is restricted to quartic characters; with the forced factor 4/5 at 2 the development also proves the constants pi^2/10, 7 pi^2/68, 7 pi^2/36 and 7/136 = (1/20)(35/34) = (7/72)(9/17). It also identifies the pairs the model keeps: for positive m, n the average of z^m conj(z^n) is 1 exactly when m/n is an r-th power in Q, that is when (m, n) = (d a^r, d b^r) with a, b coprime, and 0 otherwise. Modulo a single prime p with r | p - 1 it proves the finite-character counterpart: there are exactly r Dirichlet characters mod p with chi^r = 1, the sum of chi(a) conj(chi(b)) over them is r when a/b is a nonzero r-th power mod p and 0 otherwise, so every pair (d a^r, d b^r) prime to p survives with sum r; by contrast, summed over all characters mod p, chi(m) conj(chi(n)) has sum 0 for distinct m, n < p. Release v1.2 adds the finite part of the Chebyshev bias in families p = a (mod M) of fixed order r: with rho_s(t) the average of exp(2 pi i u t/s) over the units u mod s, the sum over t < s of rho_s(c t) is s when s | c and 0 otherwise; for M > 0 and s | M the squares in Z/s x| (Z/M)^x give the prime-square term of the explicit formula as s times the square-root count beta(M, a, s) = #{y in (Z/M)^x : y^2 = a, y = -1 (mod s)}, a count of residue classes (the same finite-sum identity over the representatives 0 <= x < M holds for all M and s > 0, but is only an arithmetic identity there: vacuous at M = 0, representative-dependent when s does not divide M); beta does not decrease as s decreases along divisibility, at s = r it is 0 unless a is a square in H = ker((Z/M)^x -> (Z/r)^x) and is then the number of square roots of 1 in H; and for the imaginary families (r even, M = 2r, a = 1 + r) beta vanishes for every s unless 8 | r, and for s = r/d with d odd in every case.

records.name: GroupDimension.Palomar.D_five_eq_gamma_five_of_exp_three
records.entry_name: Fifth dimension subgroups: D₅ = γ₅ when G/γ₂ is finite of exponent 3, candidates for a counterexample, and a reduction of Kourovka 20.84
records.doc: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization accompanying S. Vorobev, "On the inclusion D_5(G) ⊆ γ_4(G): reductions, the Lie-ring proof, and evidence" (preprint, 2026; submitted to arXiv math.GR on 2026-10-22). The integral dimension subgroups D_n(G) = {g ∈ G : g − 1 ∈ Δ(G)^n} are defined from the augmentation ideal of Mathlib's integral group ring. Kourovka Problem 20.84 asks whether D_5(G) ⊆ γ_4(G) for every group; it is open and is not claimed here. Unconditional results: D_5(G) = γ_5(G) whenever G/γ_2(G) is finite of exponent 3, and more generally whenever G/γ_2(G) is a finite 3-group whose cubes form a cyclic group, and still more generally whenever G/γ_2(G) is a finite 3-group and γ_2(G)/γ_3(G) has exponent at most 3, and still more generally whenever G/γ_2(G) is a finite 3-group, γ_4(G)^3 ⊆ γ_5(G) and γ_2(G)^9 ⊆ γ_4(G), and most generally whenever G/γ_2(G) is a finite 3-group and γ_4(G)^3 ⊆ γ_5(G) (paper, Theorems 6.6, 6.8, 6.9, 6.10 and 6.11), and whenever G/γ_2(G) is a finite p-group, p odd, and [γ_2(G), γ_2(G)] ⊆ γ_5(G), in particular for finite metabelian 3-groups, which is Gupta–Tahara's theorem at p = 3 (paper, Theorem D.1; the inclusion part of Tahara's 1981 description of D_5 is formalized for this); D_5(G) lies in the Jennings product M_5(G) for finite 2-groups of class at most 3; and, for "candidates" (the paper's minimal-counterexample shape among finite 2-groups of class 3), there is no candidate of order 2^11 with Q/P_3 ≅ Z/4 × (Z/2)^7 and none of order 2^11 and rank at least 8 (paper, Lemma 5.6 and Proposition 5.7); the reduction of Problem 20.84 to finite 2-groups of class exactly 3 (Proposition 2.1); and a minimal counterexample is a candidate (Lemma 5.2). The proofs of the last two use D_3 = γ_3, Passi's D_4^2 ⊆ γ_4 and Gruenberg's residual theorem, all proved in the development (dThreeEqGammaThree, passiDFourSquare, gruenbergResidualTwo). One conditional result, with the assumption an explicit hypothesis: D_5 = 1 for groups of order 2^11, class at most 3 and rank at least 8, assuming the paper's computer result for order 2^10 (Proposition 5.7, D_5 form, assuming Proposition 5.3).

records.name: TemporalCliqueSpanners.exists_isTemporalSpanner_card_le_seven_mul
records.entry_name: Temporal cliques admit linear spanners
records.doc: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the theorem that every temporal clique on n vertices admits a temporal spanner with at most 7n edges. A temporal clique is the complete graph on a finite vertex set whose edges carry natural-number time labels, locally injective (two edges sharing an endpoint have distinct labels); a temporal spanner is a set of edges in which every vertex reaches every other one by a journey with non-decreasing labels. The result and its proof are due to Júlia Baligács (arXiv:2606.05156, 2026): the dismountability of Carnevale, Casteigts and Corsini (SAND 2025) reduces cliques to extremally matched bi-cliques, which are then covered by simple and extended stars. The compared statements give the explicit bound 7n and the asymptotic O(n) form with a bound function chosen uniformly for all cliques. They use the same definitions as the registered O(n log n) entry of the same repository. The work is supervised by Arnaud Casteigts and Karine Altisen.

records.name: LeanLab.BS2022GRH.Cert1575.chenThreshold13375_of_deep_closed
records.entry_name: An explicit version of Chen's theorem assuming the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof, conditional on the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis and on four cited results, that every even integer N at least e^{e^{13.375}} is the sum of a prime and a square-free number greater than 1 with at most two prime factors. The four cited inputs are explicit hypotheses of the theorem, never axioms: Thm5J, Thm6J and Thm7J, the Lean Lab's transcriptions of Theorems 5, 6 and 7 of M. Bordignon and V. Starichkova, An explicit version of Chen's theorem assuming the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, Ramanujan J. 64, 2024, 1213 to 1242; and LinearSieveT4 1/8349 112 114, the transcription of their Theorem 4, the explicit linear sieve of Bordignon, Johnston and Starichkova with the Table 1 row epsilon inverse 6100, C1 = 112, C2 = 114. In version 2 each of Thm5J, Thm6J and Thm7J also takes 0 <= C1 and 0 <= C2 as premises right after the sieve hypothesis, matching Table 1, which lists positive constants only. These transcriptions use the Lean normalisation U_N = 2 e^{-gamma} C2 Pi_N, twice the U_N printed in the journal; see the fidelity section. GRH for Dirichlet L-functions is the premise inside the conclusion ChenThreshold13375. The journal's own Corollary 1 has the threshold e^{e^{14}}; the threshold e^{e^{13.375}} comes from re-choosing the Section 5.4 parameters inside the authors' method, alpha = 0.00256, A = 10, u = 1500, epsilon = 1/8349, epsilon1 = 10^-20. The numeric inputs are proved here: epsilon at 1500 is below 1/8349 by a kernel certificate, decide +kernel in eleven window modules, and the Section 5.4 bracket combination is at least the main-term constant minus 10^-5, a one-sided lower bound. Chen's weighted inequality, the journal's Lemma 9, is proved unconditionally. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. An AI agent, Claude, wrote all the Lean code; the statements were checked against the paper by AI agents and are offered for human audit.

records.name: Rhone.Palomar.KingmanTrees.card_ranked_labelled_history
records.entry_name: Combinatorics and probabilities of Kingman coalescent trees: histories, shapes, topologies, root splits, Colless, and Sackin
records.doc: This entry formalizes combinatorics and probabilities of trees under Kingman's coalescent, through its embedded jump chain, in which each pair of the k current lineages is the next to merge with probability 1/binomial(k, 2). A ranked labelled history on n leaves is a sequence of n − 1 merges starting from n singletons; there are n!(n − 1)!/2^(n−1) of them, and each has probability 2^(n−1)/(n!(n − 1)!). Ranked and unranked tree shapes are defined as classes of histories under relabelling of the leaves; their numbers satisfy André's recurrence for alternating permutations, shifted by one, and the Wedderburn–Etherington recurrence, respectively, with the cases n = 1 and n = 2. The probability of a labelled rooted binary topology T is 2^(n−1)/(n! ∏(|C| − 1)), the product running over the clades C of T with at least two leaves. The probability that the root splits the leaves into a given set A and its complement is 2/((n − 1) binomial(n, |A|)). The probability that a sample S of a population of N leaves has the population root as its most recent common ancestor is (|S| − 1)(N + 1)/((|S| + 1)(N − 1)), which tends to (n − 1)/(n + 1) for a sample of fixed size n as N tends to infinity. The expected Colless and Sackin indices are n H_{⌊n/2⌋} − 2⌊n/2⌋ and 2n(H_n − 1), where H_m is the m-th harmonic number. Finally, the process of roots of the forest histories is identified with the jump chain of Kingman's partition-valued coalescent, for one step and for t steps.

records.name: Rhone.Palomar.LinkedPairPanel.panel_eq_iff
records.entry_name: Linked-pair panels: panel laws are determined by finitely many Laplace values
records.doc: This entry formalizes panels of linked site pairs observed through a reporting channel, with the pair coalescence time T following a probability law on the non-negative reals. All L sites of a panel share the same time T; given T = t, the sites are reported independently, and at each site the two lineages share one latent type with weight e^(−kt) and have independent types otherwise, each type being reported through a channel that maps K latent types to probability distributions on a finite set of labels. For an informative channel (one whose rows are not all equal) and a panel of length L, the panel laws of two time laws agree for all outcomes if and only if their Laplace transforms agree at the points rk for r = 0, …, L. If the channel erases all information, every panel law agrees. If the transforms agree up to L and differ at the next point, then panels of length L agree but some panel of length L + 1 differs. For k > 0, agreement of all panels of all lengths is equivalent to equality of the time laws.

records.name: Rhone.Palomar.NeutralFixation.fixation_real_of_nonDegenerate
records.entry_name: Neutral fixation probability in exchangeable (Cannings) models
records.doc: This entry formalizes the neutral fixation probability in exchangeable (Cannings) models with N individuals. For a non-degenerate model, the probability that the allele count started from i copies ever reaches N equals i/N, and the same holds for eventual absorption in the fixed state. The loss probability is 1 − i/N. For a degenerate model started away from the full state the probability of fixation is 0, and an example with N = 2 shows that the fixation probability can differ from the frequency without a reachability hypothesis. For N ≥ 2, non-degeneracy is shown equivalent to positive-probability reachability of the boundary {0, N} by the count chain, and to each of three conditions on the offspring number of a single parent. A general fixation statement is given for chains on {0, ..., N} whose state is mean-preserving in one step and from which the boundary {0, N} is reachable. The Moran model is shown to be non-degenerate with fixation probability i/N.

records.name: ShannonTheorem.shannon
records.entry_name: Shannon's theorem on edge colourings of multigraphs
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Shannon's theorem (1949): every finite loopless multigraph of maximum degree at most Δ has a proper edge colouring with ⌊3Δ/2⌋ colours; and its sharpness: for every Δ the Shannon triangle (three vertices with ⌊Δ/2⌋, ⌊Δ/2⌋ and ⌈Δ/2⌉ parallel edges between the three pairs) has maximum degree at most Δ and no proper edge colouring with fewer than ⌊3Δ/2⌋ colours. Multigraphs are edge families ends : ι → V × V (parallel edges allowed), a lighter representation than Mathlib's multigraph structure Graph α β (Mathlib.Combinatorics.Graph.Basic: vertex and edge sets with an incidence relation IsLink), which at the pinned revision has no degrees or edge colourings; no bridge to Graph α β is proved. Neither result is in Mathlib.

records.name: Rhone.Palomar.NoEwensFormula.boundedDen_eval
records.entry_name: No formula with denominators of bounded degree, in the total mutation parameter or in rho, for the two-locus sampling recursion
records.doc: This entry formalizes results on the degree of denominators of any closed-form expression for the solution of the two-locus sampling recursion of the coalescent with recombination, with two alleles at each locus and parent-independent mutation. The mutation rates, the recombination rate rho, and the allele frequencies are independent indeterminates, and the recursion is solved over a field of rational functions in them. An expression is built from rational constants, arbitrary coefficients from the coefficient field, the rates, sums, products, and quotients; it is admissible at degree D when every divisor evaluates to a nonzero polynomial of degree at most D in a designated variable (rho, or the total mutation rate theta_A + theta_B). A closure lemma shows that admissible expressions in inputs with bounded denominators have bounded denominators. For the sample of two lineages that carry the same haplotype at both loci, no admissible expression of degree one in rho, and none of degree two in the total mutation rate, equals the value of the solution; variants bound the total degree of the divisors in the three rates instead. For the samples of m lineages typed at locus A only and m typed at locus B only, all of allele 0, for every bound D there is an m ≥ 2 at which no admissible expression of degree D, in the total mutation rate or in rho, equals the value of the solution. Existence and uniqueness of the solutions are also stated in these settings.

records.entry_name: Weak mixing times minimality: transitivity of the product
records.doc: A continuous weakly mixing self-map of a nonempty compact Hausdorff space has a transitive actual heterogeneous product with any continuous pointwise forward-minimal self-map of a nonempty compact space. Surjectivity, arbitrarily late thick hitting blocks, syndetic hitting gaps and their intersection are proved.

records.name: Rhone.Palomar.PartitionPair.esf_pair_decomposition
records.entry_name: A partition-pair decomposition of the two-locus sampling probability with Ewens marginals
records.doc: This entry formalizes a decomposition of the two-locus sampling probability, under finite-allele parent-independent mutation, in terms of pairs of set partitions of the sample, with Ewens marginals at each locus. A partition-carrying ancestral process with coalescence, mutation, and recombination records, at each locus, which sample members lose their ancestry to the same mutation; the kernel is the probability that it ends with a given pair of partitions. The solution of the two-locus sampling recursion at a fully typed sample is the sum over pairs of partitions of the kernel times the probability that each block receives a single allele consistent with the sample. Summing the kernel over the partition at one locus gives the Ewens partition probability at the other; as the recombination rate tends to infinity the kernel tends to the product of the two Ewens partition probabilities; and with recombination rate 0 the common refinement of the two partitions has the Ewens law with parameter θA + θB. The sampling probability equals the product of its one-locus marginals for all parameter values exactly when at most one lineage is typed at one of the loci (with at least two alleles per locus). A closed form for configurations with two lineages typed at each locus is also stated, together with existence of a solution of the recursion.

The sampling probability equals the product of its one-locus marginals for all parameter values exactly when at most one lineage is typed at one of the loci (with at least two alleles per locus). A closed form for configurations with two lineages typed at each locus is also stated, together with existence of a solution of the recursion.

records.name: Rhone.Palomar.SamplingRecursion.exists_isSolution
records.entry_name: The two-locus sampling recursion of the coalescent with recombination: existence, uniqueness, and probabilistic interpretation
records.doc: This entry formalizes the two-locus sampling recursion of the coalescent with recombination, with finitely many alleles at each locus and parent-independent mutation. For positive mutation rates and nonnegative recombination rate, a solution exists and is unique, over any linearly ordered field. For real parameters, the solution at a sample typed at both loci equals the probability that the typed ancestral recombination graph, in which a mutation removes the ancestry of a lineage at that locus and assigns a type to the sample members it carries, ends with exactly the types of the sample. The solution sums to 1 over all typings of a sample of given size, tends to the product of the one-locus sampling probabilities as the recombination rate tends to infinity, and at recombination rate 0 gives a solution of a one-locus recursion on pairs of alleles. With mutation rates 0, the expected total branch length of the genealogy at locus A of a sample of size n is 2 times the sum of 1/(i + 1) for i < n − 1. The transition matrix of the typed ancestral chain is shown to be nonnegative with unit row sums.

records.name: Rhone.Palomar.SevenSiteSeparator.seven_site_separation
records.entry_name: Seven linked sites separate a two-island history from every panmictic history
records.doc: This entry formalizes a statement about blocks of seven completely linked sites with K ≥ 2 equally weighted roots, observed in three sampled sequences under an equal-rates K-state mutation model. A specific two-island history for three lineages (all three lineages start in the same island, the coalescence rate within an island is 1, and the migration rate is 1/100) produces, at mutation scale 1, a law of the seven-site block that differs from the block law of every panmictic history at every mutation scale k > 0. The panmictic histories are those given by a nonnegative locally integrable pairwise coalescence rate whose integrated clock diverges, so the population size may vary arbitrarily in time.

records.name: Rhone.Palomar.SmcPrimeBound.eventKernel_isMarkovKernel
records.entry_name: Total variation bound between an unpruned ancestral recombination process and SMC' on pairwise coalescence times
records.doc: This entry formalizes a total variation bound between the pairwise coalescence-time process of an unpruned ancestral recombination graph and the SMC' approximation, for N ≥ 1 samples, a unit-length genome, and scaled recombination rate R ≥ 0. The observed object is the collection of pairwise coalescence times of all sample pairs at every rational position in [0, 1). The total variation distance is at most an explicit double bound, which is at most min(1, R² times a quadratic coefficient in N − 1). The distance is 0 for one sample and for zero recombination. Supporting statements show that the event kernels of both processes are Markov, the two laws are probability measures, the number of live lineages of the backward process reaches at most one almost surely, the observed coalescence times are almost surely finite, and the expected number of active events, the expected total time, and the expected largest observed coalescence time are bounded by an explicit absorption budget.

records.name: Rhone.Palomar.TajimaD.markedKingmanLaw_probability
records.entry_name: Tajima's D under Kingman's coalescent: moments of the numerator, the variance estimate, and the expected spectrum
records.doc: This entry formalizes Tajima's D under Kingman's coalescent with infinitely many sites and mutation parameter θ ≥ 0, for sample size n ≥ 2. The joint law of the genealogy and the mutation counts on its branches is a probability measure. The mean of the numerator is 0 and its variance equals c₁ θ + c₂ θ², where c₁ and c₂ are Tajima's coefficients. The covariance of the pairwise-difference statistic with the number of segregating sites and the mean of their product are stated. The variance estimate based on the number of segregating sites is unbiased for that variance. The expected value of the site frequency spectrum at frequency i is θ/i for 1 ≤ i < n, and these values sum to the mean number of segregating sites; the closed-form coefficient of the expected spectrum equals θ/i and equals that mean. D is defined to be 0 when the variance estimate is nonpositive, and as a result it is 0 when there are no segregating sites and for n = 2 and n = 3; D is a measurable function of the sample.

records.name: Rhone.Palomar.WeakRegularSeparation.nonnegative_internal_branch_separation_iff
records.entry_name: When one finite block of linked sites separates a three-sample genealogy from every panmictic history
records.doc: This entry formalizes conditions under which a single finite block of linked sites separates a three-sample genealogy from every panmictic history. A law of the two coalescence-interval lengths and the tree shape of three sampled sequences is uniformly separated at mutation scale k > 0 when some block of L completely linked sites, observed under the equal-rates mutation model, has a law at ℓ1 distance at least a fixed ε > 0 from the block law of every panmictic history (any nonnegative, locally integrable, time-varying coalescence rate with a diverging integrated clock), at every mutation scale and for every alphabet size K ≥ 2. For laws with nonnegative interval lengths, a positive first coalescence time, and a regular first-survival profile matching the first coalescence time, uniform separation holds if and only if the law differs from the panmictic law with the profile's rate, in which the tree shape is uniform and independent of the times; a version for laws of the interval lengths alone, with a uniform independent shape, is also given. For three-sample symmetric island histories with time-varying coalescence and migration rates under the stated integrability hypotheses, uniform separation holds if and only if the history is not the one with all three lineages starting in the same island, no migration, and a diverging integrated coalescence clock. For finite-phase histories, separation is equivalent to failure of a density identity characterizing the panmictic form.

records.name: Rhone.Palomar.SelectionTheorems.fisher_fundamental_theorem
records.entry_name: Classical identities and a limit theorem of selection theory
records.doc: This entry collects classical identities and a limit theorem from selection theory. The identities are stated for finite populations; Geiringer's limit theorem is stated for the deterministic infinite-population recombination model on finitely many loci with a common finite allele set. Fisher's fundamental theorem is stated, in Ewens' interpretation, as the equality of the partial change in mean fitness (the change in allele frequencies under selection, weighted by least-squares average effects) with the additive genetic variance divided by mean fitness, for arbitrary genotype frequencies and any number of loci, together with nonnegativity of that change. A grouped covariance decomposition and a multilevel Price equation are stated as identities for arbitrary weights. Hamilton's rule is derived from the least-squares regression of fitness on own and social genotypes, and the existence of the Lande–Arnold gradient, equal to the inverse phenotypic covariance matrix applied to the vector of selection differentials, is stated under a nonsingular phenotypic covariance. Geiringer's theorem is stated as convergence of repeated recombination to the product of the single-locus marginals, under the condition that every pair of loci is separated with positive probability.

records.name: ThickSensitive.separated_open_targets
records.entry_name: Weak mixing and thick common multi-sensitivity
records.doc: A continuous surjective weakly mixing map on a nontrivial metric space admits one positive separation constant such that every finite family of nonempty open sets has arbitrarily long, arbitrarily late blocks of common positive separation times. Witness pairs may depend on the set and time. Finite-family common hitting thickness and separated open targets are proved.

Witness pairs may depend on the set and time. Finite-family common hitting thickness and separated open targets are proved.

records.name: CKM.NativeTightCodeConsumer.code_bound
records.entry_name: On the local geometry of the tight 39-point code in 𝕆P²
records.doc:
Cohn, Kumar and Minton constructed a universally optimal code of thirty-nine points in the octonionic projective plane 𝕆P², whose existence was conjectured by Hoggar. Its points form thirteen mutually unbiased Jordan frames, and a four-parameter phase family deforms the code through such configurations. This Lean development describes their local geometry under the automorphism group F₄. At every nonresonant phase, every nearby real solution of the defining equations belongs to one of four smooth families of labelled configurations. In a local slice for F₄, their union has normal form R⁴ × ⋃ᵢ₌₁⁴ R⁶ᵢ, with the R⁶ᵢ in direct sum. The distance to the localized family union is bounded by a phase-dependent constant times the square root of the residual, and the exponent 1/2 is sharp in the ambient configuration space. On an explicit open dense subset of the nonresonant phases, the complexified families are exactly the top-dimensional components of the complex solution germ, each generically reduced. Every neighbourhood of the original code in the space of unlabelled tight 39-point codes modulo F₄ contains points of local dimension 10.

The results are local, the resonant germ at the original code is not classified, and lower-dimensional complex components are not excluded. For exact frames and strongly convex C² overlap potentials, we prove a two-sided comparison of the energy gap with squared overlap errors and, near each nonresonant orbit, a quartic lower bound in distance to the localized family union. records.name: LeanLab.AlmostPrimes.U1504DudekAll.dudek_all_ap12
records.entry_name: On the sum of a prime and a square-free number
records.doc: Conditional on one explicit hypothesis, AP12Lower 0.21, taken as a hypothesis of the theorem and never as an axiom: for every integer x >= 10^9, each reduced residue class mod 12 holds more than 0.21 x / log x primes p <= x. Under it, a complete Lean 4 proof of Theorem 1 of A. W. Dudek, On the sum of a prime and a square-free number, The Ramanujan Journal 42, 2017: every integer N > 2 is the sum of a prime and a square-free number. AP12Lower 0.21 is implied by Corollary 1.6 of M. A. Bennett, G. Martin, K. O'Bryant and A. Rechnitzer, Explicit bounds for primes in arithmetic progressions, Illinois J. Math. 62, 2018, which gives 1/4 in place of 0.21; the entry proves that implication in Lean, with the corollary itself stated as a hypothesis. The even case, every even N >= 4, is proved with no hypothesis. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. The Lean code was written by an AI agent and is offered for human audit.

records.name: SidonSubmission.sidon_fourier_uniformity
records.entry_name: Extremal Sidon sets: Fourier uniformity and partition regularity
records.doc: A Lean formalization of Ortega and Prendiville's results on Sidon sets in integer intervals. It proves Fourier bounds for near-maximal and largest Sidon sets, equidistribution in progressions and Bohr sets, and monochromatic solutions to partition regular linear equations in at least five variables. It also proves sharp obstruction constructions and records a correction to the paper's dimension-independent approximation claim.

records.name: AuslanderYorke.equicontinuous_of_stable_open_sets
records.entry_name: Auslander–Yorke dichotomy for minimal metric maps
records.doc: For a continuous map of a metric space with every forward natural orbit dense, either the map is sensitive in the open-set pair sense or its natural iterate family is equicontinuous at every point. Stable open sets are propagated using dense orbits and finite early-time continuity. On nonempty spaces nonsensitivity is equivalent to equicontinuity; no compactness or uniform-equicontinuity assertion is required.

On nonempty spaces nonsensitivity is equivalent to equicontinuity; no compactness or uniform-equicontinuity assertion is required.

records.name: PalomarC3a.c3a_gt_121418
records.entry_name: A finite two-temperature lower bound for the GHR sum-difference constant
records.doc: The Gyarmati-Hennecart-Ruzsa constant C₃ₐ is the supremum of real exponents theta for which every K > 1 admits a positive constant c and arbitrarily large nonempty finite integer sets X with nonempty partners Y satisfying |X+Y| <= K|X| and c|X+Y|^theta <= |X-Y|. This formalization proves the strict bound C₃ₐ > 60709/50000 = 1.21418. A finite type at depth 10^13, separate difference and sum tilts, cyclic compression, and a proved finite-set principle supply the bound. The result concerns extremal sumset and difference-set growth in additive combinatorics. The paper's general limiting theorem is outside the formalized claim.

records.name: InfHarmonic.main_estimate
records.entry_name: Uniform interior C^{1,α} estimates for infinity-harmonic functions in dimensions d ≥ 3
records.doc: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main results of the preprint "Uniform Interior C^{1,α} Estimates for Infinity-Harmonic Functions" (OpenAI, 2026). For every dimension d ≥ 3 there are α ∈ (0, 1/3] and C < ∞ such that every bounded viscosity solution u of the infinity-Laplace equation Δ_∞u = Σ u_i u_j u_ij = 0 on the unit ball of ℝ^d is differentiable on the half ball, with sup |∇u| + [∇u]_{C^{0,α}} ≤ C · osc u (Theorem 1.1). Consequently every infinity-harmonic function on a connected open subset of ℝ^d, d ≥ 3, is C¹ (Corollary 1.2). The proof rests on a Liouville theorem for the degenerate limiting equation D²v[(∇ₓv, 1)] = 0 on space-time, for entire solutions admitting uniform affine fits at all scales (Theorem 3.1), which is also formalized. All three results are proved from Mathlib with no sorry and no axioms beyond propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, including the Crandall–Ishii–Lions theorem of sums and Alexandrov's theorem used along the way.

records.name: GeoSeqV4.halton_not_quasiUniform
records.entry_name: Low-discrepancy quasi-uniform digital sequences in every dimension (Halton-type failure and residue sequences)
records.doc:
Two results of the manuscript "Low-discrepancy quasi-uniform digital sequences in every dimension" (version 1): Corollary cor:halton of Theorem thm:nonqu, and Theorem thm:residue with Corollaries cor:korobov and cor:residueQU for one explicit sequence. Quasi-uniform means here: there is a real B such that h(P_[N]) <= B delta(P_[N]) for every N >= 2, where P_[N] is the set of the first N points, h is the Euclidean covering radius of [0,1]^s (a supremum over the cube of the minimum distance to the points) and delta is the minimum Euclidean distance over pairs of distinct indices. (1) For every prime p, every s >= 2 and all pairwise coprime polynomials b_0, ..., b_(s-1) over Z/pZ of degree >= 1, the Halton-type sequence in these bases (Goda-Hofer-Suzuki, Def. 2: coordinate c of the point with index n = sum_k n_k p^k reads the b_c-adic digits (V div b_c^Q) mod b_c of V = sum_k n_k z^k, each written as its deg(b_c) coefficients, the coefficient of z^(deg(b_c)-1) first) is not quasi-uniform, and for every eps > 0 there are m and two distinct indices v, w < p^m whose points have Euclidean distance less than eps (p^m)^(-1/s). For every prime p and every s such bases exist. (2) Let s >= 2, let p > 2^s be prime and rho = floor(p^(1/s)). Consider the residue sequence with the Faure places a_c = c, scale theta = 1 and the Korobov check vector v = (rho, rho^2, ..., rho^(s-1), -1): the digital sequence over Z/pZ with generator matrices C_c[n][i] = v_c^(-1) [t^n] (c + t)^i w_c(c + t)^(-(n+1)), w_c(z) = prod_(c' != c) (z - c'), and coordinates y_c = sum_n y_(c,n) p^(-n-1) with digits in {0, ..., p-1}. It is a (0,s)-sequence in base p; for every K >= 1, any two distinct indices u, u' < N = p^(sK-1) give points at toroidal Euclidean distance (sum_c (d_c - round(d_c))^2)^(1/2), d = difference of the points, at least (rho - 1) p^(-1/s) N^(-1/s); and it is quasi-uniform. Moreover rho >= 2 and rho^s < p, every v_c is nonzero, the places are distinct, and the power series w_c(c + t) over Z/pZ times its inverse is 1. (The entry states no discrepancy bound; that (0,s)-sequences have low discrepancy is classical and is not part of this entry.)

The Challenge (HeadlineSeqV4/Challenge.lean, 195 lines) imports only Mathlib and defines everything it uses from scratch (digital sequences from infinite generator matrices over ZMod p, the (0,s)-sequence property, Euclidean and toroidal distances, covering radius, minimum distance, quasi-uniformity, the Halton-type points, the residue generator matrices). records.name: DixonRelations.zeroSum_irreducible
records.entry_name: The additive theorem for 2-transitive Galois groups (Girstmair; Dixon, Theorem 1') and its representation-theoretic engine
records.doc: Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of the homogeneous case and, at the roots, of the printed form (relations with value in K), with coefficients in any field K of characteristic 0, of the additive theorem for 2-transitive Galois groups (Girstmair, Manuscripta Math. 39 (1982) 81-97, Proposition 4, Assertion 3, p. 86, for every field whose characteristic does not divide |G|; stated by J. D. Dixon, Acta Arith. 82 (1997) 293-302, as Theorem 1', p. 301, with its proof omitted), of its representation-theoretic engine (classical: Huppert, Endliche Gruppen I, p. 597, Satz 20.2, as cited by Girstmair, Acta Arith. 89 (1999) 53-96, p. 78; used by Dixon on p. 297, in the proof of Theorem 1(ii), citing Curtis-Reiner Section 32B), and of two criterion forms over any field whose hypothesis is the irreducibility of the augmentation module instead of 2-transitivity (the 'if' direction of Girstmair 1982, Proposition 4, Assertion 2, in its module form). Eight compared theorems, in namespace DixonRelations, in this order. (1) zeroSum_irreducible, the engine: for a finite group G acting 2-transitively on a finite set Omega with 2 <= |Omega| and a field K of characteristic 0, the augmentation (zero-sum) subspace V0 = {f : Omega -> K | sum_x f x = 0} of the permutation module Omega -> K is an irreducible K[G]-module; proved in the substantive form of simplicity, that a G-invariant subspace W <= V0 with W != bot equals V0. The G-action is the permutation representation (g . f) x = f (g^{-1} . x), and a subrepresentation is a Submodule together with an explicit invariance hypothesis. (2') additive_core_of_irreducible, the zero-sum criterion form: for any field K, any group G (finite or not) acting on a finite Omega, an injective family alpha : Omega -> L into a K-vector space L, K-linear maps phi g with phi g (alpha x) = alpha (g . x) (no homomorphism property assumed), and the hypothesis hirr (every nonzero G-invariant K-subspace of V0 is V0, word for word the conclusion of (1); it holds vacuously when V0 = 0, that is |Omega| <= 1), any c with sum_x c x = 0 and sum_x c x . alpha x = 0 is 0. (2) additive_core, the zero-sum form for an abstract family: the same conclusion for K of characteristic 0 and a finite group G acting 2-transitively on Omega with 2 <= |Omega|; it is (1) followed by (2'). (3) additive_roots_no_relation, the zero-sum form at the roots: for K of characteristic 0 and an irreducible f in K[X] of degree >= 2 whose Galois group acts 2-transitively on the roots of f in the splitting field, any K-valued coefficient tuple c on the roots with sum_r c r = 0 and sum_r c r . r = 0 is 0; G = f.Gal, Omega = f.rootSet f.SplittingField (with Mathlib's instance Polynomial.Gal.galActionAux), the family is the inclusion of the root set, phi g is the field automorphism g read as a K-linear map (the compatibility holds by rfl), and 2 <= |Omega| follows from card_rootSet_eq_natDegree with separability from Irreducible.separable; f.SplittingField appears in the 2-transitivity hypothesis and in the types of c and of the relation hypothesis. (3) is the zero-sum part (value 0, coefficient sum 0) of the homogeneous case of Dixon's Theorem 1' at the roots; the full homogeneous case at the roots is (5), and the inhomogeneous case is (6). (4') relModule_le_span_one_of_irreducible, the span-one criterion form: under the hypotheses of (2') and a transitive action, every coefficient tuple c with sum_x c x . alpha x = 0 is a scalar multiple of the all-ones tuple, i.e. relModule K alpha is contained in the line K . (fun _ => 1). This is the 'if' direction of Girstmair 1982, Proposition 4, Assertion 2 (p. 86: "If G is primitive on G/H, (G,H) admits only trivial relations over K iff the complementary module U(G/H) of K epsilon_0 is simple"), whose hypothesis is, like hirr, the simplicity of a module; Girstmair 1999 restates it in character form as Proposition 12 (p. 78), "essentially contained in Proposition 4 of [11]". (4') assumes transitivity in place of primitivity; for a transitive action, hirr already forces primitivity (elementary, not formalized: the zero-sum functions constant on the blocks of a nontrivial block system form a nonzero proper invariant subspace of V0), so the difference is one of form only. (4) relModule_le_span_one, the span-one form: the same conclusion under the hypotheses of (2); it is (1) followed by (4'). (5) relModule_roots_le_span_one, the span-one form at the roots: under the hypotheses of (3), relModule K of the root family (fun r => (r : f.SplittingField)) is contained in K . (fun _ => 1); it is (4) at the roots. (6) roots_inhomogeneous_iff_const, Dixon's printed form at the roots: under the hypotheses of (3), sum_r c r . r = algebraMap K f.SplittingField k for some k in K if and only if c is constant; in Dixon's notation this is U = K.e. Dixon's Theorem 1' is stated for any subfield K of C and for relations with value in K; compared statements (2), (3), (4) and (5) concern its homogeneous case (value 0) and (6) its printed form (value in K), for every field K of characteristic 0, and (2') and (4') take any field. Girstmair 1982 states the additive theorem for every field whose characteristic does not divide |G|, so characteristic 0 is a sub-case of his hypothesis; (2') and (4') take any field, but their content is carried by hirr, which this entry proves only in characteristic 0 and only for 2-transitive actions, as (1). An uncompared bridge, BDS.isAtom_zeroSumSubrep_iff, shows that hirr together with V0 != bot is atomicity of V0 in Mathlib's lattice of subrepresentations of the permutation representation on Omega -> K. (1) is proved by an elementary, character-free stabilizer-averaging argument; Dixon (p. 297) cites Curtis-Reiner Section 32B for the statement only; Curtis-Reiner was not consulted, and nothing is claimed about its proof. records.name: SinkReset.reset_word_le_of_isAk
records.entry_name: Sharp reset thresholds for bounded-response synchronization games with a sink
records.doc: Lean 4 / Mathlib statements of the theorem M(n,k) = sum_{i=1}^{n-1} ceil(i/k) for k = 1 or n <= k+3 (Lipin-Volkov k-game on automata with a sink), rendered as an upper and a lower bound, with the headline case M(5,2) = 6, proved in Solution.lean from the development SinkReset.Plan written in the conductor formalize run 2026-10-25_formalize-sinkresetthresholds. The endpoints k = 1 (Rystsov's tight bound n(n-1)/2) and k = n-1 were known from Lipin-Volkov; the new content is M(k+2,k) = k+2 and M(k+3,k) = k+4 for k >= 2, including the non-divisible pairs (4,2) and (5,3), which the Lipin-Volkov conjecture (stated for k | n-1 only) does not cover; (5,2) is the first pair with k | n-1 that is neither endpoint, i.e. the first pair on which the Lipin-Volkov conjecture itself was open ((4,2) is the first non-endpoint pair of all).

records.name: PaperCharZero.Palomar.theoremA
records.entry_name: PCF all the way down
records.doc:
Let k be a field of characteristic zero and let f: X → X be a finite surjective map of integral k-schemes of finite type. By the critical locus of f we mean the image in X of the critical locus of the map induced on the normalization of X. By the branch locus we mean the image of the critical locus under f.

We say that f is post-critically finite (PCF) if, for every irreducible divisor D contained in the branch locus, the forward orbit f(D) ∪ f^2(D) ∪ … is algebraic, that is, a finite union of subvarieties, taken as a closed subscheme with its reduced induced structure.

We prove that if f is PCF and A is a preperiodic divisor for f with f^{r+s}(A) = f^r(A), then, setting B = f^r(A) and g = f^s, the restriction of g to B is PCF.

This proves the PCF all the way down conjecture: restricting again to preperiodic divisors and iterating gives PCF maps at every stage.

records.name: HardyLadder.Entry.ladder_prob_le
records.entry_name: The two-qubit Hardy ladder: the closed form P_K*(q) and its unique maximiser for every K, Hardy's optimum at K = 1, and the optimum (8 rho^2 + rho - 11)/25 in the cubic field Q(rho) at K = 2
records.doc: Kernel-checked optimum of Hardy's K-step ladder for two qubits (Hardy 1993; Hardy 1997; Boschi, Branca, De Martini and Hardy 1997), for a real Schmidt state c0|00> + c1|11> and real projective settings, the probabilities written out as squared real amplitudes. For every K: under the ladder constraints P(A_K = 1, B_K = 1) <= q^2 (1 - q^{2K})^2 / ((1 + q^2)(1 + q^{2K+1})^2), q = c1/c0, with equality attained (Cereceda 2002, eqs. (18)-(19)); the probability is below 1/2 (the two-qubit, real-settings case of a bound that follows in every dimension from Cereceda 2016, eq. (9), with Wehner 2006), and for every eps > 0 and every large enough K some state and settings exceed 1/2 - eps (the "(50 - delta)%" of Hardy 1997 and Boschi et al. 1997). For every K >= 1 the maximiser of the closed form on (0, 1) is the unique zero there of Cereceda's polynomial m_K (Cereceda 2002, eq. (20), stated there without proof): the derivative of the closed form, the existence and uniqueness of the zero, the maximum and its uniqueness, and, over all Schmidt states and real settings, the optimum, its attainment at the Schmidt ratio r, and that every optimal configuration has Schmidt ratio r or 1/r (attainment at 1/r follows from the uncompared symmetry). Worked instances: the K = 1 optimum is phi^{-5} = (5 sqrt 5 - 11)/2 (Hardy 1993), attained at a state with 2 c0 c1 = 3 - sqrt 5 and only where 2 c0 c1 = 3 - sqrt 5 (Hardy's condition); the K = 2 optimum is (8 rho^2 + rho - 11)/25 = 0.17455..., rho the plastic number (the real root of x^3 - x - 1), attained at Schmidt weights c0^2 = rho^{-1}, c1^2 = rho^{-5} (c1/c0 = rho^{-2}) and only where {c0^2, c1^2} = {rho^{-1}, rho^{-5}}. The value 0.17455 is in print numerically; the closed form, the maximiser rho^{-2}, the weights and the minimal polynomial 25x^3 + 17x^2 + 2x - 1 of the value were not found in the literature searched (2026-10-28) and are the entry's new content. Also: the K = 2 value is not totally real (its minimal polynomial has a non-real complex root). Optimality over complex settings is not formalised. Thirty compared statements.

records.name: WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture96.conjecture96
records.entry_name: Proof of WOWII Conjecture 96 (DeLaVina, Graffiti.pc)
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof of Conjecture 96 of Written on the Wall II (Graffiti.pc): every connected graph G on at least two vertices satisfies α(G) ≤ 1 + min_v disteven(v)·(max_v l(v) − 1), where disteven(v) is the number of vertices at even distance from v and l(v) is the independence number of the neighbourhood of v. The proof gives the stronger bound α(G) ≤ 1 + disteven(v)·(L − 1) for every vertex v, which is sharp for stars.

records.name: Parking.tvDist_firstCoordsLaw_bounds
records.entry_name: Parking functions: total variation threshold and critical profile
records.doc: A Lean formalization of the total variation threshold for initial coordinates of a uniform parking function. The three recorded results give uniform finite-size bounds, the Gaussian critical profile at scale n/log n (including zero and infinite parameters), and a quantitative relative-entropy and total-variation comparison with independent marginals. The library reconstructs the supplied manuscript through Borel marginal asymptotics, homogeneous log-concavity and entropy methods. It also proves the separate Pitman–Stanley volume-polynomial remark. The results concern probabilists and combinatorialists studying random discrete structures, approximation by independent variables and negative dependence.

records.name: ABLP2026.lemma_2_1
records.entry_name: Fractional triangle decompositions of dense tripartite graphs
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main results of Allsop, Bowtell, Lesgourgues and Petrova, "Improved bounds on completion of partial Latin squares" (arXiv:2609.37877, 2026): there is η > 0 (here η = 1/20000) such that every K₃-divisible spanning subgraph of K_{n,n,n} with minimum partite degree at least (0.769 − η)n has a fractional triangle decomposition (Theorem 1.3). Also formalized: the Farkas characterization (Lemma 2.1); the reduction to triangle-covered, balanced, untied and nonzero edge weightings (Proposition 3.1, Corollary 3.5), with Lemma 3.4 proved through an integral maximum flow; the non-uniform proportional discharging (Definition 4.1) and its two estimates (Propositions 4.2 and 4.3); and the numerical inequality g_d ≥ 1 for the article's piecewise-linear f (Proposition 4.4). The two-variable inequalities of Proposition 4.4, which the article settles by numerical minimisation, are proved exactly by Bernstein certificates checked in Lean. Not formalized: the article's Corollary 1.4 (completion of partial Latin squares), which also needs the fractional-to-exact transfer of Barber, Kühn, Lo, Osthus and Taylor for tripartite graphs.

records.entry_name: A dimension-free weak-type (1,1) bound for the Gaussian Riesz transforms
records.doc: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main results of Gutiérrez and Manfredi, "A direct obstacle proof of a dimension-free weak-type (1,1) bound for the Gaussian Riesz transforms" (arXiv:2610.26478). For the Gaussian measure dγₙ = π^{-n/2} e^{-|x|²} dx on ℝⁿ, the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck operator L = -½Δ + x·∇ and the normalized gradient D = 2^{-1/2}∇, the vector Riesz transform R_γ = D L^{-1/2} Π₀ has exactly one linear extension to L¹(γₙ) satisfying t·γₙ{|R_γ f| > t} ≤ 2‖f‖₁ for all t > 0, in every dimension n (Theorem 5.1). The proof goes through a Gaussian obstacle decomposition F = g + L^{1/2}u, with existence, uniqueness and the variational characterization of u, and the identification Dom(L^{1/2}) ⊆ W^{1,2}(γₙ) (Theorem 3.1). Also formalized: the principal-value realization of the extension by the Gaussian Riesz kernels (Proposition 5.3), the coordinatewise, historically normalized and unnormalized-measure bounds (Corollary 5.4), and the complex-valued bound with constant 8/π (Corollary 5.5). The Hermite basis of L²(γₙ) and the spectral calculus of L are built from Mathlib; there is no sorry and no axiom beyond propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.name: NairTenenbaum.Submission.theoremOne
records.entry_name: Short sums of certain arithmetic functions (Nair–Tenenbaum)
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of Nair and Tenenbaum's uniform upper bounds for short sums of nonnegative arithmetic functions evaluated at integer polynomial values. Theorem 1 retains the coefficient-independent height threshold and the restricted-discriminant dependence of the bound. Theorem 2 gives a greatest-prime-factor bound with a strict exponential gain for arbitrary nonconstant irreducible integer polynomials, including those with fixed prime divisors. Theorem 3 treats prime arguments with the explicit constant-term correction. The development also proves the ten corollaries on progressions, Hooley moments, smooth values, shifted primes, dyadic averages, and Goldbach representations, and Lemma 2 for general class-M weights. Corollary 6 has an explicit nonconstancy condition; the printed Lemma 1 has a checked counterexample and the required replacements are proved.

records.name: SmallRatio.reciprocity
records.entry_name: SmallRatio: Dedekind sums along Euclid's algorithm and the small-ratio formula
records.doc: For a prime p and 0 < h < p, the Dedekind sum s(h,p) is determined, up to an explicit error of order log p, by the fractions of small height congruent to plus or minus h: with the sum over the coprime pairs u, v >= 1 with uv < p/2, |12 s(h,p) - p sum ([hv = u mod p] - [hv = -u mod p])/(uv)| <= 6n <= 12 log_2 p + 6, where n is the length of Euclid's algorithm on (p, h). Summed over any set H of residues, in particular over a subgroup of odd order, this gives |12 sum_{h in H} s(h,p) - p S_H(p)| <= |H| (12 log_2 p + 6), where S_H(p) is the signed sum of 1/(uv) over the coprime pairs with uv < p/2 and u/v in H or -H. The development proves Dedekind reciprocity from scratch (by counting lattice points), the identities of Euclid's algorithm and the bound n <= 2 log_2 k + 1, the alternating-sum form 12 s(h,k) = sum (-1)^{j+1} k/(r_j q_{j-1}) + E with |E| <= 4n, and Legendre's pairing of the small coprime pairs with the steps of the algorithm, by a lattice-basis argument instead of continued fractions.

records.name: FreezingStatements.height_scaling_limit
records.entry_name: Uniform attachment with freezing: Scaling limits — Lean formalization
records.doc: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of arXiv:2308.00484, "Uniform attachment with freezing: Scaling limits", published in Ann. Inst. H. Poincaré Probab. Statist. 61(4) 2679–2708 (2025). It proves the Introduction's height theorem, the subcritical Gromov–Hausdorff–Prokhorov (GHP) limit to a measured segment, the critical GHP limit to a random compact measured real tree T(f) together with its geometric properties (leaves carry the mass; binary if and only if the reciprocal-square integral diverges; root condensation otherwise), and the supercritical distance-matrix limit in its corrected zero-diagonal form. All numbered intermediate results are proved, several in corrected or qualified forms. The CRT corollary (cor:CRT) is not formalized. Height and forward-tree modules are adapted from the companion formalization of "Uniform attachment with freezing" by the same contributor (not yet public; see docs/companion-provenance.md).

records.name: IJM.TSP.MSTCost_le_OPT
records.entry_name: Machine-Checked Christofides 3/2-Approximation and Polyhedral Complexity Barriers for the Traveling Salesperson Problem in Lean 4
records.doc: This formalization develops a machine-checked theory of the Traveling Salesperson Problem (TSP) on finite undirected graphs over Fin n in Lean 4 across two principal modules. First, in Christofides.lean (compared against ChallengeChristofides.lean), we formalize the complete Christofides-Serdyukov 3/2-approximation algorithm for Metric TSP: the Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) lower bound (cost(T) <= OPT), Euler's handshaking parity invariant for odd-degree vertices, the minimum-weight perfect matching upper bound on odd-degree vertices (2 * cost(M) <= OPT) via alternating matching decomposition of shortcut cycles, multigraph degree parity of T U M, constructive existence of Eulerian circuits via Hierholzer cycle splicing and complete Christofides certificates, metric walk shortcutting contraction, and the unconditional 3/2-approximation guarantee in both exact integer scaling and real arithmetic. Second, in TSPComplexity.lean (compared against ChallengeTSPComplexity.lean), we formalize polyhedral and complexity-theoretic barriers for Decision TSP: a fuel-bounded branch-and-cut state machine with verified soundness, completeness, and support-pruned cycle-separation rank decision equivalence; the Dantzig-Fulkerson-Johnson (DFJ) subtour cut inequality (every valid tour crosses any proper nonempty cut at least twice); the continuous Held-Karp LP relaxation embedding; a machine-checked proof that the 10-vertex Petersen graph fractional assignment (x_e = 2/3) strictly separates the Held-Karp relaxation from the integral TSP polytope with zero slack on singleton cuts and slack >= 2/3 on all nontrivial cuts; Yannakakis DFJ slack matrix nonnegativity and conditional Fiorini-Rothvoss PSD extension complexity scaling; and polynomial-time reductions from Hamiltonian Cycle and gadget-parameterized 3-SAT to Decision TSP.

First, in Christofides.lean (compared against ChallengeChristofides.lean), we formalize the complete Christofides-Serdyukov 3/2-approximation algorithm for Metric TSP: the Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) lower bound (cost(T) <= OPT), Euler's handshaking parity invariant for odd-degree vertices, the minimum-weight perfect matching upper bound on odd-degree vertices (2 * cost(M) <= OPT) via alternating matching decomposition of shortcut cycles, multigraph degree parity of T U M, constructive existence of Eulerian circuits via Hierholzer cycle splicing and complete Christofides certificates, metric walk shortcutting contraction, and the unconditional 3/2-approximation guarantee in both exact integer scaling and real arithmetic. Second, in TSPComplexity.lean (compared against ChallengeTSPComplexity.lean), we formalize polyhedral and complexity-theoretic barriers for Decision TSP: a fuel-bounded branch-and-cut state machine with verified soundness, completeness, and support-pruned cycle-separation rank decision equivalence; the Dantzig-Fulkerson-Johnson (DFJ) subtour cut inequality (every valid tour crosses any proper nonempty cut at least twice); the continuous Held-Karp LP relaxation embedding; a machine-checked proof that the 10-vertex Petersen graph fractional assignment (x_e = 2/3) strictly separates the Held-Karp relaxation from the integral TSP polytope with zero slack on singleton cuts and slack >= 2/3 on all nontrivial cuts; Yannakakis DFJ slack matrix nonnegativity and conditional Fiorini-Rothvoss PSD extension complexity scaling; and polynomial-time reductions from Hamiltonian Cycle and gadget-parameterized 3-SAT to Decision TSP.

records.name: DosenPetric.Palomar.maximality
records.entry_name: Maximality of the Došen–Petrić Boolean Category
records.doc: Let P be a nonempty set of propositional variables. The freely generated zero-identity Boolean category B(P) of Došen and Petrić is maximal: every congruence on its morphisms preserved by the operations on morphisms and uniform formula substitution is either equality or identifies every pair of parallel morphisms. The formalization gives two proofs of maximality and proves the congruence dichotomy. It also proves that the identity and zero endomorphism of each variable are distinct, and that there is no morphism from the terminal object to the initial object.

records.name: NoUniversalFSigma.not_isUniversalFSigma
records.entry_name: There is no universal Fσ equivalence relation
records.doc: There is no universal Fσ equivalence relation. This is the main result of arxiv:2610.31052. More detail: An equivalence relation E on a Polish space X is said to be Fσ if it is a countable union of closed subsets of X × X. For equivalence relations E and F on Polish spaces X and Y, we say that E is Borel reducible to F, written E ≤_B F, if there exists a Borel function f : X → Y such that for all x, y ∈ X, we have x E y if and only if f(x) F f(y). An Fσ equivalence relation E is universal if for every Fσ equivalence relation F, we have F ≤_B E. The theorem states that there's no such relation.

records.name: PoissonConjecture.poisson_conjecture
records.entry_name: fc-poisson-2
records.doc: A machine-checked proof that the Poisson conjecture fails for two canonical pairs, and hence for every n >= 2, following the explicit counterexample of C. D. Long (2026). The statements and definitions are Formal Conjectures' (PoissonConjecture.lean, arXiv math/0608009), copied verbatim into Challenge.lean, so this entry proves Formal Conjectures' own statements.

records.name: Erdos919.erdos_919.variants.iff_erdos_918_i
records.entry_name: Reductions for Erdős Problem 919
records.doc: Erdős Problem 919 asks for a graph on the ordinal omega_2 squared with chromatic number aleph_2, or aleph_1, such that every subgraph on a vertex set of smaller order type has chromatic number at most aleph_0. This formalization proves in ZFC that the aleph_2 question is equivalent to the first question of Erdős Problem 918, that the aleph_1 question is equivalent to the existence of a graph on aleph_2 vertices that is not countably chromatic although all its subgraphs on aleph_1 vertices are, that the aleph_2 question implies the aleph_1 question, and that the aleph_1 question has a positive answer under the continuum hypothesis. The proof blows a graph on omega_2 up to a graph on omega_2 times omega_2 in the lexicographic order. It does not settle either question in ZFC.

The proof blows a graph on omega_2 up to a graph on omega_2 times omega_2 in the lexicographic order. It does not settle either question in ZFC.

records.name: ArtGallery.agpOrth_inER
records.entry_name: The orthogonal art gallery problem is ∃ℝ-complete (point-point and point-boundary), in Lean 4
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of material in a forthcoming manuscript entitled "The Orthogonal Art Gallery Problem is ∃ℝ-complete". A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof, for an explicit single-tape Turing machine model, that deciding whether an orthogonal simple polygon (every edge horizontal or vertical) with rational corners can be guarded by g guards is ∃ℝ-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions, both when the guards must see the whole polygon (point-point) and when they must see only its boundary (point-boundary). Both problems also reduce to ETR by formulas whose only variables are the 2g coordinates of the guards. As far as we could determine, hardness for orthogonal polygons was open: it is treated neither by Abrahamsen, Adamaszek and Miltzow (J. ACM 2021) nor by Stade (SoCG 2025). The hardness proof is a new construction derived from Stade's polygon: needles become corridors, wedges become rectangles with needle cutters, the slanted mouths of the copy nooks are kept through helper guards pinned by four-armed crosses, and the addition gadgets are replaced by new orthogonal rooms. Its visibility, pinning and coverage facts are checked by the kernel as certificates (cone propagation with a symbolic height parameter, polynomial sign tests for the copy nooks, coverage by convex items). The proofs use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.name: BKLOT2017.corollary_1_6
records.entry_name: Triangle decompositions of dense tripartite graphs and completion of partial Latin squares
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Corollary 1.6 for r = 3 of Barber, Kühn, Lo, Osthus and Taylor, "Clique decompositions of multipartite graphs and completion of Latin squares" (J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 151 (2017), arXiv:1603.01043): fractional triangle decompositions above a threshold give triangle decompositions above the same threshold. Precisely: if δ ≥ 3/4 and, for every ε > 0, every K₃-divisible tripartite graph with three parts of size n ≥ n₀(ε) and minimum partite degree at least (δ + ε)n has a fractional triangle decomposition, then for every ε > 0 there is n₀ such that every K₃-divisible tripartite graph with parts of size n ≥ n₀ and minimum partite degree at least (δ + ε)n has a triangle decomposition (BKLOT2017.corollary_1_6). The hypothesis δ ≥ 3/4 is an extra assumption of the Lean statement: the article does not need it because the fractional threshold is known to be at least 3/4, which is not formalized here. Combined with the fractional bound of Allsop, Bowtell, Lesgourgues and Petrova (pinned entry PALOMAR-2026-10-30-000008), this gives the unconditional statement with threshold 0.769 − 1/20000 (BKLOT2017.corollary_1_6_ablp). The proof follows the iterative absorption of the article (absorbers, vortex of partitions with random reserves, cover-down, balancing graph, assembly) but replaces the regularity-based Section 8 by a route through the fractional threshold and the Haxell–Rödl transfer. Version 2 adds Theorem 1.4 and Corollary 3.2 for r = 3, the completion of partial Latin squares: for every ε > 0 and all large n, every partial Latin square of order n in which every row, every column and every symbol is used at most (1 − δ − ε)n times extends to a Latin square, above the fractional threshold δ ≥ 3/4 (BKLOT2017.theorem_1_4, from Cor16 δ by BKLOT2017.corollary_3_2) and unconditionally with 1 − δ = 0.231 + 1/20000 (BKLOT2017.theorem_1_4_ablp).

records.name: ErdosPaperVI.theorem_A
records.entry_name: Optimal clique partitions under local perturbations
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main results of the author's preprint "Optimal Clique Partitions under Local Perturbations" (Erdős #81 series, Paper VI). For a graph G on n vertices with a core P of size p = ⌊(n+1)/3⌋, h = Δ(G △ (K_P ∨ I_O)) and u, s, m the numbers of core, crossing and exterior edges: if p ≥ 18h + 1 then cp(G) = cp_{≤4}(G) = s − u − 2m = M(n) + C − A − 2m with M(n) = ⌊n(n+1)/6⌋ (Theorem A), and cp_{≤3}(G) − cp(G) = m (Theorem B); if p ≥ 63h, every assignment of the orders 4 or 5 to the exterior edges is realized by an optimal partition (Theorem C); for p ≥ 16 each assignment has at least p^{⌊p²/64⌋} optimal partitions and 2^m p^{⌊p²/64⌋} ≤ N(G) ≤ (n+1)^{5e(G)} (Theorem E). Also: the formula for other core sizes in an explicit window (Proposition 2.1), the intrinsic maximum over all cores (§8.1), the exact optimum with one exceptional vertex, cp = cp_{≤4} = cp*_= = s − u − 2m + D(a,b), ν₃ = ν₃* = u + min(a,b) and the restriction gap (Theorem D), and the complete-join variant cp(G) = M(n) − 2m (Theorem A.1). Twelve statements in all. The constants 18, 63, 16 and 24 are those of the paper; their optimality is not claimed.

For a graph G on n vertices with a core P of size p = ⌊(n+1)/3⌋, h = Δ(G △ (K_P ∨ I_O)) and u, s, m the numbers of core, crossing and exterior edges: if p ≥ 18h + 1 then cp(G) = cp_{≤4}(G) = s − u − 2m = M(n) + C − A − 2m with M(n) = ⌊n(n+1)/6⌋ (Theorem A), and cp_{≤3}(G) − cp(G) = m (Theorem B); if p ≥ 63h, every assignment of the orders 4 or 5 to the exterior edges is realized by an optimal partition (Theorem C); for p ≥ 16 each assignment has at least p^{⌊p²/64⌋} optimal partitions and 2^m p^{⌊p²/64⌋} ≤ N(G) ≤ (n+1)^{5e(G)} (Theorem E). Also: the formula for other core sizes in an explicit window (Proposition 2.1), the intrinsic maximum over all cores (§8.1), the exact optimum with one exceptional vertex, cp = cp_{≤4} = cp*_= = s − u − 2m + D(a,b), ν₃ = ν₃* = u + min(a,b) and the restriction gap (Theorem D), and the complete-join variant cp(G) = M(n) − 2m (Theorem A.1). Twelve statements in all. The constants 18, 63, 16 and 24 are those of the paper; their optimality is not claimed.

records.name: Freezing1.SIR.physical_sir_geometric_local_limit_of_source_ratio
records.entry_name: Uniform attachment with freezing: SIR epidemic and infection-tree limits
records.doc: Lean proofs of the local, fluid and terminal geometric limits of the SIR epidemic and its infection tree. The selected results include the finite-rate geometric Bienaymé limit, strong-rate non-tightness, the finite-rate fluid and height/distance survival mixtures, and the strong-rate fluid, height, distance and maximum-height limits. The physical model uses independent exponential recoveries and infection-age contact paths; existence for positive rates and the relevant clock-law identifications are proved. This entry covers T06–T07 and shares its proof repository with the other main-result groups.

records.name: Erdos835Palomar.johnson_chromaticNumber_composite
records.entry_name: Erdős Problem 835 when k + 1 is composite: the chromatic number of J(2k, k) exceeds k + 1
records.doc: Erdős Problem 835 asks whether, for some k > 2, the k-element subsets of a 2k-element set can be coloured with k + 1 colours so that every (k + 1)-element set sees all k + 1 colours among its k-element subsets; equivalently, whether the Johnson graph J(2k, k) has chromatic number k + 1 for some k > 2. Jie Ma and Quanyu Tang showed that this fails whenever k + 1 is not prime. This Lean 4 formalization proves, with Mathlib only: the equivalence between the colouring property and χ(J(2k, k)) = k + 1 for k > 0; χ(J(2k, k)) > k + 1 for every k > 2 with k + 1 composite; the consequence for every odd k > 2; and χ(J(18, 9)) > 10. The proof is a double count of the k-subsets of one colour inside a (k + j)-set, which forces k + 1 to divide (k + j).choose j for 1 ≤ j ≤ k; a prime p < k + 1 dividing k + 1 violates this at j = p. The case where k + 1 is prime, and so the problem itself, remains open; no new mathematics is claimed.

records.name: AffineFK.affine_reverse_faber_krahn_principal_results
records.entry_name: A formal proof of an affine reverse Faber-Krahn inequality
records.doc: The three principal manuscript results M01, M02 and M03, with their original domains and quantifier order. M01: one finite C>0 before every n>0 and compact convex Euclidean body K with nonempty interior; there exists a literal real special-linear matrix S with finite actual H0 Rayleigh infimum on interior(S K) and lambda_1(interior(S K))*volume(K)^(2/n)<=C*n. M02: one finite C>0 before every n>0 and origin-symmetric compact convex volume-one K with nonempty interior in maximal Gaussian measure position; its actual H0 Rayleigh infimum is at most C*n. M03: for each real P>=2 one finite C(P)>0 precedes every n>0, every even isotropic probability law nu satisfying the conventional compact-set IsLogConcaveMeasure condition, least Poincare constant at most P and finite actual Gaussian-relative Fisher information, and every origin-symmetric compact convex body D with nonempty interior supporting nu almost everywhere; lambda_1(interior D)<=C(P)*(n+sqrt(n*I(nu|gamma))). The log-concave density is derived from the law's original finite-information hypothesis; no density witness, covariance lower bound, ellipsoid-existence conclusion or desired spectral estimate is an additional premise. This standalone combined M01/M02/M03 package passed its own ordinary Linux sandboxed Comparator --paranoid with all six configured kernels. Its actual build, complete fixed-statement comparison, private proof inspection, axiom reports and separate AI reviews are retained under verification/.

records.name: MurtySimonConjecture.murty_simon
records.entry_name: The Murty–Simon conjecture on diameter-2-critical graphs
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the proof by Sanjana Das and Jacob Fox of the Murty–Simon conjecture (arXiv:2610.39032, 2026). A graph is diameter-2-critical if its diameter is 2 and deleting any edge increases the diameter. Theorem 1.1: every diameter-2-critical graph on n vertices has at most ⌊n²/4⌋ edges (murty_simon), and a diameter-2-critical graph with ⌊n²/4⌋ edges is isomorphic to K_{⌈n/2⌉,⌊n/2⌋} (murty_simon_equality). records.entry_name: The height of the infection tree
records.doc: A Lean formalization of all 31 numbered results of The height of the infection tree under the embedded SIR epidemic model, with six explicit statement corrections or endpoint conventions. The height theorem retains arbitrary asymptotic infection-rate sequences and the full Bernoulli mixture across early extinction and macroscopic survival. The strong profile theorem retains exact lattice heights, the Gaussian logarithmic correction and compact-parameter uniformity. These results concern probabilists studying random trees, branching processes and epidemic geometry. The proposed Palomar entry selects the two main theorems and the following parameter-uniform strengthening; the full library and result-by-result coverage record are included.

records.name: APNLinearity.linearity_upper_bounds
records.entry_name: Linearity bounds for APN functions
records.doc: Lean 4 formalization of linearity bounds for almost perfect nonlinear (APN) maps F: 𝔽₂ⁿ → 𝔽₂ⁿ. Write N = 2ⁿ and let L(F) denote the maximum Walsh magnitude over components indexed by nonzero vectors. For n ≥ 5, the formalization establishes L(F) ≤ N − 6, together with L(F) ≤ N − √N/4 − 2 when n is even. For n ≥ 4, ordering the Walsh magnitudes in nonincreasing order as L_k(F) gives L_k(F) ≤ (N/√k)√(1 + (2^(k−1) − 1)/N) for 1 ≤ k ≤ N(N − 1). In particular, L₂(F) ≤ 2⌊N/3⌋ and L₄(F) ≤ N/2. Further bounds relate linearity to the count q of nonplateaued components with nonzero indices. In odd dimension, q > 0 implies L(F)² ≤ N(1 + √(q(N − 1))). In even dimension, whenever 1/2 ≤ C < 1, the condition q ≤ (4C − C² − 1)N/4 + 1 implies L(F) ≤ CN. Additional results sharpen the upper bound on the linearity in certain odd dimensions and constrain the second-largest Walsh magnitude when the linearity is close to N.
