records.name: KLSOpenAI.kls
records.entry_name: Dimension-free KLS Poincare bound for isotropic log-concave densities
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib library for Poincare inequalities, log-concave probability measures and stochastic localization. Its dimension-free KLS theorem bounds the intrinsic local-slope Poincare constant by one universal constant times the covariance operator norm, including dimension zero and singular affine supports, for log-concave probability laws with finite second moment. The proof follows Bizeul-Klartag-Lehec through finite-horizon cutoff localization, the compact Letwin constant-8 quadratic variance bound and approximation. Supporting results include Cheeger-Buser comparisons, covariance and energy interfaces and moment-map calculus. This Palomar configuration compares two density statements. Each asserts the existence of a positive constant C that works in every dimension n >= 1 and for every measurable isotropic log-concave probability density. The pinned OpenAI statement gives Var(f) <= C * E|grad f|^2 for smooth compactly supported tests and is the statement registered in PALOMAR-2026-11-01-000014 v1. The density-coordinate formulation of Bizeul-Klartag-Lehec Theorem 1.1 applies to every locally Lipschitz f in L^2 and uses an extended nonnegative squared-gradient integral that may be infinite. The locally Lipschitz definitions and bridge are new project code, not part of the OpenAI model. No numerical final KLS constant or uncut Eldan construction is claimed.

records.name: IsotropicMetric.lintegral_exp_passageTime_le
records.entry_name: Fluctuation bounds for first-passage percolation
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of two papers of S. Armstrong and A. Bou-Rabee on the fluctuations of passage times in first-passage percolation. "Curvature and variance in lattice first-passage percolation": for independent, identically distributed edge weights on Z^d, d >= 2, whose law nu has an exponential moment and nu({0}) below the critical probability of bond percolation (Assumption (W)), and for constants delta in (0, 1], r > 0, Lambda >= 0 and lambda > 0, there are epsilon > 0 and C such that E exp(|T(0, x) - mu(x)| / (C |x|^((1 - epsilon)/2))) <= 2 for every unit vector xi in R^d, rational or not, at which the time constant mu has a quadratic expansion on the orthogonal hyperplane with these constants (Assumption (Curv): a linear term, a quadratic form at least lambda |h|^2, and a remainder at most Lambda |h|^(2 + delta) for |h| <= r), and every x in Z^d other than 0 within distance |x|^(3/4) of the ray through xi; epsilon and C do not depend on the direction (Theorem 1.1). The repository also proves the variance bound that follows, Var T(0, x) <= 2 C^2 |x|^(1 - epsilon), and Var T(0, floor(n xi)) <= n^(1 - epsilon) for every sufficiently large integer n, uniformly in the direction, the floor taken coordinatewise. "Fluctuation bounds for rotationally invariant first-passage percolation": for the random density psi(chi * W) of Gaussian white noise W on R^d, d >= 2, with chi smooth, radial and supported in the closed unit ball and psi continuous with values between two positive constants, the passage time T over rectifiable curves has a time constant mu = lim t^(-1) E T(0, t e_1), and there are epsilon > 0 and C such that E exp(|T(0, x) - mu |x|| / (C |x|^((1 - epsilon)/2))) <= 2 for every point x with |x| >= 1 (Theorem 1.1); the same holds for every density of white noise or of a homogeneous Poisson process that is jointly measurable, determined by the noise in the closed unit ball around each point, bounded between two positive constants and equivariant under rotations and translations (Assumption A, Theorem 1.2). The repository also proves the variance bounds that follow, Var T(0, t e_1) <= t^(1 - epsilon) for every sufficiently large t and Var T(0, x) <= |x|^(1 - epsilon) for every point x with |x| sufficiently large. Every result of the literature that the proofs cite is stated and proved in the repository.

"Curvature and variance in lattice first-passage percolation": for independent, identically distributed edge weights on Z^d, d >= 2, whose law nu has an exponential moment and nu({0}) below the critical probability of bond percolation (Assumption (W)), and for constants delta in (0, 1], r > 0, Lambda >= 0 and lambda > 0, there are epsilon > 0 and C such that E exp(|T(0, x) - mu(x)| / (C |x|^((1 - epsilon)/2))) <= 2 for every unit vector xi in R^d, rational or not, at which the time constant mu has a quadratic expansion on the orthogonal hyperplane with these constants (Assumption (Curv): a linear term, a quadratic form at least lambda |h|^2, and a remainder at most Lambda |h|^(2 + delta) for |h| <= r), and every x in Z^d other than 0 within distance |x|^(3/4) of the ray through xi; epsilon and C do not depend on the direction (Theorem 1.1). The repository also proves the variance bound that follows, Var T(0, x) <= 2 C^2 |x|^(1 - epsilon), and Var T(0, floor(n xi)) <= n^(1 - epsilon) for every sufficiently large integer n, uniformly in the direction, the floor taken coordinatewise. "Fluctuation bounds for rotationally invariant first-passage percolation": for the random density psi(chi * W) of Gaussian white noise W on R^d, d >= 2, with chi smooth, radial and supported in the closed unit ball and psi continuous with values between two positive constants, the passage time T over rectifiable curves has a time constant mu = lim t^(-1) E T(0, t e_1), and there are epsilon > 0 and C such that E exp(|T(0, x) - mu |x|| / (C |x|^((1 - epsilon)/2))) <= 2 for every point x with |x| >= 1 (Theorem 1.1); the same holds for every density of white noise or of a homogeneous Poisson process that is jointly measurable, determined by the noise in the closed unit ball around each point, bounded between two positive constants and equivariant under rotations and translations (Assumption A, Theorem 1.2). The repository also proves the variance bounds that follow, Var T(0, t e_1) <= t^(1 - epsilon) for every sufficiently large t and Var T(0, x) <= |x|^(1 - epsilon) for every point x with |x| sufficiently large. Every result of the literature that the proofs cite is stated and proved in the repository.

records.name: RQStatement.Palomar.theoremB
records.entry_name: Rational structures on quivers and a generalization of Gelfand's equivalence: Theorem B
records.doc: For every field E of characteristic 0 and every integer l >= 0 (lambda = l^2), the category HC_lambda(sl_2, SO(2))_E of E-rational Harish-Chandra modules for (sl_2, SO(2)) with generalized infinitesimal character lambda is equivalent to the category Rep^nil(Gamma_E) of finite-dimensional nilpotent representations of an E-rational quiver Gamma_E: the Gelfand quiver (with the relation a_- b_- = a_+ b_+) if l >= 1 and the cyclic quiver if l = 0, carrying the action of Gal(E(sqrt(-1))/E) that swaps the two outer vertices when sqrt(-1) is not in E.  For E = C this is Gelfand's classical equivalence; E = Q is Theorem A of the paper.  Harish-Chandra modules over E are modelled by Galois descent: an E-vector space M_E together with the weight decomposition and the sl_2-action on L_E (x)_E M_E, L_E = E(sqrt(-1)), and the condition that these structures are defined over E.  The compared statement asserts the existence of an equivalence; the underlying formalization proves that the paper's explicit functor E_E is one.

records.name: MacMahon.minimum_size
records.entry_name: The ten minimum universal sets of MacMahon cubes
records.doc: A universal inventory of six-coloured MacMahon cubes can build a 2 by 2 by 2 model of every target variety, using eight distinct physical copies, without requiring internal face colours to match. We prove that the minimum inventory size is twelve and classify all ten labelled inventories attaining it, even when repetitions are allowed. They are exactly the two-triangle sets in Conway's tableau. The proof derives row and column sums of two from usability inequalities, proves symmetry, and eliminates every other degree-two inventory by corner coverage. Finite kernel-checked witnesses establish sufficiency. The formalization also verifies the proper cube rotations, outward faces, and completeness and uniqueness of the thirty geometric representatives.

records.name: ErdosPaperV.lemma_3_1
records.entry_name: Colorability and realizability defects in resource-dominated packing relaxations
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main results of the author's preprint "Colorability and Realizability Defects in Resource-Dominated Packing Relaxations" (Erdős #81 series, Paper V). For a conflict system (finite objects with a symmetric irreflexive conflict relation) and a multiset X of objects, the loss between fractional and integral packings is bounded by the colourability defect D_q of the conflict graph H[X] of the copies (Lemma 3.1, Corollary 3.2, Theorems 3.3, 3.4, 3.4w), and, more generally, by the cost of a realizability certificate whose classes are realized in a fixed target system (Theorems 4.2 and 4.4). Applications: host completion through list edge colouring of bipartite multigraphs (Theorem 5.2: Galvin and Borodin–Kostochka–Woodall; Corollary 5.3; Example 5.5, a quadratic separation on K_{r,r}), the vertex-copy inequalities ν₃*(G_{v→u}) + ν₃*(G_{u→v}) ≤ 2ν₃*(G), ν₃(G_{v→u}) + ν₃(G_{u→v}) ≤ 2ν₃(G) + oct(H[T₂]) and ≤ 3ν₃(G) for triangle packings (Theorems 6.1, 6.2, Corollary 6.2a) and mixed triangle/K₄ copy inequalities (Theorem 7.3). Eighteen statements in all.

records.name: ErdosPaperIV.theorem_A
records.entry_name: Clique partitions of chordal graphs: quantitative stability and sharp eventual bounds
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the chordal results of the author's preprint "Clique partitions with rooted simplicial defect: quantitative stability and sharp eventual bounds" (Erdős #81 series, Paper IV). With M(n) = ⌊n(n+1)/6⌋: there is b such that every chordal graph on n vertices has a clique partition into pieces of order at most four with at most M(n) + b pieces (Theorem A); for n large every chordal graph on n vertices has one with at most M(n) pieces, and some chordal graph on n vertices has one with exactly M(n) pieces that is optimal among all clique partitions (Theorem B, the bound asked in Erdős Problem #81 and its sharpness); 1/6 is the least quadratic coefficient (§6.3); the uniform mixed rounding of fractional triangle/K₄ packings (Theorem 3.1); integral stability with explicit constants and edit distance at most 16δ to a complete-split graph, for 0 ≤ δ ≤ γn² with γ = 10⁻¹⁶/4 (Theorem 6.1); same-root control of near-optimal partitions: one clique root satisfies all the conclusions of Theorem 6.1 and, for it, every partition with at most M(n) + τ pieces has at most τ + 48δ noncanonical pieces (Corollary 6.1a); the root-defect identity (6.7b); and the eventual classification of the extremal chordal graphs as complete-split graphs with a core of optimal size (Corollary 6.2). Version 2 adds the fixed-defect results for graphs of rooted simplicial defect at most s: the sharp eventual bound Q_s(n) = M(n + s) − C(s + 1, 2), attained by a partition optimal among all clique partitions (Theorem C); same-root stability with A_s = 2·10⁴¹·(s + 1)⁸ for 0 ≤ δ ≤ γn², edit distance at most A_s δ, at most τ + (1 + 7A_s)δ noncanonical pieces carrying at most 10τ + 10(1 + 7A_s)δ edges (Theorem C′); comparison with an optimal-size template at distance at most A_s δ + n√((1 + 4A_s)δ) and the equality case cp = c₄ = Q_s(n) (Corollary 6.3); the necessity of the square-root term (Proposition 6.3a); the bounds F₄(G) ≤ M(n − s) + ns (minus C(s + 1, 2) when 4s ≤ n) and their integral form up to εn² (Proposition 6.4); the sublinear-defect bound n²/6 + o(n²) and root stability (Theorem 6.5); the bound Q_s(n) for all s ≤ S once n ≥ T(P(S)), an explicit tower (Corollary 6.6); and the annex inequality: a chordal K_{d+2}-free graph has fractional triangle packing number at most ν₃ + (10 + d/2)n (G.1). 21 statements. The thresholds N and γ in Theorems B, C, C′ and Corollary 6.3 are existential; b, N, A_s and the tower are not claimed optimal.

With M(n) = ⌊n(n+1)/6⌋: there is b such that every chordal graph on n vertices has a clique partition into pieces of order at most four with at most M(n) + b pieces (Theorem A); for n large every chordal graph on n vertices has one with at most M(n) pieces, and some chordal graph on n vertices has one with exactly M(n) pieces that is optimal among all clique partitions (Theorem B, the bound asked in Erdős Problem #81 and its sharpness); 1/6 is the least quadratic coefficient (§6.3); the uniform mixed rounding of fractional triangle/K₄ packings (Theorem 3.1); integral stability with explicit constants and edit distance at most 16δ to a complete-split graph, for 0 ≤ δ ≤ γn² with γ = 10⁻¹⁶/4 (Theorem 6.1); same-root control of near-optimal partitions: one clique root satisfies all the conclusions of Theorem 6.1 and, for it, every partition with at most M(n) + τ pieces has at most τ + 48δ noncanonical pieces (Corollary 6.1a); the root-defect identity (6.7b); and the eventual classification of the extremal chordal graphs as complete-split graphs with a core of optimal size (Corollary 6.2). Version 2 adds the fixed-defect results for graphs of rooted simplicial defect at most s: the sharp eventual bound Q_s(n) = M(n + s) − C(s + 1, 2), attained by a partition optimal among all clique partitions (Theorem C); same-root stability with A_s = 2·10⁴¹·(s + 1)⁸ for 0 ≤ δ ≤ γn², edit distance at most A_s δ, at most τ + (1 + 7A_s)δ noncanonical pieces carrying at most 10τ + 10(1 + 7A_s)δ edges (Theorem C′); comparison with an optimal-size template at distance at most A_s δ + n√((1 + 4A_s)δ) and the equality case cp = c₄ = Q_s(n) (Corollary 6.3); the necessity of the square-root term (Proposition 6.3a); the bounds F₄(G) ≤ M(n − s) + ns (minus C(s + 1, 2) when 4s ≤ n) and their integral form up to εn² (Proposition 6.4); the sublinear-defect bound n²/6 + o(n²) and root stability (Theorem 6.5); the bound Q_s(n) for all s ≤ S once n ≥ T(P(S)), an explicit tower (Corollary 6.6); and the annex inequality: a chordal K_{d+2}-free graph has fractional triangle packing number at most ν₃ + (10 + d/2)n (G.1). 21 statements. The thresholds N and γ in Theorems B, C, C′ and Corollary 6.3 are existential; b, N, A_s and the tower are not claimed optimal.

With M(n) = ⌊n(n+1)/6⌋: there is b such that every chordal graph on n vertices has a clique partition into pieces of order at most four with at most M(n) + b pieces (Theorem A); for n large every chordal graph on n vertices has one with at most M(n) pieces, and some chordal graph on n vertices has one with exactly M(n) pieces that is optimal among all clique partitions (Theorem B, the bound asked in Erdős Problem #81 and its sharpness); 1/6 is the least quadratic coefficient (§6.3); the uniform mixed rounding of fractional triangle/K₄ packings (Theorem 3.1); integral stability with explicit constants and edit distance at most 16δ to a complete-split graph, for 0 ≤ δ ≤ γn² with γ = 10⁻¹⁶/4 (Theorem 6.1); same-root control of near-optimal partitions: one clique root satisfies all the conclusions of Theorem 6.1 and, for it, every partition with at most M(n) + τ pieces has at most τ + 48δ noncanonical pieces (Corollary 6.1a); the root-defect identity (6.7b); and the eventual classification of the extremal chordal graphs as complete-split graphs with a core of optimal size (Corollary 6.2). Version 2 adds the fixed-defect results for graphs of rooted simplicial defect at most s: the sharp eventual bound Q_s(n) = M(n + s) − C(s + 1, 2), attained by a partition optimal among all clique partitions (Theorem C); same-root stability with A_s = 2·10⁴¹·(s + 1)⁸ for 0 ≤ δ ≤ γn², edit distance at most A_s δ, at most τ + (1 + 7A_s)δ noncanonical pieces carrying at most 10τ + 10(1 + 7A_s)δ edges (Theorem C′); comparison with an optimal-size template at distance at most A_s δ + n√((1 + 4A_s)δ) and the equality case cp = c₄ = Q_s(n) (Corollary 6.3); the necessity of the square-root term (Proposition 6.3a); the bounds F₄(G) ≤ M(n − s) + ns (minus C(s + 1, 2) when 4s ≤ n) and their integral form up to εn² (Proposition 6.4); the sublinear-defect bound n²/6 + o(n²) and root stability (Theorem 6.5); the bound Q_s(n) for all s ≤ S once n ≥ T(P(S)), an explicit tower (Corollary 6.6); and the annex inequality: a chordal K_{d+2}-free graph has fractional triangle packing number at most ν₃ + (10 + d/2)n (G.1). 21 statements. The thresholds N and γ in Theorems B, C, C′ and Corollary 6.3 are existential; b, N, A_s and the tower are not claimed optimal.

records.name: ErdosSeriesNotes.note_I_partition_of_certificate
records.entry_name: Two application notes of the Erdős #81 series: realizability transfer and exact chordal stability
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the two research notes of the author's Erdős #81 series, in one package. Note I, "From realizability certificates to the Erdős 81 bound": a realizability certificate of Paper V for an auxiliary conflict system whose target is the physical system of copies of K₃ and K₄ in G (conflict when they share an edge, gain C(|K|,2) − 1), with q ≥ 1 classes and budget q·e(G) + cost ≤ q·T + w(X), gives a clique partition of G into pieces of order at most four with at most T pieces (note_I_partition_of_certificate; no chordality); a physical packing with e(G) − g(P) ≤ T does the same (note_I_partition_of_paid_packing); with a certified fractional optimum w, the far branch (e(G) − w < n²/6 − ηn², every η > 0, large n, no chordality) and the near branch (chordal, n ≥ 4·10¹², η = 10⁻¹⁶) give partitions with at most M(n) = ⌊n(n+1)/6⌋ pieces (note_I_far_certificate, note_I_near_certificate); assembled through the transfer, every large chordal graph has such a partition (note_I_erdos81_eventual) and every chordal graph one with at most M(n) + b pieces for an absolute b (note_I_erdos81_all_orders). Note II, "Exact stability for nearly extremal chordal clique partitions": for n large, every chordal graph on n vertices with cp(G) ≤ M(n) and 2000 (M(n) − cp(G)) ≤ n has the root P = {v : n < 2 deg v}, which is a clique, with cp(G) = B(n,|P|) − A − 2m = cp_{≤4}(G), M − cp = (M − B) + A + 2m, edit distance to K_P ∨ I_O equal to A + m and at most M − cp, and (6|P| − 2n − 1)² ≤ 24(M − cp) + 25 (note_II_eventual_root_stability). Seven statements; the thresholds N and the constant b are existential.

records.name: KotzigTheorem.kotzig_borodin
records.entry_name: Kotzig's theorem on light edges of planar graphs
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Kotzig's theorem on light edges and its relatives, for finite simple graphs with the combinatorial planarity (genus-zero rotation systems) of the registered entry Kuratowski's theorem. The weight of an edge uv is deg u + deg v. A planar graph of minimum degree at least three has an edge of weight at most 13 (kotzig_borodin; the form without 3-connectivity conjectured by Erdős and proved by Borodin); a planar graph of minimum degree at least four has an edge of weight at most 11 (light_edge_minDegree_four); Kotzig's theorem (1955): a 3-connected planar graph has an edge of weight at most 13, and at most 11 if it has no vertex of degree three (kotzig); Wernicke's theorem (1904): a planar graph of minimum degree at least five has a vertex of degree five adjacent to a vertex of degree at most six (wernicke). Four statements. The proof is a discharging argument carried out directly on the rotation system, without triangulating.

records.entry_name: Kotzig's theorem on light edges of planar graphs
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Kotzig's theorem on light edges and its relatives, for finite simple graphs with the combinatorial planarity (genus-zero rotation systems) of the registered entry Kuratowski's theorem. The weight of an edge uv is deg u + deg v. A planar graph of minimum degree at least three has an edge of weight at most 13 (kotzig_borodin; the form without 3-connectivity conjectured by Erdős and proved by Borodin); a planar graph of minimum degree at least four has an edge of weight at most 11 (light_edge_minDegree_four); Kotzig's theorem (1955): a 3-connected planar graph has an edge of weight at most 13, and at most 11 if it has no vertex of degree three (kotzig); Wernicke's theorem (1904): a planar graph of minimum degree at least five has a vertex of degree five adjacent to a vertex of degree at most six (wernicke). Four statements. The proof is a discharging argument carried out directly on the rotation system, without triangulating.

records.name: BorodinTheorem.light_face
records.entry_name: Borodin's light triangles in planar graphs of minimum degree five
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Borodin's theorem on light triangles, for finite simple graphs with the combinatorial planarity (genus-zero rotation systems) of the registered entry Kuratowski's theorem. The weight of a triangle is the sum of the degrees of its vertices. Every plane map of a graph of minimum degree at least five has a face of length three of weight at most 17 (light_face), and hence a planar graph of minimum degree at least five has a triangle of weight at most 17 (light_triangle). Two statements. The proof is a discharging argument run on the rotation system, with face charges in place of an edge-maximal counterexample; the local analysis at 5-vertices (32768 configurations of neighbour degrees capped at eight and corner types) is checked by decide in the kernel.

records.name: LebesgueTheorem.light_star
records.entry_name: Light stars and paths in planar graphs of minimum degree five (Jendrol'–Madaras)
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Theorems 1, 2 and 3 of Jendrol' and Madaras (1996), for finite simple graphs with the combinatorial planarity (genus-zero rotation systems) of the registered entry Kuratowski's theorem. Every planar graph of minimum degree at least five has: a vertex X of degree five with three distinct neighbours A1, A2, A3 such that deg A1 = 5, deg A2 ≤ 6 and deg A3 ≤ 7, or deg A1 = deg A2 = deg A3 = 6 (light_star, Theorem 1; in particular a 5-vertex with three neighbours of degree at most seven, "Lebesgue's star"); a vertex of degree five with four distinct neighbours of degree at most ten (light_star4, Theorem 2); and a path on four vertices whose degrees sum to at most 23 (light_path4, Theorem 3). The proofs are discharging arguments run on the rotation system with face charges instead of triangulating or using edge-maximal counterexamples; the local analyses (32768, 16384, 32768 and 100000 configurations) and the parity of an 11-cycle are checked by decide in the kernel.

records.entry_name: Full beta lambda calculus and finite Turing machine computability
records.doc: Closed untyped de Bruijn lambda terms under full beta reachability of Church numerals compute exactly the unary partial numerical functions computed by finite three-symbol unary Turing machines. records.name: Erdos935.erdos_935.parts.ii
records.entry_name: Erdős Problem 935: powerful parts of products of consecutive integers
records.doc: For the powerful part Q_2(m) of m, this formalization proves that limsup Q_2(n(n+1)...(n+l))/n^2 is infinite for every l >= 2 (the second question of Erdős Problem 935), and at least 1 for every l >= 1 (a consequence of a result of Mahler noted by Erdős). Both use solutions of the Pell equation x^2 = 8y^2 + 1.

records.name: LeanLab.PNTPort.ExplicitPsi1.Trivial.theorem2_of_RH_hsw
records.entry_name: On the Riemann hypothesis and the difference between primes
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof of Theorems 1, 2 and 3 of A. W. Dudek, On the Riemann hypothesis and the difference between primes, Int. J. Number Theory 11, 2015, arXiv 1402.6417. Each theorem is conditional on the Riemann hypothesis, the paper's own hypothesis, stated with Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis. Theorem 2: for every real x at least 2 there is a prime in the interval from x - (4/pi) sqrt(x) log x to x. Theorem 1: there is c > 0 such that the interval from x to x + c sqrt(x) log x holds more than sqrt(x) primes for every real x at least 2. Theorem 3: for every epsilon > 0 and all large x there is a prime in the interval from x - (1 + epsilon) sqrt(x) log x to x. Each theorem also takes one cited input as an explicit hypothesis, never as an axiom: HSWN70 gZ, the zero count of Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong, arXiv 2107.06506, Corollary 1.2, for T at least 70, stated for gZ, the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function counted with multiplicity. The paper cites the zero count of Trudgian 2014 at this point, whose constant Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong report to be in error; the corrected count is used instead. The bounds of Schoenfeld 1976 for psi - theta, which the paper also cites, are not an input here: the needed estimate is proved. Dudek's Lemma 4 and the explicit formula for psi_1 are proved as well. An AI agent, Claude, wrote the Lean code, with the ported PrimeNumberTheoremAnd files credited to their authors in PORTING.md; the statements were checked against the paper by AI agents and are offered for human audit.

records.name: GoldbachLean.Chebyshev1852.Explicit.psi_ge_chebyshev30
records.entry_name: Mémoire sur les nombres premiers
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof, with no unproved steps and no hypotheses, of explicit two-sided bounds for Chebyshev's function psi from P. L. Chebyshev, Mémoire sur les nombres premiers, 1852, with Chebyshev's constant A = log 2/2 + log 3/3 + log 5/5 - log 30/30 = 0.92129.... For every natural number n at least 30, psi of n is at least A n - 5 log n + 2 log 30 - 1; for every natural number n, psi of n is at most 6A/5 n + 2 log^2 n + 160. The proof uses Chebyshev's combination of log n!, log of the factorials of n/2, n/3 and n/5, and log of the factorial of n/30, as in the paper, with error terms weaker than Chebyshev's. Mathlib has Chebyshev type bounds only with the constants log 2 and log 4. The Lean code was written by an AI agent and is offered for human audit. Goldbach's conjecture is open and is not claimed.

records.name: KomlosSzemerediThreshold.isHamiltonian_of_log_add_loglog_add
records.entry_name: The Hamiltonicity threshold of the random graph G(n, p) (Komlós–Szemerédi)
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the sharp Hamiltonicity threshold of the binomial random graph: if ω(n) → ∞, then G(n, (log n + log log n + ω(n))/n) is Hamiltonian with probability tending to 1, and G(n, (log n + log log n − ω(n))/n) is Hamiltonian with probability tending to 0 (Komlós–Szemerédi 1983; Bollobás 1984). The edge probability is clipped to [0, 1] (min 1 above, max 0 below). The statements are given in the finite product model of the registered entry PALOMAR-2026-10-28-000021 (one independent Bernoulli(p) coin per pair of distinct vertices of Fin n) and, as corollaries, for Mathlib's SimpleGraph.binomialRandom with the edge probability projected to [0, 1]. Hamiltonicity is Mathlib's SimpleGraph.IsHamiltonian.

records.name: MadarasTheorem.light_star3
records.entry_name: Light 3-stars and light pairs of faces in plane graphs of minimum face size five (Madaras)
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Theorems 1.1 and 1.3 of Madaras (2004), for finite simple graphs with the combinatorial planarity (genus-zero rotation systems) of the registered entry Kuratowski's theorem. In every plane map of a finite simple graph of minimum degree at least three whose faces all have length at least five, some vertex x of degree three has three distinct neighbours a, b, c with deg a = deg b = 3 and deg c ≤ 4 (light_star3); in particular the star K1,3 is light, with degree sum at most 13. In the same setting, some face of length five shares an edge with a face of length at most six such that all vertices of both faces have degree at most nine (light_pair; the two faces may coincide when the graph is not 2-connected). Two statements. The proof of Theorem 1.1 is a discharging argument on the rotation system with charges deg − 4 and ℓ − 4 in which every face gives each corner at a 3-vertex a weight depending only on the degrees of the two neighbours along the face, and vertices of degree at least five give 1/5 to each 3-neighbour; the local inequalities are checked by decide in the kernel. This replaces the article's transfer of charge between adjacent 3-vertices. Theorem 1.3 is proved by a second discharging with charges 2 deg − 6 and ℓ − 6: vertices give their charge to their corners, and every face gives 1/5 across each edge to an adjacent poor face (length five, all degrees at most five, at most one of degree at least four).

records.name: CliquefreeResults.weighted_existence
records.entry_name: Weighted independent sets in clique-free graphs
records.doc: A Lean formalization of a weighted independent-set existence bound for finite clique-free graphs. For every integer r at least four, positive real degree weights s, and nonnegative real objective weights a, a K_r-free graph has an independent set whose a-weight is at least c_r times the sum of a_v f(s(N(v))/s_v), where f is Shearer's function. The coefficient is the explicit positive rational c_r = 1/(1 + 1152 B_0 r), with a fixed absolute constant B_0, and has proved upper and lower bounds of order 1/r. The proof combines scalar potentials, a weighted triangle dichotomy, sparse neighborhood restriction, deletion identities, and compactness induction.

records.name: BModel.one_zero_system_exists
records.entry_name: Discrete Beurling number systems with integer error below every power, without a zero-free half-plane (assuming the short-interval prime number theorem (84))
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of S. Lavery, "Discrete Beurling number systems with integer error below every power of x and no zero-free half-plane". The headline theorem, BModel.one_zero_system_exists, constructs a discrete Beurling generalized number system whose integer counting function satisfies N(x) = x + O_ε(x^ε) for every ε > 0, while its zeta function is zero-free on no half-plane Re s > 1 − ε (a discrete [1, 0]-system in the sense of Broucke–Debruyne–Révész). The second theorem, BModel.corollary_2_2_complete, is Corollary 2.2: the answer to Question Q (must N(x) = Ax + O(x^θ) with θ < 1/2 force a zero-free half-plane?) is negative. The project also proves Theorem A for every θ ∈ (0, 1/2 − 10⁻⁴]: a system with N(x) = x + O(x^θ log* x) whose zeta function has zeros ρ_k with 1 − Re ρ_k = (log log x_k + O(1))/log x_k, i.e. at distance 1·log log x_k / log x_k from the line Re s = 1. The method is integer-first: a randomised greedy rule chooses each generalized prime so that the integer count tracks a target x + R(x) whose oscillation R plants the zeros; the main work is a positive drift for the queue of composites at every scale, using a Beurling–Saias-type resolvent bound, a local prime number theorem for the realised system and a cluster-counting theorem, with numerical certificates checked by the Lean kernel (decide +kernel). In Lean both theorems are conditional on one explicit hypothesis, BaseRange.Huxley84, eq. (84) of the paper: a short-interval prime number theorem for the rational primes (relative error ≤ (log q)⁻³ on every interval of length ≥ (2q)^{7/12} in [q, 2q], for large q). This is a known theorem (Heath-Brown 1988 with the de la Vallée Poussin error term) that is not in Mathlib; it is a hypothesis of the theorems, not an axiom. The paper and the formalization were produced with heavy AI assistance (Claude agents; the Lean development was started by Aristotle, Harmonic) and have had no human expert review.

records.name: BandParityTower.Ha_spec
records.entry_name: BandParityTower: the band-parity tower and its limit modulo eight
records.doc: For a prime p let a = v_2(p-1), m = (p-1)/2^a, H_a the subgroup of (Z/p)^x of order m and s(x) = (-1)^<x>. The development proves the tower of band-parity laws of Paper I of the author's series: the cyclotomic tower (every coordinate of the band-parity sum of the character of order 2^a is congruent modulo 4 to an explicit count), the band-parity tower f_a = sum over H_a of s(u) s(u^2) = m (mod 4) at every odd prime, the doubling count sum over 2H_a of s(u) s(2u) = 2 N_a - m, the imaginary law e_a = 2 N_a - m (mod 4) at every prime p = 1 (mod 4) with its level-3 form, the collapse e_a = +-f_a when 2 is a 2^(a-1)-th power residue, and E. Lehmer's criterion for 2 to be a 2k-th power residue. It also proves the power-map family, the companion law Re C = Im C = kappa (mod 4) at p = 1 (mod 8), and Lehmer-type invariants of the inversion map modulo 4; and, modulo 8, the joint-parity form, the dichotomy, squaring cycles and the order-three pair, the defect lemma, odd multipliers as floor sums and the fifth-interval formula linking M_H(5) to B_{1,theta_p}.

The development proves the tower of band-parity laws of Paper I of the author's series: the cyclotomic tower (every coordinate of the band-parity sum of the character of order 2^a is congruent modulo 4 to an explicit count), the band-parity tower f_a = sum over H_a of s(u) s(u^2) = m (mod 4) at every odd prime, the doubling count sum over 2H_a of s(u) s(2u) = 2 N_a - m, the imaginary law e_a = 2 N_a - m (mod 4) at every prime p = 1 (mod 4) with its level-3 form, the collapse e_a = +-f_a when 2 is a 2^(a-1)-th power residue, and E. Lehmer's criterion for 2 to be a 2k-th power residue. It also proves the power-map family, the companion law Re C = Im C = kappa (mod 4) at p = 1 (mod 8), and Lehmer-type invariants of the inversion map modulo 4; and, modulo 8, the joint-parity form, the dichotomy, squaring cycles and the order-three pair, the defect lemma, odd multipliers as floor sums and the fifth-interval formula linking M_H(5) to B_{1,theta_p}.

records.name: Erdos654.erdos_654.parts.i
records.entry_name: Erdős Problem 654: distinct distances from a point when no four points are concyclic
records.doc: Erdős asked whether, for every set of n points in the plane with no four on a circle, some point has at least (1 - o(1))n distinct distances to the other points. Feng et al. (arXiv:2601.22401; construction found by their agent Aletheia) answered no, using 4m points on the coordinate axes at powers of 2 and 3. This formalization proves the negative answer and their statement (for every m >= 10 there are 4m points, no four on a circle, each with at most 3m - 1 distinct distances to the other points), using a different set on the same axes: (±2i, 0) and (0, ±(2j - 1)) for 1 <= i, j <= m. An auxiliary lemma gives the bound for every m >= 1.

records.name: Erdos657.erdos_657.variants.straus
records.entry_name: Erdős Problem 657: Straus's observation on isosceles-free point sets with few distances
records.doc: Erdős asked whether a set of n points in the plane with no isosceles triangle must determine at least f(n)n distinct distances for some f(n) tending to infinity, and asked the same in R^k for each fixed k. Straus observed that no such bound holds uniformly in the dimension. In the form stated in formal-conjectures: for every k there are 2^k points in R^k with no isosceles triangle and at most 2^k - 1 distinct distances. This formalization proves that statement, using the points whose i-th coordinate is 0 or sqrt(2^i); the sources consulted do not record Straus's own construction.

records.name: Kac.lintegral_returnTime
records.entry_name: Kac's return-time formula for any measure-preserving map
records.doc: A machine-checked proof of Kac's return-time formula. For a measure-preserving map f and a measurable set A, the integral over A of the first return time to A equals the measure of the points whose orbit ever meets A. The return time is valued in the extended naturals, infinite for a point that never returns, and with that convention the formula holds for every measure, with no finiteness, sigma-finiteness, conservativity or ergodicity assumption. For an ergodic map of a probability space and mu(A) > 0 the integral is 1, so the mean return time to A, starting in A, is 1 / mu(A).

records.name: QuarterSumLadder.even_quartic_setting
records.entry_name: QuarterSumLadder: the quarter-sum ladder and the weight-two congruences
records.doc: For a prime p = 1 (mod 8) and a quartic character chi modulo p (even, with w = chi(2) = +-1), the development proves that the coordinates of B_(2,chi) = c0 + i c1 are integers with c0 = 4(E_1 + E_-1), c1 = 4(E_i + E_-i) and c0 + c1 = p - 1 modulo 8, and that 8 divides both exactly when w = 1, i.e. when 2 is a fourth power. A Gauss-Lehmer product argument gives the quartic Gauss lemma w = (-1)^(R_1 + R_3) for the quarter counts R_r, the parity of the four quarter counts when w = 1, and the parity of R_2 through the order of 2. For the quarter sum Omega = x + iy (2N(Omega) = h^-(K) for the imaginary cyclic quartic field K of conductor 4p, not formalized) it proves criteria in the quarter counts for 2^k | 2N(Omega), 2 <= k <= 6, a classical evaluation of the fourth, the coordinate valuation formula, a congruence modulo 16 linking c0 - c1 to x - y, and the valuation of B_(2,chi) at 1 + i on its first three cases.

records.doc: For a prime p = 1 (mod 8) and a quartic character chi modulo p (even, with w = chi(2) = +-1), the development proves that the coordinates of B_(2,chi) = c0 + i c1 are integers with c0 = 4(E_1 + E_-1), c1 = 4(E_i + E_-i) and c0 + c1 = p - 1 modulo 8, and that 8 divides both exactly when w = 1, i.e. when 2 is a fourth power. A Gauss-Lehmer product argument gives the quartic Gauss lemma w = (-1)^(R_1 + R_3) for the quarter counts R_r, the parity of the four quarter counts when w = 1, and the parity of R_2 through the order of 2. For the quarter sum Omega = x + iy (2N(Omega) = h^-(K) for the imaginary cyclic quartic field K of conductor 4p, not formalized) it proves criteria in the quarter counts for 2^k | 2N(Omega), 2 <= k <= 6, a classical evaluation of the fourth, the coordinate valuation formula, a congruence modulo 16 linking c0 - c1 to x - y, and the valuation of B_(2,chi) at 1 + i on its first three cases.

records.name: OpenQuantumProblem35.ame_7_2_not_exists
records.entry_name: Absolutely maximally entangled states of seven parties: for d >= 2, AME(7, d) exists exactly when d >= 3
records.doc: Machine-checked proofs that no absolutely maximally entangled state of seven qubits exists, and that for local dimension d >= 2 an absolutely maximally entangled state of seven parties exists exactly when d >= 3. The statements and definitions are Formal Conjectures' (Open Quantum Problem 35), copied verbatim into Challenge.lean, so this entry proves Formal Conjectures' own statements; one proof step inside the definition combineFirst is changed so that Comparator can match it, and the definition is unchanged. The proofs follow Huber, Gühne and Siewert (2017) and Shi, Zhang, Zhao and Li (2026).

records.name: Erdos393.erdos_393.variants.luca
records.entry_name: Erdős Problem 393: f(n) tends to infinity, assuming the abc conjecture
records.doc: Let f(n) be the least m >= 1 such that n! = a_1 ... a_t with a_1 < ... < a_t = a_1 + m. Assuming the abc conjecture, f(n) tends to infinity. The proof follows Luca's proof that abc implies finitely many solutions of P(x) = n!, for the polynomials prod_{i in T} (x + i): for a fixed set T of d offsets, the shift y = d a + sum(T) gives d^d prod_{i in T} (a + i) = y^d + y^k R(y) with k + deg R <= d - 2 and R(0) != 0, and abc, with rad(n!) <= 4^n, bounds y by an exponential in n, while y^d >= n!. It does not assume Luca's theorem; only the reduction from f(n) to these polynomials is specific to Problem 393.

records.name: GoldbachLean.Saouter1998.Paper.N_form
records.entry_name: Checking the odd Goldbach conjecture up to 10^20
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the mathematics of Y. Saouter, Checking the odd Goldbach conjecture up to 10^20, Math. Comp. 67, 1998, 863 to 866. Proved with no hypothesis: Lemma 1, the paper's form of Theorem 5 of Brillhart, Lehmer and Selfridge 1975, for every even F; Theorem 1, the primality criterion for N = 2^22 R + 1 below 10^20 with R odd and any base a with a^((N-1)/2) = -1 modulo N; Lemma 2 by quadratic reciprocity; Theorem 2, the case of base 5; the primality of the 100 rungs of Table 1 and of the first and last primes printed in the paper. The printed ladder constant 1258213 is a misprint for 12582913, and this repair is proved. The entry does not reverify Saouter's computation: his ladder of about 250 million rungs is checked only through its first 100 rungs. As a derived result, not a theorem of the paper, every odd number from 7 to 10^20 is a sum of three primes, conditional on one cited input taken as an explicit hypothesis, never as an axiom: EvenGoldbachUpTo of 4 * 10^18, the published computation of T. Oliveira e Silva, S. Herzog and S. Pardi, Math. Comp. 83, 2014, not proved here. That proof uses Saouter's prime ladder with 25 Proth rungs as in Helfgott and Platt, so the paper's range is reproduced by a different ladder on a much larger even input than Saouter's 4 * 10^11. Ternary Goldbach for all odd numbers is Helfgott's theorem, from his 2013 preprint, and is not formalized here. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. AI agents wrote the Lean code, which is offered for human audit.

Proved with no hypothesis: Lemma 1, the paper's form of Theorem 5 of Brillhart, Lehmer and Selfridge 1975, for every even F; Theorem 1, the primality criterion for N = 2^22 R + 1 below 10^20 with R odd and any base a with a^((N-1)/2) = -1 modulo N; Lemma 2 by quadratic reciprocity; Theorem 2, the case of base 5; the primality of the 100 rungs of Table 1 and of the first and last primes printed in the paper. The printed ladder constant 1258213 is a misprint for 12582913, and this repair is proved. The entry does not reverify Saouter's computation: his ladder of about 250 million rungs is checked only through its first 100 rungs. As a derived result, not a theorem of the paper, every odd number from 7 to 10^20 is a sum of three primes, conditional on one cited input taken as an explicit hypothesis, never as an axiom: EvenGoldbachUpTo of 4 * 10^18, the published computation of T. Oliveira e Silva, S. Herzog and S. Pardi, Math. Comp. 83, 2014, not proved here. That proof uses Saouter's prime ladder with 25 Proth rungs as in Helfgott and Platt, so the paper's range is reproduced by a different ladder on a much larger even input than Saouter's 4 * 10^11. Ternary Goldbach for all odd numbers is Helfgott's theorem, from his 2013 preprint, and is not formalized here. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. records.name: FabriciJendrolTheorem.light_path
records.entry_name: Light paths and only paths in 3-connected planar graphs (Fabrici–Jendrol')
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the two theorems of Fabrici and Jendrol' (1997), for finite simple graphs with the combinatorial planarity (genus-zero rotation systems) of the registered entry Kuratowski's theorem. Theorem 1 (light_path): a 3-connected planar graph that contains a path on k ≥ 1 vertices contains such a path whose vertices all have degree at most 5k. Theorem 2 (only_paths_light): for every connected planar graph H that is not a path (not isomorphic to pathGraph on its vertex count) and every m, there is a 3-connected planar graph containing a copy of H in which every copy of H (an injective edge-preserving map) has a vertex of degree at least m. Two statements. Theorem 1 follows the proof reproduced in the Jendrol'–Voss survey (maximal counterexample, chords at major vertices, a major vertex with at most five major neighbours). Theorem 2 uses a different construction from the article's: H is completed to an edge-maximal planar graph, whose faces are triangles, and two chains of repeated stellations are inserted in every face, so that the light vertices induce disjoint paths; the result is a plane triangulation, hence 3-connected. The extremal example for 5k is not formalized.

records.name: OpenQuantumProblem35.ame_12_5_open
records.entry_name: An absolutely maximally entangled state of twelve five-level systems: AME(12, 5) exists
records.doc: A machine-checked proof that an absolutely maximally entangled state of twelve five-level systems exists. The statement and definitions are Formal Conjectures' (Open Quantum Problem 35, `ame_12_5_open`), copied verbatim into Challenge.lean, so this entry proves Formal Conjectures' own statement; one proof step inside the definition combineFirst is changed so that Comparator can match it, and the definition is unchanged. The witness is the graph state of the AME(12, 5) graph of S. Bevins and Y. Bidav. The proof is a general graph-state criterion over ZMod 5 plus 924 kernel-checked cut certificates.

records.name: QuarticPairing.pointwise_pairing
records.entry_name: QuarticPairing: the pairing of the twists in Conjecture 1.2 of David, Dunn, Hamieh and Lin
records.doc: Conjecture 1.2 of C. David, A. Dunn, A. Hamieh and H. Lin (arXiv:2306.11875) asserts that the sums S_beta(X; l) of normalized quartic Gauss sums g(c) over primary primes c of Z[i] with N(c) <= X and c = beta (mod 4), twisted by (conj(c)/|c|)^l and weighted by the von Mangoldt function, are b_beta X^(3/4) + O(X^(1/2+eps)) with b_beta nonzero when l = 0 and O(X^(1/2+eps)) when l is nonzero. The development proves that if g(c)^2 = -kappa c/|c| for a fixed unit kappa on the support of the weight (the identity (1.2) of the same paper), then g(c) conj(c)/|c| = -kappa conj(g(c)), so S_beta(X; 1) = -kappa conj(S_beta(X; 0)), and the cases l = 0 and l = 1 of the conjecture force b_beta = 0, which the conjecture excludes; the same holds when the identity fails on an exceptional set of weight O(X^(1/2+eps)). More generally S_beta(X; 1 - l) = -kappa conj(S_beta(X; l)) for every l. The corrected conjecture, with main term -kappa conj(b_beta) X^(3/4) at l = 1, is shown equivalent under the identity to its cases l <= 0, and that main term is shown to be the only one compatible with the case l = 0. It also proves the pairing identities A(nu^3, -m) = -kappa conj A(nu, m) for the twisted moments and the fact behind the special role of order four: if |g| = 1 and g^k = xi then conj(g) = g^(k-1) conj(xi). The Gauss sum and the von Mangoldt function are abstract functions on the Gaussian integers, so no quartic residue symbol is defined.

records.name: PalomarLX.boundedRouting
records.entry_name: Exact directed L/X diameter of the symmetric group
records.doc: For every n >= 5, the directed Cayley graph of the symmetric group S_n with unit-cost generators L = (0 1 ... n-1) and X = (0 1) has diameter (3n^2 - 8n + 12)/4 for even n and (3n^2 - 8n + 9)/4 for odd n. The formalization proves matching upper and lower bounds, and the existence of a literal L/X word within the sharp bound between every ordered pair of permutations. The independent statement takes the maximum of minimum word lengths over all ordered pairs. No inverse shift is included among the unit-cost moves.

records.name: DegreeNine.hadamardInv_posSemidef_iff
records.entry_name: The Arithmetic of Time: reversible units of a degree-nine field. The units of K = LM (L, M cubic) with rank-one Hermitian symbol are exactly those of trivial relative norm to L and to M, a group of rank two, and exactly those whose Schur multipliers run both ways
records.doc: Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of ten statements. Let K be a number field of degree 9 containing a totally real cubic field L and a cubic field M with one real place. Then K = LM has signature (3, 3), and its nine embeddings are the pairs (lambda, mu). A slot assignment, fixed by a labelling of L's embeddings and a non-real embedding mu_1 of M, places the nine conjugates of x in K in a 3 x 3 Hermitian array, the symbol of x; the symbol of x^-1 is its entrywise (Hadamard) inverse. (1) For every finite index type, a positive semidefinite complex matrix with no zero entry has positive semidefinite Hadamard inverse iff it is w w* (rank one); (2) for every complex matrix with no zero entry (positive semidefiniteness not assumed), the Schur multipliers of the matrix and of its Hadamard inverse are both completely positive iff it is w w*. Statements 1-2 are supporting lemmas. (3) The setting: L and M are linearly disjoint, L M = K, and K has 3 real and 3 complex places. (4) The slot assignment exists, is a bijection Fin 3 x Fin 3 ~ (K -> C) with real diagonal and conjugate-symmetric slots, and is unique. (5) For x != 0 in K, the symbol of x is rank one iff N_{K/L}(x) and N_{K/M}(x) are one and the same positive rational number. (6) For a unit u, the symbol is rank one iff N_{K/L}(u) = N_{K/M}(u) = 1. (7) These units H are torsion-free and their logarithmic embedding spans a Z-module of rank 2, so H is isomorphic to Z^2 (the isomorphism is not itself a Lean term). (8) For a unit u, the Schur multipliers of the symbols of u and of u^-1 are both completely positive iff u is in H. (9) There is a unit of infinite order all of whose powers run both ways. (10) The degree-four contrast: in a field with two real places and one complex place, both Schur multipliers of the 2 x 2 place symbol of a unit u and of u^-1 are completely positive iff u is positive at both real places and |sigma(u)| = 1. Statements 4-6, 8 and 9 hold for every labelling and every non-real mu_1. The compositum place bookkeeping is ported, with citation, from the registered entry PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012; it is not re-proved. Application to time (no compared statement asserts it): in the arithmetic of time the tick is multiplication by a unit; if a unit acts by multiplication on a Hermitian register of its places and an admissible tick must be completely positive, then in degree four a tick u != 1 runs both ways only through a conjugate on the unit circle (Salem type); in a field such as Q(Q), Q^4 = Q + 1, the only such elements are +-1 (not proved in this entry; it follows from statement 17 of the registered entry PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012, since Q(Q) is contained in Q(rho, Q)), so there the arithmetic gives time a direction; in degree nine a rank-two group of units runs both ways, so the direction is not a property of arithmetic in general: it rests on the degree-four shape and on Q(Q) having no conjugate on the unit circle. The ticks are completely positive, not trace-non-increasing. Companion of the registered entry PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006 (the arithmetic of time), whose README Scope section is reproduced verbatim in this entry's README.

records.name: MellinDuality.multiplier_constant_half
records.entry_name: MellinDuality: Mellin duality for the band-parity companion
records.doc: For an odd prime p, an odd character chi modulo p and m >= 0, the multiplier family C(a) = sum over 0 < n < p/2 of chi(n) (-1)^(n + <a n^(2m)>) has Fourier transform over the characters 2 sum_a conj(psi)(a) C(a) = G(conj psi) G(chi psi^(2m)), with the multiplier constant G(psi) = sum_m psi(m) (-1)^m = 2 (1 - 2 psi(2)) B_(1,psi). The development proves this Mellin duality over any commutative ring, its inversion over the odd complex characters and its form bilinear in first Bernoulli numbers, the half-sum identity, the exponent family and its two collapses. At p = 5 (mod 8), for the quartic character, it proves the coset decomposition of the family, its exact sums over the cosets of the fourth powers, conjugate dynamics, the two second-moment identities, the decomposition of the second-order products of the band-parity companion by coprime pairs, and Parseval's identity for the band weight. Through the inversion and Parseval's identity over the odd characters it proves, for every a not divisible by p, the exact second moment sum over odd chi of |sum over odd psi of psi(a) (1 - 2 conj(psi)(2)) (1 - 2 chi(2) psi(2)^2) B_(1,conj psi) B_(1,chi psi^2)|^2 = ((p - 1)/2)^4.

records.doc: For an odd prime p, an odd character chi modulo p and m >= 0, the multiplier family C(a) = sum over 0 < n < p/2 of chi(n) (-1)^(n + <a n^(2m)>) has Fourier transform over the characters 2 sum_a conj(psi)(a) C(a) = G(conj psi) G(chi psi^(2m)), with the multiplier constant G(psi) = sum_m psi(m) (-1)^m = 2 (1 - 2 psi(2)) B_(1,psi). The development proves this Mellin duality over any commutative ring, its inversion over the odd complex characters and its form bilinear in first Bernoulli numbers, the half-sum identity, the exponent family and its two collapses. At p = 5 (mod 8), for the quartic character, it proves the coset decomposition of the family, its exact sums over the cosets of the fourth powers, conjugate dynamics, the two second-moment identities, the decomposition of the second-order products of the band-parity companion by coprime pairs, and Parseval's identity for the band weight. Through the inversion and Parseval's identity over the odd characters it proves, for every a not divisible by p, the exact second moment sum over odd chi of |sum over odd psi of psi(a) (1 - 2 conj(psi)(2)) (1 - 2 chi(2) psi(2)^2) B_(1,conj psi) B_(1,chi psi^2)|^2 = ((p - 1)/2)^4.

records.name: QuadraticFloorII.euler_factor
records.entry_name: QuadraticFloorII: fibre sums and quartic traces at conductor 8lp
records.doc: Sequel to QuadraticFloor. For an odd prime p, the alternating floor sums S_{A,B,C}(p) = sum over 0 <= n < p of (-1)^floor((A n^2 + B n + C)/p) with admissible (B, C) are averages of first Bernoulli numbers of the odd characters vartheta_{p,psi} = eta_p chi_{-4}^delta psi modulo 8Ap. The development proves that, weighted by psi_0(b)^2 and summed over the units b modulo A, these sums give minus the sum of B_{1,vartheta_{p,psi}} over the fibre psi^2 = psi_0^2, which is real when psi_0^4 = 1; that for a prime l = 1 (mod 4), a quartic character xi modulo l and an odd prime p != l the real part of B_{1,Theta_{l,p}}, Theta_{l,p} = vartheta_{p,xi}, and the Bernoulli number of eta_p (./l) are signed combinations of floor sums (the case l = 13 included); the Euler-factor relation B_{1,f 1_{l does not divide}}^{(ml)} = (1 - f(l)) B_{1,f}^{(m)} and the class-number shapes of the coefficients three and five; the quarter-range formula B_{1,vartheta_{p,psi}}^{(8Ap)} = -sum_{0<x<=2Ap} vartheta_{p,psi}(x); and an elementary proof that both coordinates of B_{1,Theta_{l,p}}^{(8lp)} are even integers, for every odd prime p. Every Bernoulli number is taken at a stated modulus; 8lp is the conductor of Theta_{l,p} only for p != l.

records.name: WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture84.conjecture84
records.entry_name: Written on the Wall II, Conjecture 84: tree(G) ≥ 2 rad(G) / δ(G)
records.doc: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Conjecture 84 of DeLaViña's "Written on the Wall II" (conjectures of Graffiti.pc): for every finite simple connected graph G with positive minimum degree δ(G), the maximum number of vertices of an induced subtree satisfies tree(G) ≥ 2·rad(G)/δ(G). The formal statement is the one recorded in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (WrittenOnTheWallII/GraphConjecture84.lean, theorem `conjecture84`), copied verbatim together with its definition of `largestInducedTreeSize`. The proof formalizes the argument of J. J. Gebendorfer's manuscript "Induced trees in graphs with a cut vertex" (28 October 2026): the case δ(G) ≥ 2 follows from a diametral geodesic, and the case δ(G) = 1 from the stronger theorem tree(G) ≥ 2·rad(G) for every connected graph with a cut vertex, proved by a minimal-counterexample reduction to a 2-connected core with pendant paths of equal positive length. Along the way the induced-tree consequence tree(H) ≥ 2·rad(H) − 1 of Chung's induced-path bound (Erdős–Saks–Sós 1986, Theorem 2.2) is proved, which is all the argument needs.

records.name: Erdos1033.erdos_1033
records.entry_name: Erdős Problem 1033: a butterfly blow-up beating 2(√3 - 1)
records.doc: Lean 4 / Mathlib proof that the Bollobás–Erdős question of Erdős Problem 1033 has a negative answer. For every t ≥ 1 an explicit blow-up of the butterfly graph (two triangles sharing a vertex) on n = 668t vertices has 111561t² > n²/4 edges, and every triangle has degree sum exactly 978t, while 978/668 < 2(√3 - 1). Hence it is false that every graph on n vertices with more than n²/4 edges has a triangle with degree sum at least (2(√3 - 1) - o(1))n.

records.name: Erdos654.erdos_654.variants.feng
records.entry_name: Erdős Problem 654: the Aletheia counterexample
records.doc: Lean 4 / Mathlib proof that Erdős Problem 654 has a negative answer: for every m ≥ 10 there is a set of n = 4m points in the Euclidean plane, no four on a circle, in which every point has fewer than 3n/4 distinct distances to the other points. Consequently it is false that every n-point planar set with no four concyclic points has a point with (1 - o(1))n distinct distances. The construction (Aletheia; Feng et al., arXiv:2601.22401) places the points (0, ±3^(k+1)) and (±2^(j+1), 0) on the two coordinate axes.

records.name: TypedTriangle.Vortex.main_theorem_T
records.entry_name: Triangle decompositions III: physical typed absorption and prescribed statistics
records.doc: The Lean source supplement of Paper III of the Nash-Williams series (preprint 1.0), packaged with a Mathlib-only Challenge. Theorem T: for fixed labels I, allowed label multisets F and constants alpha > 0, C >= 1, h >= 6, every labelled graph of order at least n0 that has an exact diffuse fractional triangle seed of constant C (H1), whose edge indicator lies in the integer lattice spanned by its allowed triangles (H2), with at least alpha n common neighbours labelled k for every pair of distinct vertices and every label k completing an allowed type (H3), and at least alpha n^(i-4) physical hinges of some order 6 <= i <= h for every pair of allowed triangles on a common edge (H4), has an allowed triangle decomposition. Theorem T+: for every eta > 0 and q the decomposition can moreover be chosen so that every family of at most n^q triangle tests bounded by 1, and the Pasch count, are within eta n^2 of their values under the seed. Applications: Latin squares following a bounded stochastic profile with prescribed statistics and Pasch count (Theorem 8.1), the uniform and signed rank-one profiles with their intercalate counts (Corollaries 8.2 and 8.3), two Latin squares each of which separately approximates, up to eps m^2, the same prescribed statistics and the same eight coarse-block targets (their own values need not coincide), with intercalate counts near different targets (Theorem 8.4, m divisible by four), and the balanced complete five-partite graph with parts of size 3|A| and rainbow triangles (Corollary 8.5). Seven statements. All thresholds are existential; the explicit tower bound of Section 7 is not compared.

records.name: CountingSetsWithSmallSumset.card_cliqueNum_cayleySumGraph_gt_le'
records.entry_name: Counting sets with small sumset
records.doc: Lean 4 formalization of Green's paper Counting sets with small sumset, and the clique number of random Cayley graphs. For a finite abelian group Γ, let S_k^m(Γ) be the family of the sets X in Γ with |X| = k whose restricted sumset X ∔ X = {x + y : x, y in X, x ≠ y} has m elements. The paper bounds |S_k^m(Γ)| for Γ = Z/NZ and Γ = F_2^n, through a bound for the number of Freiman isomorphism classes of sets with small restricted sumset in a vector space. It deduces that the Cayley sum graph of a random subset of Z/NZ almost surely has clique number at most 160 log_2 N, and that the Cayley graph of a random subset of F_2^n almost surely has clique number between C_1 n log_2 n and C_2 n log_2 n. The formalization proves these results with C_1 = 1/4 and C_2 = 308, both as limits and as explicit bounds on the number of exceptional sets.

records.name: Erdos338.erdos_338.variants.lowerDensity_pos
records.entry_name: Erdős Problem 338: restricted order of robust sets of positive lower density
records.doc: If A \ F is a basis for every finite set F and A has positive lower density, then A has a restricted order: every sufficiently large integer is a sum of a bounded number of distinct elements of A. This is a partial result on Erdős Problem 338 (Erdős and Graham ask whether every such A, without the density condition, has a restricted order). The proof counts pairs to show that, for every R, the numbers with at least R representations as a sum of two distinct elements of A have positive lower density, uniformly in R; uses Kneser's theorem for finite abelian groups to write all large numbers of one residue class as sums of a bounded number of such numbers; fixes the residue class with distinct elements of A; and chooses the representations greedily so that all summands are distinct.

records.name: RML.ExpSum.Weil.prime_bound
records.entry_name: Weil Bounds Toolkit

records.name: Montgomery2016.theorem_1_1
records.entry_name: Fractional clique decompositions of dense partite graphs
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main theorem of R. Montgomery, "Fractional clique decompositions of dense partite graphs" (arXiv:1603.01039; Combin. Probab. Comput. 26 (2017)): for r ≥ 3, every balanced K_r-divisible r-partite graph with parts of size n in which every vertex has at least (1 − 1/(10⁶r³))n neighbours in every other part has a fractional K_r-decomposition (Theorem 1.1); and its non-partite consequence: every graph on n vertices with minimum degree at least (1 − 1/(10⁶r³))n has a fractional K_r-decomposition. The whole proof is formalized: clique counts (Proposition 3.2, Lemma 3.3), the two gadgets (Lemmas 4.2, 4.3), the splitting lemma (Lemma 4.4), the moving lemmas (Lemmas 5.2, 5.3, 5.6) and the final averaging. Not formalized: Theorem 1.2 (integral decompositions), which also needs the fractional-to-exact transfer of Barber, Kühn, Lo, Osthus and Taylor.

records.name: Hironaka.allFundamentalTheorems_printedRange
records.entry_name: Resolution of Singularities of an Algebraic Variety Over a Field of Characteristic Zero
records.doc: Heisuke Hironaka's 1964 papers 'Resolution of singularities of an algebraic variety over a field of characteristic zero I,II' were seminal achievements in the history of algebraic geometry. They had inestimable impact on a broad range of research areas in mathematics including geometry, topology, number theory, differential equations, and mathematical physics. The achievement was recognised by a Fields medal awarded to Hironaka in 1970. The papers constitute a veritable tour de force contained in 217 densely-packed pages. The algebraic and combinatorial complexity of the papers is daunting, especially towards the later portions, and have led to a significant level of persistent incomprehension even on the part of domain experts. Because more transparent proofs of the same result appeared in the 1990s, the question of understanding the original papers in detail has become somewhat forgotten. In the associated repository, we have formalised Hironaka's argument in full, modulo results he cites. We have also compiled an erratum, and included complementary arguments for a few portions of the paper that had non-trivial gaps. In a separate publication, we will give some of the narrative background, the interesting story of the mathematical community's tortuous efforts to understand these great works. The size of the formalization has forced us to split this work over three Palomar entries, one for each comparator configuration. The related entries can be found at PALOMAR-2026-11-04-000004 and PALOMAR-2026-11-04-000012 respectively.

records.name: C4Separation.distance_separation
records.entry_name: A quantitative homotopy-interleaving gap over the cyclic-four group algebra
records.doc: Over the group algebra F2[C4] of the cyclic group of order four in characteristic two, we give an explicit five-stage real-indexed persistence diagram F of unbounded chain complexes. Its stages are shifts of the periodic free resolution of the trivial module, on half-open intervals [i, i+1), with zero diagram before time 0 and from time 5 on. We compare three distances from F to the zero diagram: the homology interleaving distance (supremum over all degrees of the interleaving distances of the F2-homology persistence modules); the interleaving distance in an arbitrary localisation of the category of whole real diagrams at the objectwise quasi-isomorphisms (the derived category of real diagrams); and the strict homotopy-interleaving distance, which allows arbitrary finite zigzags of objectwise quasi-isomorphisms of both entire diagrams, including nonzero acyclic replacements of zero. The Lean development proves d_CohI(F,0) = 1/2 < d_IHC(F,0) = 1 < 5/4 <= d_HI(F,0) <= 5/2. So the three distances are quantitatively separated by a single explicit example. The lower bound for the strict metric comes from a fourfold defining-system obstruction for the resolution. The derived upper bound comes from a natural nullhomotopy of the two-unit shift. The upper bound 5/2 for the strict metric is witnessed directly, because every five-unit shift of F vanishes.

records.name: GeneralizedKServer.TowerLowerBound.full_line_tower_lower_bound
records.entry_name: Deterministic generalized k-server: tower lower bound and strict upper bound
records.doc: For generalized k-server, each named server moves in its own metric space, a request specifies one point per space, and matching any coordinate serves the request. The development proves a height-k tower lower bound on the deterministic competitive ratio on k real lines for k at least three, allowing arbitrary additive constants. It also proves existence of a lazy deterministic algorithm on arbitrary metric spaces with arbitrary positive movement weights and prescribed initial configuration, with an explicit factor depending only on k and no additive cost or horizon input. The refined deterministic factor is at most tower(k+4) for k at least two.

records.name: LeanLab.GoldbachShort78.goldbach_short_1075
records.entry_name: Goldbach numbers in short intervals of length x^(26/1075+ε)
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof that for every ε > 0 and all large natural x there is a Goldbach number, an even sum of two primes, in the interval from x to x + 3 x^(26/1075+ε). The theorem is conditional on two cited results taken as explicit hypotheses, never as axioms, and neither is proved here: LiRow052, R. Li, arXiv 2308.04458, Theorem 2, the row θ = 0.52, primes in the intervals from n - n^(0.52+ε) to n with a lower bound of the right order, with some positive constant since the printed constant differs between versions of the paper; and LiPrintedExceptionalCount, R. Li, arXiv 2407.05651 v6, Theorem 1.1, primes in the intervals from n to n + n^(1/21.5+ε) for almost all n. The argument adapts Theorem 7.1 of arXiv 2407.05651 v6, page 27, exponent 21/860 from the 0.525 of Baker, Harman and Pintz. The exponent 26/1075 is lower by 1/4300, and the gain is only the replacement of 0.525 by Li's 0.52. Li prints this exponent himself, as Theorem 7 of arXiv 2308.04458, with no ε and no factor 3, so this is a formal check of a known result and not a new exponent. Li's later note, Primes in almost all short intervals II, claims 1/22+ε in place of 1/21.5+ε, so 26/1075 is not claimed as the best exponent. Both cited papers are used here in their arXiv preprint form. Proved with no cited input: the passage from a count of primes in the intervals below n to a count in the windows from x - 2Y to x - Y, and the combinatorial step from the two counts to a Goldbach number. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. AI agents wrote the Lean code, Claude, Codex and Gemini, as listed in PORTING.md, and it is offered for human audit.

records.name: PoissonConjecture.poisson_conjecture.variants.jacobian_implication
records.entry_name: The Jacobian conjecture in dimension 2n implies the Poisson conjecture in dimension n
records.doc: A machine-checked proof that, over a field of characteristic zero, the Jacobian conjecture in dimension 2n implies the Poisson conjecture in dimension n (K. Adjamagbo and A. van den Essen, 2007, Theorem 7). The statement and definitions are Formal Conjectures' (poisson_conjecture.variants.jacobian_implication in PoissonConjecture.lean, arXiv math/0608009), copied verbatim into Challenge.lean, so this entry proves Formal Conjectures' own statement. A Poisson endomorphism's Jacobian matrix lies in Mathlib's symplectic group, so its determinant is a unit; the Jacobian conjecture then gives a polynomial inverse.

records.name: LeanLab.Helfgott2013.U1538.lemma61_paper
records.entry_name: Helfgott's Proposition 6.2 on the ternary Goldbach minor arcs
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof of Lemma 6.1 and Proposition 6.2 of H. A. Helfgott, The ternary Goldbach conjecture is true, arXiv 1312.7748v2, Section 6.1, pages 46 to 48. Lemma 6.1 is a summation by parts bound. Proposition 6.2 turns l2 bounds on S1 over the major arcs and l-infinity bounds on S2 off them into a bound for the integral of |S1|^2 |S2| over the minor arcs, without the factor log x that a plain product of norms would lose. Lemma 6.1 is stated as in the paper. Proposition 6.2 is given in three forms: an abstract measure form with a natural upper endpoint; the arcs of display 3.5 for a finite exponential polynomial S1 and a natural upper endpoint; and absolutely summable coefficients with a real upper endpoint, over any increasing measurable family of sets. The hypotheses 6.4 and 6.5 of the Proposition stay hypotheses, as in the paper, and are not proved for any exponential sum. This is one step of Helfgott's proof. The ternary Goldbach theorem itself is not formalized here, nor is Theorem 6.3 of the paper. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. AI agents wrote the Lean code, Claude, Codex and other lab agents, as listed in PORTING.md, and it is offered for human audit.

records.name: FreezingGrowth.Paper.theorem_1_2
records.entry_name: Does freezing impede the growth of random recursive trees?
records.doc: We formalize the principal results of “Does freezing impede the growth of random recursive trees?” for uniform attachment trees with freezing. We prove uniform height lower bounds over all admissible operation sequences with n attachment steps: the height is at least e log n − 5 log log n with probability tending to one, uniformly over these sequences, and the same lower bound holds for expected height for sufficiently large n. We also formalize deletion comparisons: deleting attachment or freezing steps can increase expected height, whereas deleting the attachment–freezing pair at the first change of sign stochastically decreases height.

records.name: ConjCoord.tCoeff_check
records.entry_name: ConjCoord: a class number congruence modulo 16 for p = 5 (mod 16) and Conjecture coord of Paper V
records.doc: For primes p = 5 (mod 16), p = a^2 + b^2 with b even, the companion note proves h(-8p) = h(-4p) + 8 [b = +-6 (mod 16)] (mod 16), which settles Conjecture 5.3 of Paper V of the K Project series. The proof writes 4(h(-8p) - h(-4p)) as a combination of representation numbers of x^2 + 2y^2 + 4z^2 and x^2 + 2y^2 + 2z^2. It shows that a weight-2 form Phi built from sieved theta series vanishes modulo 256, by Sturm's theorem and a finite check below the bound 512, and reads off the coefficient at p. This development formalizes the proof with the modular input (Serre-Stark modularity and Sturm's theorem) and Gauss's three-square class number formula as explicit hypotheses. It proves the finite check by kernel computation, the iteration of Sturm's theorem, the inversion of theta(1), the bijections relating the ternary forms to sums of three squares, the uniqueness argument for p = a^2 + b^2, the congruence, Conjecture 5.3 given Paper V Theorem 5.2(iv), and the corollaries on the octant sum and with Desnoux's congruence.

The proof writes 4(h(-8p) - h(-4p)) as a combination of representation numbers of x^2 + 2y^2 + 4z^2 and x^2 + 2y^2 + 2z^2. It shows that a weight-2 form Phi built from sieved theta series vanishes modulo 256, by Sturm's theorem and a finite check below the bound 512, and reads off the coefficient at p. This development formalizes the proof with the modular input (Serre-Stark modularity and Sturm's theorem) and Gauss's three-square class number formula as explicit hypotheses. It proves the finite check by kernel computation, the iteration of Sturm's theorem, the inversion of theta(1), the bijections relating the ternary forms to sums of three squares, the uniqueness argument for p = a^2 + b^2, the congruence, Conjecture 5.3 given Paper V Theorem 5.2(iv), and the corollaries on the octant sum and with Desnoux's congruence.

records.name: KostochkaThomason.complete_minor_of_edges
records.entry_name: Complete minors and average degree (Kostochka–Thomason)
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Kostochka–Thomason theorem, following the short proof of Alon, Krivelevich and Sudakov. complete_minor_of_edges (their Theorem 1): there is d0 such that for every integer d ≥ d0, every nonempty finite simple graph with at least d·|V| edges has the complete graph K_t as a minor for every natural number t ≤ d / (10 √(ln d)). kostochka_thomason: there is a constant c > 0 such that for every integer d ≥ 2, every nonempty finite simple graph with at least d·|V| edges (average degree at least 2d) has a K_t minor for every t ≤ c·d / √(ln d). Minors are branch-set models, with the definition of the registered entry Mader's theorem and Hadwiger's conjecture for t ≤ 4, whose library is a pinned dependency. Two statements; the thresholds d0 and c are existential (the proof gives d0 = ⌈exp(R0²)⌉ + 1 with R0 ≥ 1400).

records.name: ZZN.T.solvableBT_main
records.entry_name: Two-colour Zig-Zag Numberlink on rectangles
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof that two-colour Zig-Zag Numberlink on rectangular grids (the paired 2-disjoint path cover problem: two vertex-disjoint paths s0 → t0 and s1 → t1 that together visit every cell) is decided by an explicit procedure, and that an explicit construction finds a solution whenever one exists. For both sides at least 11, an instance is solvable exactly when it passes a finite catalogue of forbidden patterns; for a side at most 10, a plug dynamic program decides it. The finite cases of the characterization are 21 boxes of slice certificates and 59 window certificates, all checked by the kernel.

records.name: FixedNumerator.ddhl_3_6
records.entry_name: FixedNumerator: the local step in extending a theorem on quartic Gauss sums over primes to a fixed numerator
records.doc: Theorem 1.1 of C. David, A. Dunn, A. Hamieh and H. Lin (arXiv:2306.11875) bounds the sums of normalized quartic Gauss sums g(c) over primary primes c of Z[i] in a class modulo 4, twisted by (c/|c|)^l. The companion note extends it to g(nu, c) with any fixed numerator nu. The only new ingredient is a local identity that splits off the primes dividing nu from the coprimality conditions of the Type I Dirichlet series. This development formalizes that step from the identities of DDHL Section 3, taken as hypotheses on an abstract symbol and Gauss sum: the splitting identity g(mu, pi^k c') = (-1)^C(c', pi^k) g(mu, pi^k) g(mu pi^(2k), c') with no condition linking mu and pi, and DDHL (3.6). It proves the identity for the truncated series as an exact finite identity (Lemma 2.2), and removes pi from the coprimality condition for every valuation e = ord_pi(mu) (Corollary 2.3): on the series prime to pi the valuation reduces modulo 4; for every e the splitting has the terms k = 4j <= e and k = e + 1; and for the four exact valuations e = 1, 3 it gives single equations with an explicit finite inverse, for e = 0, 2 the coupled pair of DDHL (8.6)-(8.7). It also proves lower bounds for the determinants on Re s >= 1 and the 2-adic facts behind the signs.

records.name: Hironaka.MainTheorem.Ch0.exists_isInvertible_subsheaf_pullback
records.entry_name: Resolution of Singularities of an Algebraic Variety Over a Field of Characteristic Zero
records.doc: Heisuke Hironaka's 1964 papers 'Resolution of singularities of an algebraic variety over a field of characteristic zero I,II' were seminal achievements in the history of algebraic geometry. They had inestimable impact on a broad range of research areas in mathematics including geometry, topology, number theory, differential equations, and mathematical physics. The achievement was recognised by a Fields medal awarded to Hironaka in 1970. The papers constitute a veritable tour de force contained in 217 densely-packed pages. The algebraic and combinatorial complexity of the papers is daunting, especially towards the later portions, and have led to a significant level of persistent incomprehension even on the part of domain experts. Because more transparent proofs of the same result appeared in the 1990s, the question of understanding the original papers in detail has become somewhat forgotten. In the associated repository, we have formalised Hironaka's argument in full, modulo results he cites. We have also compiled an erratum, and included complementary arguments for a few portions of the paper that had non-trivial gaps. In a separate publication, we will give some of the narrative background, the interesting story of the mathematical community's tortuous efforts to understand these great works. The size of the formalization has forced us to split this work over three Palomar entries, one for each comparator configuration. The related entries can be found at PALOMAR-2026-11-03-000021 and PALOMAR-2026-11-04-000012 respectively.

records.entry_name: Schatten-class truncated Toeplitz operators
records.doc: Lean formalization of Schatten-class truncated Toeplitz operator results from the local Lopatto–Rochberg manuscript. Includes analytic and coanalytic Besov classifications for every real p>0, compactness and interpolation criteria, splitting and polynomial-symbol results, and Hilbert–Schmidt energy, differential and squared-kernel quotient descriptions.

records.name: NaturalProofs.natural_proofs_barrier
records.entry_name: The natural proofs barrier (Razborov and Rudich)
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof of Theorem 4.1 of A. A. Razborov and S. Rudich, Natural proofs (1997). If a generator G_k from k bits to 2k bits, computed by circuits of polynomial size, has hardness at least 2^(k^ε) for some ε > 0 and infinitely many k, then no P/poly-natural combinatorial property is useful against P/poly. The proof follows the paper. The generator gives Goldreich–Goldwasser–Micali functions of n variables with polynomial-size circuits, which a useful property must reject. The circuit that decides the large constructive subproperty then tells these functions apart from random functions. A hybrid argument over the levels of the tree and over the nodes of a level, with all other nodes fixed, gives a circuit of size 2^O(n) that tells one output of G_k apart from a uniform string with advantage 2^(-O(n)), which contradicts the hardness for n a small power of k.

records.name: SchurWitness538.schur_six_538
records.entry_name: A Schur 6-colouring of [1, 538]
records.doc: A Lean 4 check, with Lean core only, of the existence of a colouring of the integers 1 to 538 with 6 colours and no monochromatic x + y = z, with x = y allowed. So the integers 1 to 538 are the union of six sum-free sets, which gives S(6) ≥ 538 for the Schur number S(6). The largest lower bound in the sources that the author read on 3 November 2026 is S(6) ≥ 537, by Chen, Zhu and Long. The paper paper/schur-six-538.md in this repository states the result.
