records.name: Overfull.overfull_of_critical
records.entry_name: Overfullness of critical graphs with small minimum degree (Cao–Chen–Jing–Shan; Chen–Cao)
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Theorem 1.2 of Cao, Chen, Jing and Shan with a weaker constant. overfull_of_critical: if a finite simple graph G is Δ-critical (connected, its line graph is not Δ(G)-colourable, and G − e is Δ(G)-edge-colourable for every edge e) and 3|V(G)| + 7δ(G) ≤ 4Δ(G) + 10, then G is overfull: |E(G)| > Δ(G)·⌊|V(G)|/2⌋. The article assumes 4Δ − 7δ ≥ 3n − 17; the hypothesis here is 4Δ − 7δ ≥ 3n − 10, stronger by 7, because two common-neighbour counts in the article's proof (Case 2 of Section 3 and the fork branch of Case 1) use one more unit of degree than is available and are short by 2 under the article's constant. With the constant −10 every count closes, and the proof needs neither n ≥ 13 nor the Chetwynd–Hilton theorem for Δ ≥ n − 3. One statement. The proof includes the lemmas the article imports: Vizing's adjacency lemma, the multifan lemma, Kierstead paths on four vertices, the fork lemma of Cao and Chen, the short-kite lemma of Cao, Chen and Shan, and the kite lemma (Lemma 2.8, in the form used by Theorem 1.2), with proofs written from scratch where the article only cites them. Version 2 adds two statements. overfull_of_critical_cc: Theorem 1.3 of Chen and Cao (arXiv:2512.07252) with a weaker constant: a Δ-critical graph with 2|V(G)| + 5δ(G) ≤ 3Δ(G) + 6 is overfull (the article assumes 3Δ ≥ 2n + 5δ − 12; the constant −6 comes from counting common neighbours of three vertices without the article's refinements). overfull_of_critical_ccjs: CCJS Theorem 1.2 with its original constant: a Δ-critical graph with 4Δ − 7δ ≥ 3n − 17 and n + δ ≥ 27 is overfull (then 3Δ ≥ 2n + 5δ − 6). Three statements.

records.name: OSReconstructionAudit.e_to_r
records.entry_name: OSreconstruction
records.doc: A machine-checked proof of the Osterwalder-Schrader correspondence between Euclidean Schwinger functions and relativistic Wightman distributions, in both directions, for every spatial dimension d >= 1. The Euclidean side is a family of Schwinger functions on the zero-diagonal Schwartz space (OS II's test space) satisfying E0-E4; the relativistic side is a family of tempered distributions satisfying the Wightman function axioms (Poincare covariance, spectrum condition, locality, positivity, Hermiticity, clustering). They are linked by a Wick pairing: one holomorphic kernel on the forward tube whose boundary values give the Wightman distribution and whose restriction to Wick- rotated points gives the Schwinger function. Three theorems are verified: E'->R (OS axioms plus linear growth yield Wick-paired Wightman distributions); E'->R' in OS II's form (with growth E0' (4.1), the Wightman distributions exist, satisfy the output bound R0' (4.3), and are unique among Wick-paired families; the two growth conditions are proved equivalent); and R->E (every Wightman family yields, via an explicit constructor, Schwinger functions satisfying E0-E4, with no growth hypothesis). The asymmetry is OS II's correction of OS I and is reproduced faithfully: growth is assumed on the Euclidean side and not recovered, so the two directions do not compose to a biconditional. Scope: theorems about Wightman functions, not the GNS reconstruction of operators. Four conventions are weaker than the textbook ones and are visible in the Challenge: the forward tube carries the extra condition Im z_0 in the open forward cone; locality is stated for adjacent transpositions; reflection positivity goes through a totalized coercion onto zero-diagonal tests; growth is a hypothesis, not a conclusion. To our knowledge this is the first machine-checked proof of the OS reconstruction theorem; its audience is constructive and axiomatic QFT, where it is the bridge every Euclidean construction crosses. The companion formalization of the massive free field and the Proca Wick square inhabits its hypotheses.

records.name: ElboimSly.Challenge.existsUnique_trajectories
records.entry_name: Infinite cycles in the interchange process in five dimensions (Elboim-Sly), formalized in Lean 4
records.doc: A complete Lean 4 formalization of D. Elboim and A. Sly, Infinite cycles in the interchange process in five dimensions (arXiv:2211.17023v3). In the interchange process on Z^d, each edge carries an independent rate-one Poisson clock and swaps the particles at its endpoints when it rings; run for time beta, it yields a random permutation pi_beta of Z^d. Toth conjectured that pi_beta has infinite cycles for d >= 3 and beta large; Elboim and Sly proved this for d >= 5. The library proves their Theorem 1 (for d >= 5 and beta large, pi_beta almost surely has an infinite cycle), the quantitative bound from its proof (the cycle of the origin is finite with probability less than 2/beta), and the multiscale induction behind both, Theorem 3.2, whose hypotheses (H1)-(H5) control relaxed times, local probabilities, displacement, a Brownian coupling and the proximity of two walks for the cyclic random walk at every scale. The model is constructed on the infinite lattice (Poisson clocks, existence and uniqueness of particle trajectories, bijectivity of pi_s), and nothing the paper cites is assumed: Poisson point processes and their exploration, the zero-one law, continuous-time random walk estimates, Brownian motion and its hitting and escape estimates, Freedman's inequality and the strong approximations are proved from Mathlib. Zaitsev's multidimensional KMT theorem, the paper's one external input, is replaced by two couplings proved in the library: a KMT coupling for Poisson increments and a strong approximation for bounded sign-symmetric vectors; the exponent of the Brownian coupling in (H4) becomes 41/100 instead of 2/5, and Theorem 1 is unchanged. Every statement is checked against a Mathlib-only restatement with leanprover/comparator, and the library uses only Lean's standard axioms.

records.name: Hironaka.MainTheorem.Ch0.I
records.entry_name: Resolution of Singularities of an Algebraic Variety Over a Field of Characteristic Zero
records.doc: Heisuke Hironaka's 1964 papers 'Resolution of singularities of an algebraic variety over a field of characteristic zero I,II' were seminal achievements in the history of algebraic geometry. They had inestimable impact on a broad range of research areas in mathematics including geometry, topology, number theory, differential equations, and mathematical physics. The achievement was recognised by a Fields medal awarded to Hironaka in 1970. The papers constitute a veritable tour de force contained in 217 densely-packed pages. The algebraic and combinatorial complexity of the papers is daunting, especially towards the later portions, and have led to a significant level of persistent incomprehension even on the part of domain experts. Because more transparent proofs of the same result appeared in the 1990s, the question of understanding the original papers in detail has become somewhat forgotten. In the associated repository, we have formalised Hironaka's argument in full, modulo results he cites. We have also compiled an erratum, and included complementary arguments for a few portions of the paper that had non-trivial gaps. In a separate publication, we will give some of the narrative background, the interesting story of the mathematical community's tortuous efforts to understand these great works. The size of the formalization has forced us to split this work over three Palomar entries, one for each comparator configuration. The related entries can be found at PALOMAR-2026-11-03-000021 and PALOMAR-2026-11-04-000004 respectively.

The algebraic and combinatorial complexity of the papers is daunting, especially towards the later portions, and have led to a significant level of persistent incomprehension even on the part of domain experts. Because more transparent proofs of the same result appeared in the 1990s, the question of understanding the original papers in detail has become somewhat forgotten. In the associated repository, we have formalised Hironaka's argument in full, modulo results he cites. We have also compiled an erratum, and included complementary arguments for a few portions of the paper that had non-trivial gaps. In a separate publication, we will give some of the narrative background, the interesting story of the mathematical community's tortuous efforts to understand these great works. The size of the formalization has forced us to split this work over three Palomar entries, one for each comparator configuration. The related entries can be found at PALOMAR-2026-11-03-000021 and PALOMAR-2026-11-04-000004 respectively.

records.name: ThresholdChallenge.main
records.entry_name: Existence of the q-colorability threshold for sparse random graphs
records.doc: For every integer q at least 3, the formalization proves the existence of a limiting q-colorability threshold for sparse random graphs. A single constant alpha_q in [1/2, log(q)/log(q/(q-1))] gives the transition for the uniform model with floor(c n) edges and the transition at d = 2 alpha_q for the binomial model with edge probability d/n. For every fixed eta in (0,1), there is C > 0 such that, for all sufficiently large n, the first loss of q-colorability under independent uniform additions of unordered pairs of distinct vertices lies within C n (log n)^(-3/2) steps of deterministic integer centers with probability at least 1-eta. The centers divided by n converge to the same alpha_q. Repeated edges are retained in this process. The scope is Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 of the included manuscript.

records.name: CDR.bicolourable3_mul
records.entry_name: Bicolouring Steiner triple systems (Colbourn–Dinitz–Rosa product, Dinitz–Stinson conditions)
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the product theorem of Colbourn, Dinitz and Rosa for bicoloured Steiner triple systems and of the necessary conditions of Dinitz and Stinson. A bicolouring of an STS colours the points so that every block receives exactly two colours. bicolourable3_mul (CDR 1999, Theorem 2.4): if there is an (a, b, c)-bicolourable STS(u) with c = max(a, b, c) and c ≤ a + b, and an (x, y, z)-bicolourable STS(v), then there is an (ax + by + cz, ay + bz + cx, az + bx + cy)-bicolourable STS(uv). Dinitz–Stinson Proposition 1.2: for a bicoloured STS on v points with colour classes of sizes c_k, 3 Σ c_k (c_k − 1) = v (v − 1) (IsSTS.three_mul_sum); no two distinct colour classes have size 2 (not_two_classes_of_size_two); and with three colour classes at most one class size is odd (Bicolourable3.not_two_odd). Four statements. The proof of Theorem 2.4 includes Lemma 2.3 of the article (forbidden latin squares exist when max(a, b, c) ≤ n/2), Ryser's theorem on completing latin arrays, and de Werra's equalized edge colourings of bipartite graphs.

records.name: CayleyErdősGyárfás.odd_order_cayley_contains_two_power_cycle
records.entry_name: Odd-ordered Cayley graphs satisfy Erdős–Gyárfás
records.doc: Every Cayley graph of a finite group of odd order with an inverse-closed, identity-free generating set of size at least three contains a simple cycle of length 2^n for some n ≥ 2. For a noncyclic group of odd order, two such cycles can be chosen as translates meeting at exactly one vertex. A symmetric figure-eight lifts through an abelian normal subgroup of an odd-order group, and a power-of-two cycle lifts through a normal 2-subgroup of a finite group. The cycle conclusion also holds for finite nilpotent groups with a generating set satisfying the same degree condition.

records.name: Plantholt.theorem_1_2
records.entry_name: Plantholt's overfull criterion for graphs of high minimum degree, with 1-factorization theorems for dense regular graphs (6/7 and 11/12)
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Theorem 1.2 of M. Plantholt, Overfull conjecture for graphs with high minimum degree (J. Graph Theory 47, 2004), and of a 1-factorization theorem for dense regular graphs in the style of Chetwynd and Hilton (1989). theorem_1_2: if c ≥ 3/4 is such that every regular graph of even order n and degree at least c n is 1-factorizable, and G has even order n with (3δ − Δ)/2 ≥ c n, then G is Class 1 (χ′ = Δ) if and only if G has no Δ-overfull subgraph. lineGraph_colorable_of_isRegular: a d-regular graph of even order 2n with 11 n ≤ 6 d is d-edge-colourable, i.e. 1-factorizable; this is a weaker form of Chetwynd–Hilton 1989, Theorem 2 (d ≥ ½(√7 − 1)|V|), proved with the same architecture. overfull_criterion: Plantholt's theorem with c = 11/12, i.e. if G has even order n and 11 n ≤ 6 (3δ − Δ), then G is Class 1 if and only if it has no Δ-overfull subgraph. lineGraph_colorable_of_isRegular67: the theorem of Chetwynd and Hilton (Proc. London Math. Soc. 50, 1985) that a d-regular graph of even order 2n with 12 n ≤ 7 d (degree at least 6/7 of the order) is 1-factorizable. overfull_criterion67: Plantholt's theorem with c = 6/7, i.e. even order n and 12 n ≤ 7 (3δ − Δ). Five statements. A Δ-overfull subgraph has an odd number ≥ 3 of vertices and more than Δ ⌊|V(H)|/2⌋ edges; edge colourings are colourings of the line graph.

records.name: Balanced.exists_equitable_strong
records.entry_name: Equitable strong (vertex-distinguishing) edge colourings: Rudašová–Soták, Theorem 3.1
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Theorem 3.1 of J. Rudašová and R. Soták, Vertex-distinguishing proper edge colourings of some regular graphs (Discrete Math. 308, 2008). exists_equitable_strong: if a finite simple graph G has a strong (vertex-distinguishing) proper edge colouring with m colours and m ≤ k, then G has an equitable strong proper edge colouring with k colours. One statement. Edge colourings are colourings of the line graph; the palette of a vertex is the set of colours of its edges; strong means distinct vertices have distinct palettes; equitable means the colour classes differ in size by at most one.

records.name: AVRegularityChallenge.interior_regularity
records.entry_name: Anomalous regularization of passive scalars up to the Obukhov–Corrsin exponent
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of S. Armstrong and V. Vicol, "Anomalous regularization of passive scalars up to the Obukhov–Corrsin exponent" (2026, included as doc/paper.pdf). The velocity field b is constructed as in Armstrong and Vicol, "Anomalous diffusion by fractal homogenization": a bounded, Z^2-periodic, divergence-free field on R x T^2, built from shear flows alternating in direction at infinitely many scales, Hölder continuous in space and time with exponent alpha < 1/3, with its scale separation parameter q taken close to 1 depending on s. For the advection-diffusion equation d_t theta + b . grad theta = kappa Laplacian theta on T^2 and every s < (1 - alpha)/2, with b built for that s, it proves: the solutions are bounded at positive times in C^{0,s}(T^2) by C times the L^2 norm of the initial datum, uniformly in kappa in a union of bands accumulating at zero (Theorem A); every solution dissipates a fixed fraction of its variance in unit time, and the variance decays exponentially, with constants independent of kappa in the bands, of the L^2 datum and of the initial time (Theorem B); the local form of Theorem A in space-time tubes that follow the flow of the coarse velocity fields, without boundary conditions (Theorem C); and the compactness of the solutions as kappa tends to zero in the bands, with limits that solve the transport equation and satisfy the bounds of Theorems A and C (Corollary D). It also contains every statement of Part I of the paper.

records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of S. Armstrong and V. Vicol, "Anomalous regularization of passive scalars up to the Obukhov–Corrsin exponent" (2026, included as doc/paper.pdf). The velocity field b is constructed as in Armstrong and Vicol, "Anomalous diffusion by fractal homogenization": a bounded, Z^2-periodic, divergence-free field on R x T^2, built from shear flows alternating in direction at infinitely many scales, Hölder continuous in space and time with exponent alpha < 1/3, with its scale separation parameter q taken close to 1 depending on s. For the advection-diffusion equation d_t theta + b . grad theta = kappa Laplacian theta on T^2 and every s < (1 - alpha)/2, with b built for that s, it proves: the solutions are bounded at positive times in C^{0,s}(T^2) by C times the L^2 norm of the initial datum, uniformly in kappa in a union of bands accumulating at zero (Theorem A); every solution dissipates a fixed fraction of its variance in unit time, and the variance decays exponentially, with constants independent of kappa in the bands, of the L^2 datum and of the initial time (Theorem B); the local form of Theorem A in space-time tubes that follow the flow of the coarse velocity fields, without boundary conditions (Theorem C); and the compactness of the solutions as kappa tends to zero in the bands, with limits that solve the transport equation and satisfy the bounds of Theorems A and C (Corollary D). It also contains every statement of Part I of the paper.

records.name: BklsPalomar.theorem1
records.entry_name: Balanced edge colourings: Balister–Kostochka–Li–Schelp 2004, Theorems 1, 6, 10(2) and Corollary 12
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of four results of P. N. Balister, A. V. Kostochka, H. Li and R. H. Schelp, Balanced edge colorings (J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 90, 2004). Edge colourings with k colours are colourings of the line graph with Fin k; the palette of a vertex is the set of colours of its edges; numPal C S counts the vertices with palette S and cost C is the sum of the squares of these counts. theorem1 (Theorem 1): in a k-colouring of least cost, palettes of the same size are used numbers of times differing by at most two. theorem6 (Theorem 6): a proper 3-colouring of the edges (a map Sym2 V → Fin 3 proper at every vertex) can be replaced by a proper 4-colouring in which distinct vertices with the same key see different colour sets, when two distinct vertices with equal key, degree and colour set have degree 3 and no three distinct vertices of degree 3 share a key. theorem10 (Theorem 10, part 2): if 3 ≤ k, Δ(G) ≤ k, n_0, n_1, n_2 ≤ 1, n_3, n_4, n_k ≤ 2, n_{k-1} ≤ k + 1 and n_d ≤ (d-4)/(d-3) · min(2 C(k-3, d-3), C(k, d)) - 2 for 5 ≤ d ≤ k - 2 (n_d the number of vertices of degree d), then G has a strong (vertex-distinguishing) edge colouring with k + 1 colours. corollary12 (Corollary 12): if Δ(G) ≥ √(2n) + 4 (n vertices), δ(G) ≥ 5 and k is least with n_d ≤ C(k, d) for all d, then G has a strong edge colouring with k + 1 colours and every strong edge colouring uses at least k colours. Four statements.

records.name: BaranyaiTheorem.rounding
records.entry_name: Baranyai's theorem
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Baranyai's theorem: if k divides n, the k-subsets of an n-set can be partitioned into (n−1 choose k−1) parallel classes, each a partition of the set into n/k blocks of size k (a 1-factorization of the complete k-uniform hypergraph); and of Baranyai's rounding lemma: every real matrix can be rounded entrywise to floors or ceilings so that all row sums, column sums and the total are also rounded. The proof includes the integral max-flow theorem for integer capacities. Mathlib has neither result.

records.entry_name: Finite-order exponential mixing does not imply the central limit theorem
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of Theorems A, B, and C of the paper. It constructs stationary processes with finite-order exponential mixing and no Gaussian subsequential limit, then realizes the phenomenon in analytic and smooth dynamical systems.

records.name: SettlingSum.plastic_settling_sum
records.entry_name: The settling sum of the plastic number: sum_{n >= 1} ||rho^n||^2 = rho. The squared distances from the powers of the plastic number to the nearest integers sum to the plastic number itself; the even-power trace of its two hidden conjugates is rho; with the general cubic complex-pair form
records.doc: Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of six statements. Write ||x|| = |x - round x| for the distance from a real number to the nearest integer, and let rho be the plastic number, the real root of x^3 = x + 1 and the smallest Pisot number (Siegel 1944). Convergence of sum_{n >= 1} ||theta^n||^2 for a Pisot number theta is elementary, and Pisot (1938) proved the converse; neither gives the value. (1) For every real rho with rho^3 = rho + 1, sum_{n >= 1} ||rho^n||^2 = rho (as a HasSum). (2) The tsum form of (1). (3) For every complex alpha != rho with alpha^3 = alpha + 1 (one of the two conjugates inside the unit disc), sum_{n >= 0} (alpha^(2n) + conj(alpha)^(2n)) = rho: the even-power trace of the hidden pair is the generator, the mechanism behind (1), because x^3 - x - 1 = (x - 1) x (x + 1) - 1 makes the resolvent trace sum_{roots} 1/(1 - r^2) vanish. (4) For a real theta, a complex alpha with ||alpha|| < 1, and integers a, b, c that are the elementary symmetric functions of (theta, alpha, conj alpha): sum_{n >= 1} (S_n - theta^n)^2 = Re(geo alpha), where S_n are the Newton power sums of x^3 - a x^2 + b x - c and geo alpha = alpha^2/(1 - alpha^2) + conj(alpha)^2/(1 - conj(alpha)^2) + 2 alpha conj(alpha)/(1 - alpha conj(alpha)). (5) Under the same hypotheses, for every N with ||alpha||^N < 1/4, sum_{n >= 1} ||theta^n||^2 = Re(geo alpha) + sum_{n = 1}^{N} (||theta^n||^2 - (S_n - theta^n)^2): Pisot's convergence in quantitative form for the cubic complex-pair case; (1) is the case a = 0, b = -1, c = 1, N = 10 (the smallest N with rho^(-N/2) < 1/4; the n = 10 correction term is zero), with Re(geo alpha) = 2 rho^2 + 3 rho - 2 and correction 2 - 2 rho - 2 rho^2. (6) x^3 = x + 1 has exactly one real solution. Statements 4-5 assume neither theta > 1 nor irreducibility. Pisot's theorem itself is not formalized. Not compared, proved in the repository's library only: the threshold from which the Perrin numbers are the nearest integers to rho^n (n >= 10, sharp at n = 9), a claim previously stated without proof at OEIS A001608 (R. Stephan, 2002); it was a compared statement in the withdrawn submissions of 2026-11-03/04 and was removed from the compared set on 2026-11-05 so that every compared result is one first presented here. Application to time (no compared statement asserts it): in the arithmetic of time the tick is multiplication by rho on Q(rho) and the record is the integer lattice; statement 1 says the total squared distance by which the tick history falls short of its record is exactly one tick's unit, rho, and statement 3 says that unit is returned by the two conjugates that are not seen; the quartic companion Q, Q^4 = Q + 1, is not Pisot, so by Pisot's theorem its series diverges (not proved here). That physical time is this arithmetic is the identification stated in the companion entry PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006 (the arithmetic of time), as an identification; the theorems here are its arithmetic content. That entry's README Scope section is reproduced verbatim in this entry's README.

records.name: SimpleGraph.strong_perfect_graph_theorem
records.entry_name: The Strong Perfect Graph Theorem
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof of the Strong Perfect Graph Theorem of Chudnovsky, Robertson, Seymour and Thomas: a finite graph is perfect if and only if it is Berge. A graph is perfect if every induced subgraph has chromatic number equal to its clique number. It is Berge if neither the graph nor its complement contains an induced cycle of odd length at least five. The proof follows the paper of Chudnovsky, Robertson, Seymour and Thomas (Annals of Mathematics, 2006). It formalizes the decomposition theorem for Berge graphs (Theorem 1.3 of the paper) through the numbered results of Sections 2 to 24. It also proves the earlier results that the paper cites, among them Lovász's weak perfect graph theorem, the results of Cornuéjols and Cunningham on 2-joins, of Chvátal and Sbihi on homogeneous pairs, of Chvátal on star cutsets, and of Roussel and Rubio. The statement in Challenge.lean uses only Mathlib's definitions of induced subgraphs, chromatic number, clique number, cycle graphs and induced containment.

records.name: MaxModulusPoints.Blueprint.main
records.entry_name: Maximum-modulus points of entire functions (Erdős Problem 1117), in Lean 4
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of both maximum-modulus counting questions of Hayman–Lingham Problem 2.16 (Erdős Problem 1117). For an entire function f and a radius r, let ν(f, r) be the number of points on the circle |z| = r where |f| attains its maximum on that circle. The registered theorem proves two things: some non-monomial entire function has ν(f, r) unbounded along radii tending to infinity; and for every non-monomial entire function there is one finite bound B with ν(f, r) ≤ B along a cofinal set of radii, so the counts never tend to infinity. The first part follows Pardo-Simón and Sixsmith's finite-order construction and proves the approximation step of Rempe-Gillen that it uses; the second follows Li's cofinal-bound argument. The theorem depends only on the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.name: DixmierConjecture.dixmier_conjecture
records.entry_name: The Dixmier conjecture implies the Jacobian conjecture, and is false in dimension 3 and above
records.doc: A machine-checked proof that, over a field of characteristic zero, the Dixmier conjecture in dimension n implies the Jacobian conjecture in dimension n (Bass, Connell and Wright, 1982), and so, with an explicit counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture padded to every dimension n >= 3 and proved here, that the Dixmier conjecture is false in every dimension n >= 3. The four statements and their definitions are Formal Conjectures' (DixmierConjecture.lean, arXiv math/0608009), copied verbatim into Challenge.lean, so this entry proves Formal Conjectures' own statements. The proof builds the polynomial representation of the Weyl algebra, shows it faithful in characteristic zero, and uses the classical Weyl-algebra lift described by Bass, Connell and Wright (1982, p. 297), who credit Vaserstein and Kac.

records.name: LargeIndecomposable.Challenge.theoremA
records.entry_name: Representation embeddings and the third Brauer–Thrall conjecture
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization, built on Mathlib, of the principal results of the paper Representation embeddings and the third Brauer–Thrall conjecture. Over an algebraically closed field, every representation-infinite finite-dimensional algebra admits a faithful representation embedding of a colimit-closed category of Kronecker modules that preserves infinite dimensions (Theorem A). Hence, for every infinite cardinal κ, it has 2^κ pairwise non-isomorphic indecomposable modules of dimension κ whose endomorphism rings are local with residue field k and whose radicals satisfy (rad End M)^n = 0 for one n ≤ max(30, 4 dim A) independent of κ; for κ ≥ |k| this is the largest possible number (Corollary 1.1, in full). Weaker parts of the corollary are also compared: modules of every infinite dimension, the endomorphism control without the count and the bound, and the count without the bound. The cited inputs are proved in the library: Bongartz's Theorem 6 and Göbel and Simson's rigid families over infinite fields.

records.name: CollisionIdeals.Palomar.PaperOne.genericDegreeThreeS3Collision
records.entry_name: Generic Degree Three in JC(3): Collision Geometry and Galois Group S3
records.doc: Motivated by Alpöge's generic-degree-three counterexample to JC(3), we formalize the collision geometry of complex three-dimensional Keller maps of that degree. Using classical Keller–Galois rigidity, we identify the residual generic collision factor with the normal closure of the induced function-field extension, whose Galois group is S3. The decomposition separates the diagonal and proves nonvanishing of the collision obstruction.

records.name: KeevashCounting.typical_triangle_decomposition
records.entry_name: Triangle decompositions of typical graphs of fixed density (Keevash, Counting designs, Theorem 2.1, weaker form)
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of a weaker, fixed-density form of Theorem 2.1 of P. Keevash, Counting designs (J. Eur. Math. Soc. 20, 2018). density G is |E(G)| / C(n, 2); IsTypical G c h says that every nonempty set S of at most h vertices has (1 ± |S| c) d(G)^|S| n common neighbours; Tridivisible G says that every degree is even and 3 divides |E(G)|; IsTriangleDecomposition G D says that D is a family of triangles of G and every edge lies in exactly one of them. typical_triangle_decomposition: there is h such that for every d0 > 0 there are c0 > 0 and n0 such that every (c0, h)-typical tridivisible graph on n ≥ n0 vertices with density at least d0 has a triangle decomposition. This is weaker than the article in two ways: the density is bounded below by a fixed constant (the article allows d(G) > n^(-10^-7) with c < c0 d(G)^(10^6)), and the typicality is (c, h)-typicality for an absolute, not explicit, h (the article assumes c-typicality, which concerns only degrees and pairs). One statement.

records.name: SpectralGeometry.AmmannBeenker.admitted_zero
records.entry_name: Spectral Geometry — exact multiplicity of a compact crossing on an infinite octagonal graph
records.doc: On the real square-summable states of the infinite centered octagonal cut-and-project vertex graph, take the graph Laplacian with edge weight 1/16, onsite potential V(x)=1+|p(x)|² and natural domain D(V). Add t times the coordinate projection onto the eight neighbors of the origin. At t*=17/16+√2 the two alternating ring modes meet at E*=13/4+√2. The full eigenspace at E* has real dimension exactly two. Every solution of the eigenvector equation is its amplitude at the lift (1,0,0,0) times the first compact state plus its amplitude at (1,1,0,0) times the second. No support restriction is assumed. Locality, symmetry and a strictly positive exterior energy force the exterior part to vanish; the complete central kernel supplies the two ring patterns.

Every solution of the eigenvector equation is its amplitude at the lift (1,0,0,0) times the first compact state plus its amplitude at (1,1,0,0) times the second. No support restriction is assumed. Locality, symmetry and a strictly positive exterior energy force the exterior part to vanish; the complete central kernel supplies the two ring patterns.

records.name: Erdos835.indepNum_johnson_le_johnsonBound
records.entry_name: The Johnson bound for the independence number of the Johnson graph
records.doc: The Johnson graph J(n, k) has the k-subsets of an n-set as vertices, two of them adjacent when they share k - 1 elements; an independent set is a constant-weight binary code of length n, weight k and minimum distance 4. This Lean 4 formalization proves Johnson's 1962 bound α(J(n, k)) ≤ johnsonBound n 4 k, where johnsonBound is the recursive bound A(n, d, w) ≤ ⌊n/w · A(n - 1, d, w - 1)⌋, as stated in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (Erdős Problem 835), where it is a solved statement left without proof. The proof is by recursion on (n, k): double counting the pairs (point, member) and shortening the members through a point. No new mathematics is claimed.

records.name: RestrictedPolynomials.main_theorem
records.entry_name: Reasonable bounds for restricted polynomial progressions in F_p^n
records.doc: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Theorem 1.1 of Burgin, Fragkos, Kruzel, Lacey and Stokolosa (arXiv:2610.12831). For k ≥ 2 there are M_k ≤ exp(7 k log k) and P_k ≤ exp exp(25 k² log k), and an absolute constant C₁, such that for every prime p ≥ P_k there are C, c > 0 with the following property. Every A ⊆ F_p^n with n > exp^{(K)}(1) and density at least C / (log^{(K)} n)^c, where K = k^{C₁ k}, contains a restricted polynomial progression x, x + P_1(y), …, x + P_{k-1}(y), with P_j(y) = (y_1^j, …, y_n^j) and y ∈ {0, 2, 3, …, M_k}^n \ {0}. Moreover, the k points of any such progression are pairwise distinct. The formalization also proves the two theorems that the paper cites from the literature and does not prove. The first is the inverse theorem of Bhangale, Khot, Liu and Minzer for noise stability under distributions with no abelian embedding (Theorem 1.4 of the paper, which is Theorem 1 of their "On approximability of satisfiable k-CSPs: VII"), in full generality. The second is Dimitrov's theorem on the Schinzel–Zassenhaus conjecture (Theorem 5.11 of the paper). Only Lean's standard axioms are used.

records.name: GaleHoffman.feasibility
records.entry_name: Gale's feasibility theorem, the Gale–Ryser theorem and Hoffman's circulation theorem
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of D. Gale, A theorem on flows in networks (Pacific J. Math. 7, 1957) and of Hoffman's circulation theorem (A. J. Hoffman, 1960, in the form of A. Schrijver, A Course in Combinatorial Optimization, Theorems 4.6 and 4.7). A network is a finite node type N with capacities c : N → N → ℝ, c ≥ 0 (finite capacities only); a flow is f : N → N → ℝ with f x y + f y x = 0 and f ≤ c; a demand d : N → ℝ is feasible if some flow has net inflow ∑_y f y x ≥ d x at every node. feasibility: d is feasible if and only if d(Sᶜ) ≤ c(S, Sᶜ) for every S ⊆ N (Gale's Feasibility Theorem). feasibility_int: the same for integer c and d with an integer flow (Gale's remark). feasibility_second: Gale's second formulation (for every set Y of nodes of positive demand, some flow meets the demand at all nodes of nonpositive demand and the aggregate demand of Y). gale_ryser_unsorted, gale_ryser: for a : Fin m → ℕ and b : Fin n → ℕ, a 0-1 matrix with row sums at most a i and column sums b j exists if and only if ∑_{j∈Y} b j ≤ ∑_i min(a i, |Y|) for all column sets Y, equivalently, for b nonincreasing, ∑_{j<k} b j ≤ ∑_{j<k} #{i | j < a i} for all k ≤ n (Gale's Problem I, §3). gale_ryser_exact: if moreover ∑ a = ∑ b, the row sums can be made exactly a (the Gale–Ryser theorem). hoffman, hoffman_int: on a finite directed multigraph (arc type A, tail and head maps src, tgt : A → V) with bounds d ≤ c on the arcs (real, respectively integer), there is a circulation f (real, respectively integer) with d ≤ f ≤ c if and only if d(δ^in(U)) ≤ c(δ^out(U)) for every U ⊆ V. Eight statements; no definitions beyond Mathlib's.

records.name: LennonPittel.lennon_pittel_conjecture
records.entry_name: The Lennon–Pittel conjecture on random stable matchings
records.doc: We prove the Lennon–Pittel conjecture for balanced stable marriage with independent, uniform strict preferences. Let S_n count the stable complete matchings between two sides of size n. For every positive nonincreasing sequence epsilon_n tending to zero, the probability that S_n is at least epsilon_n times its expectation tends to one. This gives a lower-tail estimate at the scale of Pittel's first-moment asymptotic. An accompanying working paper is in preparation.

records.name: CDRBicolour.cdr_conjecture
records.entry_name: The Colbourn–Dinitz–Rosa conjecture and the exact block-type spectrum
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of two results on strictly 3-bicolored Steiner triple systems. For every positive triple of class sizes a,b,c, existence is equivalent to n=a+b+c being 1 or 3 modulo 6, the identity a²+b²+c²-ab-ac-bc=n, and the exclusion of two classes of size 2. For every sufficiently large admissible profile, the number of AAC blocks is characterized exactly by two explicit arithmetic tests. The first result settles the class-size conjecture posed by Colbourn, Dinitz and Rosa in 1999; the second applies the typed absorption theorems of Triangle decompositions III. Both statements are compared in one shared development.

records.name: DukeSchulzePillot.card_divisors_le_rpow
records.entry_name: Duke–Schulze-Pillot: the upper bound of Lemma 5(ii) and a conditional Theorem 3(ii)
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization around W. Duke and R. Schulze-Pillot, Representation of integers by positive ternary quadratic forms and equidistribution of lattice points on ellipsoids (Invent. Math. 99, 1990). q(x) = ½ xᵗAx for a symmetric integer 3 × 3 matrix A with q > 0 on ℚ³ \ {0}, h ∈ ℚ³, r(q, h, n) = #{x ∈ h + ℤ³ : q(x) = n} and, for F ⊆ ℝ³, r(q, F, h, n) = #{x ∈ h + ℤ³ : q(x) = n, x/√n ∈ F}. Unconditional results: card_divisors_le_rpow (d(n) ≤ C_ε n^ε); repCount_le (r(q, h, n) ≤ C_ε n^{1/2+ε} for n ≥ 1); average_le (the same bound for every nonnegatively weighted average of such counts, which includes r(spn_N q, h, n): this is the upper half of Lemma 5(ii)). Conditional results: thm3_ii (Theorem 3(ii), r(q, F, h, n) = R(n) μ(F) + O(n^{1/2 − 1/175 + ε}) for n ≥ 1 in a set S) and spn_upper (R(n) ≤ C_ε n^{1/2+ε}) are proved under two hypotheses that are NOT proved here: hThm1, the estimate of Theorem 1 of the paper (|r(q, F, h, n) − r(q, h, n) μ(F)| ≤ C (n^{−1/175} r(q, h, n) + n^{1/2−1/175+ε}) on S), and hThm3i, the estimate of Theorem 3(i) (|r(q, h, n) − R(n)| ≤ C n^{1/2−1/28+ε} on S); R stands for r(spn_N q, h, n), μF ∈ [0, 1] for μ(F), and S for the restricted set of n. The lower bound n^{1/2−ε} ≪ r(spn_N q, h, n) of Lemma 5(ii) (Siegel's ineffective bound) is not formalized.

records.name: ThomassenManyColourings.two_rpow_card_div_nine_le_ncard_listColourings
records.entry_name: Thomassen: exponentially many 5-list-colourings of planar graphs
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of C. Thomassen, Exponentially many 5-list-colorings of planar graphs (J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 97, 2007): a finite planar graph with n vertices, every vertex of which has a list of at least five colours, has at least 2^{n/9} distinct list colourings (two_rpow_card_div_nine_le_ncard_listColourings: (2 : ℝ) ^ (n / 9) ≤ the number of maps f : V → C with f v ∈ L v and f u ≠ f v on every edge). Planarity is combinatorial: a plane map is a rotation system whose hypermap with the dart reversal has Euler defect 0 (definitions copied verbatim from the registered entry thomassen-girth-five, PALOMAR-2026-10-28-000023, so that the Challenge depends on Mathlib only). The proof follows the paper: Theorems 1–4, Claims 8–13 and the lemmas on generalized wheels they use are proved for an abstract interface of near-triangulations, which is realised by plane near-triangulations using the separation theorems of the dependency; every planar graph is a spanning subgraph of a plane near-triangulation. One statement; the definitions of the Challenge are compared with those of the Solution.

records.name: CriticalTrees.Universal.critical_height_width
records.entry_name: Critical trees are neither too short nor too fat
records.doc: Lean 4 proofs of the main results of Addario-Berry, Donderwinkel and Kortchemski, "Critical trees are neither too short nor too fat" (arXiv:2311.06163). For every critical offspring law, the height of the size-conditioned Bienaymé tree divided by log n tends to infinity and its width divided by n tends to zero in probability, along admissible sizes. These bounds are sharp: for every function f tending to infinity, a single critical offspring law has limsup P(height < f(n) log n) = 1 and limsup P(width > n/f(n)) = 1. For critical offspring laws in the local domain of attraction of the asymmetric Cauchy law (mu_n = L(n)/n^2 with L slowly varying), the height divided by an explicit scale h_n and the width divided by n E[Y 1{Y >= a_n}] both converge to 1 in probability, and height times width is O_P(n log n). The entry also includes the stochastic ordering of heights of uniform labelled trees with given degree sequences (Addario-Berry and Donderwinkel, Theorem 9), used in the paper. All 23 named results of the paper (its theorem, proposition, lemma and corollary environments) are proved in the repository; this Palomar entry compares the headline results.

records.name: GaussLegendre.sum_three_sq_iff
records.entry_name: The three squares theorem (Gauss–Legendre)
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of the three squares theorem of Legendre (1798) and Gauss (1801): a natural number is a sum of three squares if and only if it is not of the form 4^a (8 b + 7) (sum_three_sq_iff), with the corollary that every n ≡ 3 (mod 8) is x₀² + x₁² + x₂² for some x : Fin 3 → ℤ (exists_sum_sq_of_mod_eight_eq_three). The proof uses ternary quadratic forms of determinant one: a positive definite integral ternary form of determinant one is equivalent to x² + y² + z² (proved with Minkowski's convex body theorem), and for n ≢ 0 (mod 4), n ≢ 7 (mod 8) such a form with diagonal entry n is built from a prime in an arithmetic progression (Dirichlet's theorem, as in Mathlib) and quadratic reciprocity for the Jacobi symbol. Two statements; no definitions beyond Mathlib's.

records.name: Chapter10.Sequence.palomar_literal_iff_decoded
records.entry_name: Finite sequence routing formulations and continuous timing
records.doc: A qualified finite sequence-routing formalization connecting the complete source binary rows with padded elementary customer routes and exact transition cost. For fixed valid slots, explicit zero-depot clock/travel conditions give continuous timing feasibility through the earliest-schedule recurrence and an attained minimum total return over timing assignments. Capacity and global route optimization are outside scope.

For fixed valid slots, explicit zero-depot clock/travel conditions give continuous timing feasibility through the earliest-schedule recurrence and an attained minimum total return over timing assignments. Capacity and global route optimization are outside scope.

records.name: BanachMazurRotation.banach_mazur_rotation_problem.finite_dimensional
records.entry_name: The Banach-Mazur rotation problem in finite dimensions: a transitive isometry group forces a Euclidean norm
records.doc: A machine-checked proof that a finite-dimensional real normed space whose linear isometries act transitively on the unit sphere is Euclidean. This is the finite-dimensional case of the Mazur rotations problem, which appeared in Banach's 1932 book and is surveyed by Cabello Sanchez, Ferenczi and Randrianantoanina; its audience is the geometry of Banach spaces and their symmetries. It is the statement banach_mazur_rotation_problem.finite_dimensional of Formal Conjectures (BanachMazurRotation.lean), which marks it research solved. The result is classical and no priority is claimed. The proof takes the classical route: the isometries form a compact group, averaging a squared Euclidean norm over Haar measure gives an invariant quadratic form, and transitivity makes it a multiple of the squared norm. Mathlib has no topology on the isometry group, so the entry also builds it as a compact topological group with Haar measure. The general problem for separable Banach spaces, which Formal Conjectures marks research open, is not addressed.

records.name: PeriodicDifference.Problem11.problem11_iff
records.entry_name: Classification of globally periodic rational difference equations
records.doc: A complete classification of the globally periodic rational difference equations x_{n+K} = (A_0 + A_1 x_n + ... + A_K x_{n+K-1}) / (B_0 + B_1 x_n + ... + B_K x_{n+K-1}) with nonnegative coefficients, acting on positive initial data, answering Problem 11 of Gasull's survey of open problems in low-dimensional dynamical systems. Such an equation is globally periodic (every positive solution satisfies x_{n+p} = x_n for a common p >= 1) if and only if, up to rescaling x_n -> alpha x_n and unfolding (multiplying every index by an integer), it is one of the five known examples: x_{n+1} = x_n, x_{n+1} = 1/x_n, x_{n+2} = x_{n+1}/x_n, the Lyness equation x_{n+2} = (1 + x_{n+1})/x_n, and Todd's period-8 equation x_{n+3} = (1 + x_{n+1} + x_{n+2})/x_n. The result holds at every order K. Previously the question had been settled for K in {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11} (Cima, Gasull and Mañosas 2004) and for some special families, but the general case was open.

records.name: HeptagonRamsey.Heptagon.heptagon_counterexample
records.entry_name: Pálvölgyi's cyclic heptagon is not Euclidean Ramsey, so Graham's spherical-set conjecture (formal-conjectures erdos_174.variants.graham) is false; and generic seven points on a circle are not Ramsey (Theorem A.3 of arXiv:2609.23327)
records.doc: For every transcendental r > 2, the seven points (0, 0) and (j, ±√(j(2r − j))), j ∈ {1, 3, 4}, lie on the circle of centre (r, 0) and radius r and are not Euclidean Ramsey (Pálvölgyi, A cyclic non-Ramsey heptagon, arXiv:2609.23327, Theorem 1); consequently not every finite cospherical subset of a Euclidean space is Ramsey. The second statement is the negation of the conjecture that every finite spherical set is Ramsey (posed by Erdős, Graham, Montgomery, Rothschild, Spencer and Straus in 1973), in exactly the form in which google-deepmind/formal-conjectures states it as erdos_174.variants.graham (formal-conjectures PR #7706, which re-tags that statement as solved and links this proof). Ramsey is formal-conjectures' definition, Erdos174.IsRamsey, copied byte for byte: a finite set A in R^n such that for every number k ≥ 1 of colours there is a dimension d for which every k-colouring of R^d has a monochromatic distance-preserving copy of A. All four compared statements use only Mathlib and that definition. The conjecture was refuted in September 2026 by Pálvölgyi's paper (whose proofs it attributes to ChatGPT) and by OpenAI's classification of finite Euclidean Ramsey configurations, whose Lean proof (openai/math) already exhibits non-Ramsey twelve- and nine-point sets on a circle in OpenAI's own vocabulary. The proof here is Pálvölgyi's derivation-energy argument run against OpenAI's tensor criterion: a derivation D of R with D r = 1, the pairing x ⊗ y ↦ D x · D y on OpenAI's coefficient tensor ring, the weights 2, −2, −2, 2, 2, −1, −1 and the energy −24/((2r − 1)(2r − 3)(2r − 4)) ≠ 0 show that the heptagon fails OpenAI's field criterion, and the necessity half of OpenAI's classification (proved in their Lean) turns that into not Ramsey; formal-conjectures' IsRamsey, which also allows the dimension d = 0, is then reduced to OpenAI's Ramsey. The witness for the second statement is the heptagon at r = 2 + OpenAI's Liouville-type parameter, which is transcendental. Also proved, with the same definition: Theorem A.3 of the paper's appendix as printed, without its measure clause (for distinct t1, t2, t3 and t4, ..., t7 algebraically independent over Q(t1, t2, t3), the seven points ((1 − ti²)/(1 + ti²), 2ti/(1 + ti²)) are not Ramsey; the appendix is labelled by its author as written by ChatGPT and unchecked), and its corollary for seven parameters algebraically independent over Q, in the shape of OpenAI's nine-point theorem (distinct points on the unit circle, not Ramsey). Its proof follows the appendix: Lemma A.1 in its symmetric form, a derivation vanishing on Q(t1, t2, t3) with prescribed values on t4, ..., t7, weighted moments by Lagrange interpolation, and again the necessity half of OpenAI's classification. The 16 OpenAI Lean files the proofs import are included, ported to the Lean module system by header-only changes. All proofs depend on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only.

records.name: FourSquaresInCaps.jacobi_four_squares_odd
records.entry_name: Four squares in caps, and Jacobi's four-square theorem for odd N
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of two results on sums of four squares. (1) Jacobi's four-square theorem for odd N: the number of x : Fin 4 → ℤ with x₀² + x₁² + x₂² + x₃² = N equals 8 ∑_{d ∣ N} d (jacobi_four_squares_odd), following the proof of Andrews, Ekhad and Zeilberger (1993): two finite q-series identities proved by WZ telescoping, combined into a finite identity that is read modulo X^{N+1} in ℚ⟦X⟧. (2) Four squares in caps (four_squares_in_caps): for every unit vector q ∈ ℝ⁴ and every δ > 0 there is M₀ such that every odd m ≥ M₀ is β₀² + β₁² + β₂² + β₃² with β : Fin 4 → ℤ and |βᵢ − √m qᵢ| ≤ δ √m for all i, i.e. the integer points of the sphere of radius √m meet every cap of fixed angular radius. The proof uses the Duke–Friedlander–Iwaniec delta method (in Heath-Brown's form) with Gaussian weights: an exact formula through the theta transformation, Fourier bounds for the cut-off weight, and the Weil bound for Kloosterman sums, imported from the Weil Bounds Toolkit (PALOMAR-2026-11-03-000018) as a lake dependency. The main term is not evaluated: it depends on the center of the cap only through its norm, so comparing caps with a grid of centers reduces the theorem to the lower bound r₄(m) ≥ 8m for odd m, which (1) provides. All constants are effective but not explicit in the statement (M₀ is existential). Two statements; no definitions beyond Mathlib's.

records.name: Paper.principalTheorem
records.entry_name: Central limit theorem for the complex eigenvalues of Gaussian random matrices
records.doc: This project formalizes the main central limit theorem of “Central limit theorem for the complex eigenvalues of Gaussian random matrices” by Advay Goel, Patrick Lopatto, and Xiaoyu Xie (arXiv:2306.10243v2), using an expanded local manuscript as the detailed proof source. The local manuscript was prepared to ease autoformalization by adding details to the proofs. Its main theorem (Theorem 1.3) is identical to the main theorem of the arXiv version: the hypotheses and conclusion are unchanged. Only this main theorem is advertised.

records.name: OverfullCriteria.class_two_iff_overfull_subgraph
records.entry_name: Overfull criteria for edge colouring (Plantholt; Chen–Cao; Cao–Chen–Jing–Shan), unified
records.doc: A thin wrapper that restates, in one vocabulary and with Mathlib definitions only, the overfull criteria proved in PALOMAR-2026-11-04-000016 and PALOMAR-2026-11-04-000009. class_two_iff_overfull_subgraph: a finite simple graph of even order n with 12 n ≤ 7 (3δ − Δ) is of class two (its line graph is not Δ-colourable) iff it has a Δ-overfull subgraph (odd order at least 3, more than Δ (|V(H)| − 1)/2 edges); this is Plantholt's criterion with Chetwynd–Hilton's 6/7. critical_overfull: a Δ-critical graph (connected, class two, every edge-deleted subgraph Δ-colourable) with 2n + 5δ ≤ 3Δ + 6 (Chen–Cao), or 3n + 7δ ≤ 4Δ + 10 (Cao–Chen–Jing–Shan, variant), or 3n + 7δ ≤ 4Δ + 17 and n + δ ≥ 27 (Cao–Chen–Jing–Shan) has odd order, is overfull (|E| > Δ ⌊n/2⌋), and so is a Δ-overfull subgraph of itself. The only new proof is the elementary step from overfullness to odd order at least 3 (degree sum) and the conversion to the subgraph form. Two statements; no definitions beyond Mathlib's.

records.name: MirekThiele.theorem_1_3
records.entry_name: A local T(b) theorem for perfect multilinear Calderón–Zygmund operators (Mirek–Thiele), formalized in Lean 4
records.doc: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the three main theorems of M. Mirek and C. Thiele, "A local T(b) theorem for perfect multilinear Calderón–Zygmund operators", Proc. London Math. Soc. 114 (2017): the perfect multilinear local T(1) theorem (Theorem 1.3), the perfect multilinear local T(b) theorem with general testing functions on admissible collections of paths (Theorem 1.4), and the perfect multilinear global T(b) theorem (Theorem 1.11), for n-linear forms on dyadic test functions in R^d satisfying the dyadic decay, perfect smoothness and qualitative truncation conditions. The development follows the paper's proof of Theorem 1.4 (stopping times, pruning, the telescoping identities, the discrete Carleson embedding and the outer-measure Hölder inequalities of Do–Thiele, the contraction step and its iteration) and the global/local reduction of Theorem 1.11, including the atom estimate for the dyadic Hardy norm for all exponents (Burkholder's L^p bound for the dyadic square function by Marcinkiewicz interpolation). Theorem 1.3, cited as folklore in the paper, is proved by a dyadic paraproduct argument with a dyadic John–Nirenberg inequality for the paraproduct symbols. All constants depend only on the dimension, the linearity, the testing constant and the exponents.

records.name: Chapter10.palomar_source_route_penalty_proposition
records.entry_name: Finite integer penalties and literal routing QUBO transport
records.doc: A complete source-based finite penalty/energy family: the generic full ordered QUBO identity and strict integer-row minimizer equivalence, consistent fixed-coordinate energy/minimizer transport, and the literal incidence, time-indexed arc and sequence applications. records.name: WaleckiDecomposition.hamiltonian_cycles_odd
records.entry_name: Walecki's decompositions of complete graphs into Hamiltonian cycles and paths
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of Walecki's theorem: for every m, the complete graph on 2m + 1 vertices is the edge-disjoint union of m Hamiltonian cycles (hamiltonian_cycles_odd), and the complete graph on 2m vertices is the edge-disjoint union of m Hamiltonian paths (hamiltonian_paths_even). Both are stated for an arbitrary finite vertex type of the given cardinality, with Mathlib's Walk.IsHamiltonianCycle and Walk.IsHamiltonian, pairwise disjoint edge lists, and every edge of the complete graph on some cycle (path). The proof is Walecki's zig-zag construction: on ZMod (2m) the paths i, i+1, i−1, i+2, i−2, …, i+m (0 ≤ i < m) are Hamiltonian; an edge {x, y} of the i-th path has x + y ∈ {2i, 2i+1}, which makes the paths edge-disjoint, and m (2m − 1) = C(2m, 2) shows that they cover all edges; closing each path through a new vertex gives the cycles. Two statements; no definitions beyond Mathlib's.

records.name: Fournier.fournier
records.entry_name: Fournier's theorem: graphs whose maximum-degree vertices induce a forest are of class one
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of Fournier's theorem (1973): if the vertices of maximum degree of a finite simple graph G induce a forest, then G has a proper edge colouring with Δ(G) colours (fournier: G.lineGraph.Colorable G.maxDegree under (G.induce {v | G.degree v = G.maxDegree}).IsAcyclic). The proof takes an edge-minimal subgraph H of G that is not Δ(G)-edge-colourable; Vizing's theorem gives Δ(H) = Δ(G), and Vizing's adjacency lemma applied to every edge xy of H gives a neighbour of x of maximum degree other than y, so the maximum-degree vertices of H span a subgraph of minimum degree at least 2 inside the forest, which is impossible (the end of a longest path). Vizing's theorem and the adjacency lemma are imported as lake dependencies from PALOMAR-2026-10-15-000004 and PALOMAR-2026-11-04-000009. One statement; no definitions beyond Mathlib's.

records.name: Couret.Palomar.classification
records.entry_name: Three-point ordered convolution-square classification
records.doc: For three-element finite supports S and T in any abelian group, equality of all labelled coefficients of their ordered additive convolution squares is equivalent to a translation by an element annihilated by doubling, or to the explicit exceptional paired shape in the statement. Diagonal pairs are included. The full proof development is contained in this snapshot. This is an adaptation of an existing public Couret formalization; mathematical novelty and independent human review are not established.

records.name: ErdosUlamProblem.erdos_ulam_problem.variants.anning_erdos
records.entry_name: The Anning-Erdős theorem: an infinite set of points in the plane with integer distances lies on a line
records.doc: A machine-checked proof that an infinite set of points in the Euclidean plane whose pairwise distances are all integers is contained in a line (Anning and Erdős, 1945). Formal Conjectures states it next to the Erdős-Ulam problem on dense rational-distance sets, which is open; its audience is distance problems in discrete geometry. It is the statement erdos_ulam_problem.variants.anning_erdos of Formal Conjectures (ErdosUlamProblem.lean), which marks it research solved. The result is classical and no priority is claimed. The proof follows Erdős's short argument: for three points A, B, C not on a line, the differences |PA| - |PB| and |PA| - |PC| take finitely many values, and in place of the bound on how often two hyperbolas meet, each pair of values is shown to allow only finitely many points P, as the roots of a quadratic in |PA|.

records.name: KSPalomar.Intrinsic.Full.exists_intrinsic_index_nullity_m2
records.entry_name: KarcherIndex
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the Morse index and nullity of Karcher saddle towers, formalizing results from arXiv:2608.13451v2. For the Enneper-Weierstrass realizations, the two-period quotient Xi_{k,2} has index 4k-3 and bounded Jacobi-field nullity 3 for every k >= 3. For the six-ended family Xi_{3,m}, every positive integer m has index 6m-4 floor(m alpha*)-3 and nullity 7 when m alpha* is an integer, and 3 otherwise. The same threshold alpha* lies in (1/3,1/2), with certified strict bounds 0.4323617 < alpha* < 0.4323619. As in the paper, index and nullity are defined using complex-valued functions, with dimensions taken over the complex numbers. The development constructs realizations from the explicit data and supplies the geometric-to-analytic identifications, rather than assuming the existence of a realization. Supporting results include proper embeddedness and the equivalence of boundedness and finite Dirichlet energy for smooth geometric Jacobi fields on the finite period quotients.

records.name: ArtGallery.agpOrthBoundaryPoint_erComplete
records.entry_name: The orthogonal boundary-point art gallery problem is ∃ℝ-complete, in Lean 4
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of material in a forthcoming manuscript entitled "The Orthogonal Art Gallery Problem is ∃ℝ-complete". A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof, for an explicit single-tape Turing machine model, that deciding whether an orthogonal simple polygon (every edge horizontal or vertical) with rational corners can be guarded by g points of its boundary, which together must see the whole closed polygon (the boundary-point variant), is ∃ℝ-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions. The orthogonal point-point and point-boundary variants are the subject of the author's earlier entry PALOMAR-2026-11-01-000004 v1, whose definitions this entry reuses unchanged. For general polygons the boundary-point variant is treated by Abrahamsen, Adamaszek and Miltzow (J. ACM 2021); orthogonal polygons are not. The hardness proof is a new construction: the ETR-INV instance is compiled to rows of fourteen relation profiles, and the polygon is a hub with one floor slot per variable and one door per row, behind each of which hangs an orthogonal wing (a staircase corridor ending in an arithmetic room) whose boundary guards copy the slot values through the door and enforce the row relation. Its finite visibility facts are kernel-checked certificates on the wing charts, parametric in the size and value parameters. The proofs use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.name: Couret.PalomarCardinality.fibre_cardinality
records.entry_name: Cardinalities of three-point ordered convolution-square fibres
records.doc: In any finite abelian group G, fix a three-element support S and retain the entire labelled ordered additive convolution square, including diagonal pairs. The number of three-element supports with the same square is h or 2h, where h is the number of elements u satisfying u+u=0; in particular it is at most 2h. The full proof is included. This adapts a prior public Couret formalization; novelty and independent human review are not established.

records.name: TensorPCA.Paper.discontinuousTransition
records.entry_name: Statistical thresholds for Tensor PCA
records.doc: We formalize in Lean the principal statistical and constrained-landscape results of Statistical thresholds for Tensor PCA by Jagannath, Lopatto and Miolane, following a local expanded manuscript prepared solely by Patrick Lopatto, the formalization’s maintainer. This elaborated manuscript was prepared to facilitate autoformalization. At nonnegative signal strength in the ordered Gaussian tensor model, we prove the detection threshold below and above criticality for even orders k ≥ 6. For k ≥ 3, we prove the maximum-likelihood value limit at every nonnegative signal strength and the maximum-likelihood absolute-overlap limit away from criticality. We prove optimality bounds for independently randomized measurable unit estimators at nonnegative noncritical strengths, and tensor MMSE formulas at positive noncritical strengths. We also prove the discontinuous overlap transition, consistent testing among fixed nonempty finite families of distinct supercritical strengths, constrained expected and almost-sure energy limits for signed overlaps in [-1,1], and associated variational and landscape conclusions. Almost-sure limits concern fixed parameters and allow arbitrary coupling across dimensions. For interior overlaps, the four-parameter variational reduction establishes equality of infima; unrestricted minimizer attainment is not claimed.

records.name: ConditionalLogRank.stability_probability_pos
records.entry_name: Conditional logarithmic partner ranks in exponential matching markets
records.doc: Switching costs relax pairwise stability by requiring both members of a blocking pair to gain more than a common nonnegative cost. In balanced markets with n firms and n workers and independent rate-one exponential utilities, this package proves a conditional benchmark for ordinal partner ranks in Lean. Fix a matching and condition the market on its stability. If twice the cost divided by log n tends to rho in [0,1), the conditional probability that average one-based firm partner rank is at most n^t tends to (t-rho)/(1-rho) for every rho<t<1; rank 1 is best. Equivalently, the logarithm of average firm rank divided by log n converges in distribution to the uniform law on [rho,1]. Bounded or vanishing costs give rho=0, with persistent dispersion across polynomial rank scales under this conditioning. The theorem removes the original conjecture's supercritical lower bound. The proof also includes positive conditioning probability, exact integral identities, score limits, and rank-transfer estimates. This fixed-matching conditioning does not determine ranks under a uniform stable lottery in an ordinary random market, or dispersion of stable outcomes within a typical realized market. An accompanying working paper presenting these results and their economic interpretation is in preparation. A link will be added here when it is publicly available.

records.name: ReinhardtChallenge.octagon_density
records.entry_name: The Reinhardt conjecture, formalized in Lean 4
records.doc:
The Reinhardt problem asks for the centrally symmetric convex disk in the plane whose densest packing by congruent copies is least dense. Karl Reinhardt (1934) and, independently, Kurt Mahler (1947) found the smoothed octagon, a regular octagon whose corners are cut off by arcs of hyperbolas, each asymptotic to the next two side lines, with greatest packing density delta_oct = (8 - 4 sqrt 2 - log 2)/(2 sqrt 2 - 1) = 0.902414..., and Reinhardt conjectured that no centrally symmetric convex disk packs worse. The conjecture has been open since 1934; Thomas Hales cast it as a problem of Bolza in the calculus of variations (2011) and then as an optimal control problem on SL2(R) (2017), and Hales and Koundinya Vajjha studied that problem in Packings of Smoothed Polygons (2024).

This entry proves the conjecture with its equality case. Every centrally symmetric convex disk has greatest packing density at least delta_oct, with equality if and only if the disk is the image of the smoothed octagon under an invertible affine map; and the smoothed octagon, in Reinhardt's description, is a centrally symmetric convex disk of greatest packing density delta_oct.

The proof follows Hales's control formulation. A worst disk is realized by a global minimizer of the control problem, which lifts to a Pontryagin extremal, stays in Hales and Vajjha's compact domain, switches finitely often and is normal. Its switch signs fall into five classes, each excluded for periods with at least six pieces by scalar estimates; periods with at most five pieces cost at least the octagon's area, with equality only for the octagon. The scalar estimates are inequalities, polynomial identities, monotonicity and convexity arguments; a few polynomial signs are checked by explicit Bernstein expansions, and no interval cover is used. The geometric and control-theoretic foundations, among them Fejes Toth's lattice theorem, Theorem 5.0.2 of Hales and Vajjha and the Pontryagin maximum principle, come from the pinned libraries lean4-smoothed-polygon and lean4-optimal-control.
